judgment: A planet in its joy house gains strength and acts more powerfully in matters pertaining to that house; it is also used as an explanatory principle for the character of those houses (e.g., the 6th is a place of affliction because Mars, a malefic, rejoices there).
notes: The arrangement reflects sect: diurnal planets are above the horizon, nocturnal below, Mercury on the horizon. Benefics and luminaries aspect the Ascendant from their joy houses; malefics do not.

rule: Among a planet's two domiciles (where applicable), the planet's preferred joy is in the domicile matching its own sect. Saturn rejoices in Aquarius (masculine), Jupiter in Sagittarius, Mars in Scorpio, the Sun in Leo, Venus in Taurus, Mercury in Virgo, and the Moon in Cancer.
judgment: The planet is especially strong and at ease in the domicile aligned with its sect.

rule: Diurnal planets rejoice when they are oriental (rising before the Sun in the morning); nocturnal planets rejoice when they are occidental (appearing after sunset in the evening).
conditions: planet's relationship to the Sun—oriental or occidental
judgment: A planet in the correct solar relationship for its sect gains a strengthening joy condition.

rule: The three superior masculine planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars) rejoice in the masculine quadrants of the chart: from the MC to the Ascendant and from the IC to the Descendant. The Moon and Venus rejoice in the feminine quadrants: from the Descendant to the MC and from the Ascendant to the IC. Mercury rejoices in whichever quadrant contains planets of the same gender as the planets he is with at the time.
conditions: gender of planets Mercury is configured with
judgment: Placement in the correct quadrant for a planet's gender is a joy condition adding strength.
notes: Mercury's amphoteric nature is explicitly noted: he takes on the gender of the planets in his company.

rule: The Moon functions as the primary significatrix for all matters in a chart. She carries and transmits the condition of any matter to whichever planet she applies to by body or ray. The planet receiving this transmitted condition is designated the receiver of disposition. The quality of the Moon's condition determines the overall soundness or weakness of the matter in question.
judgment: A well-conditioned Moon indicates the soundness of any matter; an impaired Moon indicates its detriment. The nature of the planet receiving her disposition shapes the outcome according to that planet's own character.
notes: Reception of disposition described as passing sequentially through the planetary spheres up to Saturn, beyond which no further receiver exists.

rule: Malefic planets produce harmful outcomes by default owing to an excess of heat or cold in their constitution. Their malice is reduced when a benefic planet occupies one of the malefic's dignities, causing the malefic to receive the benefic and withhold harm. A trine or sextile aspect from a malefic also mitigates its damage because these are harmonious aspect types. Benefic planets produce beneficial outcomes by default owing to their temperate constitution; they function beneficially whether or not reception is present, though reception enhances their positive effect.
judgment: Malefics harm unless receiving a benefic in their dignity or aspecting by trine or sextile; benefics assist regardless, with stronger effect under reception.

rule: A planet is considered impeded when a malefic projects its rays over that planet's degree within the malefic's orb. If the malefic has moved past the planet by a full degree, the malefic can only instill apprehension but cannot actively impede. If a malefic is cadent from the Ascendant, it likewise generates only fear without completing actual harm. Transiting a bound belonging to a malefic causes a planet to be regarded as 'looking at' the malefic, but the malefic cannot impede in that circumstance. The same degree-separation logic applies to benefics: a benefic separated from a planet by a full degree produces hope but does not perfect the matter; a cadent benefic similarly yields hope without completion.
judgment: Active impediment requires the malefic to be within orb and not yet separated by a full degree, and not cadent. Beyond one degree of separation or in a cadent house, only fear or hope results without actual effect.
notes: The 'full degree' threshold appears to mean the malefic has entered the next whole degree, not that a full 60-minute arc has elapsed.

rule: When a planet is located in a sign that is conjunct, square, or opposite to a malefic's sign, it is in a state of contention with that malefic and must struggle against the harm directed at it. Once the malefic has passed it by a full degree, the planet has cleared the impediment and the malefic can only frighten, not harm.
judgment: Planets within the four-fold angular relationship to a malefic are under threat; escape is confirmed when separation exceeds one full degree.
notes: Described as especially relevant to horary questions.

rule: When the Moon applies to no planet within the chart, the matter signified is considered empty, cancelled, or turned away from its goal.
conditions: no applying aspect or conjunction to any planet
judgment: The matter will not proceed; it will be annulled or reversed.

rule: The planet to which the Moon applies indicates what is forthcoming regarding the matter, calibrated by that planet's inherent nature.
conditions: benefic or malefic status of applying planet
judgment: Application to a benefic indicates good outcomes ahead; application to a malefic indicates harmful outcomes ahead.

rule: The planet from which the Moon is separating indicates what has already occurred or passed regarding the matter, calibrated by that planet's inherent nature.
judgment: The nature of the planet left behind describes the quality of past events.

rule: A planet occupying the sign of its own fall (descension) indicates sorrow, confinement, and distress.
conditions: planet in sign of its own fall
judgment: Signifies grief, imprisonment, or hardship.

rule: A retrograde planet indicates defiance, contradiction, reversal, and discord.
judgment: Matters under its signification turn back, contradict themselves, or produce conflict.

rule: A planet at its first station (about to turn retrograde) signifies stagnation, dissolution, and destructive slowness. A planet at its second station (about to turn direct) signifies renewal, forward movement, and recovery from delay or difficulty.
judgment: First station: dissolution and obstruction. Second station: renewal and advancement.
notes: Judgment 11 also notes that a stationary planet generically signifies evil and inactivity, which aligns with the first-station reading; the second-station reading is more positive.

rule: A planet moving more slowly than its mean daily motion delays the timing or fulfilment of what it promises. The same slowing effect applies when a planet occupies a domicile of Saturn or Jupiter. Conversely, a planet in a domicile belonging to the luminaries or fast-moving planets hastens the timing of events.
conditions: planet speed relative to mean motion
judgment: Slow motion or placement in Saturn/Jupiter domiciles: delayed manifestation. Placement in domiciles of faster planets: accelerated manifestation.

rule: Once the Moon completes an exact conjunction with a planet (within one arc-minute), the next planet she will apply to reveals further developments and the subsequent condition of the matter in question.
conditions: exact conjunction completed to one arc-minute
judgment: The nature and condition of the next planet the Moon applies to after the exact conjunction describes what follows.

rule: A planet in the very last degree of a sign has effectively already transferred its strength to the following sign, analogous to a person standing on a threshold who has effectively departed. However, a planet in the second-to-last degree (29th degree by 0-based counting, i.e. 28°00'–28°59') still retains its strength in the current sign. Every planet's effective zone of influence extends across three degrees: the degree it occupies, the degree immediately before it, and the degree immediately after it.
judgment: Final degree: strength is in the next sign. Second-to-last degree: strength remains in the current sign. Three-degree spread of influence applies in all cases.
notes: Related to allowance of out-of-sign conjunctions elsewhere in this tradition.

rule: When a planet seeks to complete a conjunction within a sign but cannot do so before its target planet moves into the next sign, the conjunction can still be perfected if the applying planet catches the target in the following sign before the target forms a new conjunction with a third body. If the target has already joined a third planet before the original applying planet catches it, the original conjunction is blocked and the matter fails. An aspect does not block another aspect, but a bodily conjunction overrides a prior aspect-based connection. A bodily conjunction can block an aspect, but an aspect cannot block another aspect—it can only obstruct the matter.
judgment: Conjunction perfected in next sign without intervening new conjunction: matter is completed. Intervening bodily conjunction of target with third planet before original applying planet arrives: matter fails. Aspect to aspect: matter impeded but not cut off. Body overrides aspect.
notes: Distinction drawn between three modes of frustration/translation: aspect-to-aspect only impedes; body-to-aspect overrides; aspect-to-body is not addressed as a fourth mode here.

rule: A malefic that is oriental (rising before the Sun in the morning), positioned in its own domicile or exaltation, and not afflicted by another malefic is of greater practical value than a benefic that is retrograde and impeded.
judgment: A dignified, oriental, unafflicted malefic outperforms a retrograde, impeded benefic.

rule: When malefics rule the significated matter, and the Ascendant ruler or Moon applies to them by square or opposition, the matter is brought about but ultimately ruined. If instead the malefic applies to and joins a benefic (i.e. the malefic is the pusher rather than receiver), the outcome is better than when the malefic receives the disposition.
judgment: Malefic receiving disposition via square or opposition from significators: matter made but then destroyed. Malefic pushing to benefic: better outcome.

rule: A malefic planet occupying the Ascendant while in its own domicile or exaltation has its harmful nature restrained. If that same malefic is retrograde in the Ascendant, its harmful effects are amplified and its disruptive variability increases.
judgment: Dignified malefic in Ascendant: harm curtailed. Retrograde malefic in Ascendant: harm intensified and multiplied.

rule: A planet placed in a sign whose fundamental elemental quality matches the planet's own nature produces harmony and mutual compatibility. A planet in a sign contrary to its nature produces discord and weakness, as incompatible elements resist blending.
judgment: Matching natures: harmonious, productive placement. Opposing natures: detrimental, unproductive placement.
notes: Saturn cited with cold signs, Mars with hot signs as examples.

rule: When a benefic planet casts an aspect to a malefic, the malefic's capacity to harm is diminished.
judgment: Malefic's impediment is reduced.

rule: When a malefic aspects a benefic by square or opposition, the benefic's capacity to produce good fortune is diminished.
judgment: Benefic's fortune is reduced.

rule: A benefic that is cadent from the Ascendant (not in aspect to the rising sign) or retrograde loses its beneficial character and functions like a malefic.
judgment: Benefic becomes impeded and harmful rather than helpful.

rule: When planets are received (i.e. occupying a dignity of the planet they apply to), benefics express their positive qualities more strongly, and malefics express their negative qualities less forcefully.
judgment: Reception enhances benefic good; reception mitigates malefic harm.

rule: A malefic occupying a sign in which it holds no dignity whatsoever (not domicile, exaltation, or triplicity) has its harmful nature intensified. When a malefic occupies a sign in which it does hold some dignity, its malice is restrained and impediment effectively eliminated.
conditions: presence or absence of dignity in sign
judgment: Peregrine malefic: increased harm. Malefic with any dignity in sign: harm neutralized.

rule: When a malefic occupies its own domicile, exaltation, triplicity, or bounds, and is placed in an angular or succeedent house, and rules the matter in question, its strength is equivalent to that of a benefic.
conditions: own domicile or exaltation or triplicity or bounds
judgment: Malefic under these conditions functions with benefic-level strength.

rule: A benefic in a sign where it holds no dignity has its fortunate effects diminished. A benefic in a sign where it holds any form of dignity has its fortunate effects maximized and matters reach completion.
conditions: presence or absence of any dignity
judgment: Peregrine benefic: reduced good. Dignified benefic: increased good and perfected matters.

rule: Any planet—whether benefic or malefic—that is combust, under the Sun's rays, or in opposition to the Sun is weakened and unable to express its full nature. A combust benefic can produce only minimal good; a combust malefic can produce only minimal harm.
conditions: planet under rays within 12 degrees of Sun
judgment: Both types of planets are diminished: benefics produce little benefit, malefics produce little harm.

rule: Any planet, regardless of its natural malice, that occupies its own domicile, exaltation, or triplicity has whatever negative potential it carries redirected toward good.
conditions: domicile or exaltation or triplicity placement
judgment: Negative signification is converted into positive.

rule: When a malefic is angular and aspects a planet by square or opposition, its capacity to harm is at its greatest, especially if the malefic holds more dignity or occupies a stronger house than its target. Trine or sextile aspects from a malefic, even from an angle, reduce the harm it causes.
judgment: Angular malefic with square or opposition: maximum harm, especially if stronger than target. Angular malefic with trine or sextile: reduced harm.

rule: Evaluating a planet requires examining both its house position from the Ascendant and the sign it occupies. Even a naturally malefic planet can produce good when it is in a sign of matching elemental nature, in a sign where it has dignity, or in a house of good signification.
judgment: A malefic in favorable house and matching or dignified sign can signify good.

rule: A benefic that belongs to the nocturnal sect operating in a diurnal chart (or vice versa), or one that is peregrine, cadent, or combust, loses its capacity to benefit and becomes obstructive.
conditions: sect mismatch between planet and chart
judgment: Benefic under any of these conditions impedes rather than assists.
notes: 'Being in its own light' is defined as belonging to the sect of the luminary ruling the chart, not a synonym for any other dignity.

rule: Jupiter, by aspecting or joining Saturn, breaks Saturn's malice and transforms it toward good. Venus alone cannot neutralize Saturn's evil; Jupiter's involvement is required. Venus, by her own action, neutralizes Mars's malice. The principle is that each greater benefic resolves the corresponding greater or lesser malefic.
judgment: Jupiter counters Saturn; Venus counters Mars; Venus alone cannot counter Saturn without Jupiter's assistance.

rule: When a malefic pushes disposition to another malefic, one form of harm is exchanged for another. When a malefic pushes to a benefic, harm is converted into good. When a benefic pushes to a malefic, the matter begins well but ends in harm.
conditions: malefic or benefic status of each
judgment: Malefic to malefic: harm shifts form. Malefic to benefic: harm becomes good. Benefic to malefic: good followed by harm.

rule: When the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant is afflicted by a malefic via conjunction, square, or opposition, and a benefic then applies to the Moon or Ascendant ruler by square, the person is freed from the threatened harm. If a benefic applies by trine or sextile under the same circumstances, the person may partially escape the harm but may encounter a second related harm, or escape only with difficulty.
conditions: malefic conjunction or square or opposition
benefic by square vs. trine or sextile
judgment: Benefic square to afflicted significator: full rescue. Benefic trine or sextile: partial rescue or escape with secondary harm.
notes: The stronger protective effect of the square over the trine/sextile in rescue scenarios appears to relate to the benefic being in opposition to the afflicting malefic when it squares the Moon or Ascendant ruler, directly countering the malefic.

rule: A planet that holds no dignity of any kind in its sign (not domicile, exaltation, triplicity, bounds, or joy) and is additionally cadent from the Ascendant represents the worst possible condition: its signification is entirely without usefulness.
conditions: absence of all five dignities in sign
judgment: Complete absence of utility or benefit from the planet's signification.

rule: A planet that is occidental (in a later degree than the Sun, setting after the Sun, or rising in the evening in the west) has diminished strength and light. If such a planet is also malefic, its harmful effects are further reduced. If it is retrograde and occidental, it operates sluggishly in all matters.
judgment: Occidental placement weakens the planet; occidental malefic harms less; occidental retrograde planet is slow in all significations.

rule: A planet is weakened in all matters when it is within 12 degrees of the Sun (either side). Exception: a planet in the exact same degree as the Sun (cazimi) is instead strengthened.
conditions: planet in same degree as Sun
judgment: Within 12 degrees but not cazimi: planet is weak. Cazimi: planet is strong.

rule: A planet that has cleared 12 degrees from the Sun in the morning (oriental, rising before the Sun) is strong. Peak strength occurs at 15 degrees of oriental separation. A planet moving toward the Sun from the western side (about to set in the evening) begins to weaken when it comes within 15 degrees and reaches maximum weakness approaching the Sun's exact degree. Cazimi (exact solar conjunction by degree) restores full strength.
judgment: 12° oriental: strong. 15° oriental: maximum strength. Moving from 15° to 7° occidental: weakening. Under 7° to cazimi: weakest, then strongest at exact degree conjunction.

rule: A planet with no dignity in its sign becomes crafty or unreliable in nature. However, if such a planet is direct in motion and occupies an angular house or the 11th house, it can still produce good results.
judgment: Peregrine by dignity: unreliable signification. Peregrine but direct and well-placed by house: good outcome possible.

rule: The planet receiving the Moon's disposition is weakened and unable to complete its judgment if it is within 12 degrees in front of the Sun (occidental, heading toward combustion). If the receiver is oriental (ahead of the Sun in the zodiac, having emerged from combustion), it is strong and capable of executing its judgment effectively.
judgment: Occidental receiver within 12 degrees: weak, matter not completed. Oriental receiver: strong, matter judged skillfully.
notes: Metaphor of a collapsed and rebuilt structure is used to describe the re-emergence from combustion to strength.

rule: A benefic placed in the 8th house from the Ascendant neither produces good nor causes harm. A malefic in the 8th house has its harmful nature increased.
judgment: 8th house benefic: neutral, no benefit or harm. 8th house malefic: amplified harm.

rule: A planet newly entered into a sign is weak until it has traversed 6 degrees within that sign. Separately, a planet must be within 5 degrees after an angular cusp to be considered truly angular; a planet in fewer than 5 degrees before the cusp (by primary motion) is cadent, not angular.
conditions: planet in first degrees of sign
judgment: First 6 degrees of sign: planet is unsettled and weak. Within 5 degrees before cusp: cadent. 5 degrees or more past cusp up to 15 degrees: angular.
notes: The 5-degree cadency rule is associated with Ptolemaic longevity technique. The 6-degree entry threshold may derive from the average size of a bound.

rule: A planet located within 15 degrees after an angular cusp is treated as if it were in the angle. A planet beyond 15 degrees after the cusp loses angular strength. An alternative reading attributes to Ptolemy an extension of this zone to 25 degrees past the cusp.
conditions: planet position relative to angular cusp
judgment: Within 15 degrees after angle: planet is angular. Beyond 15 degrees: not angular. Ptolemaic variant: up to 25 degrees.
notes: The text presents both 15 and 25 degrees as competing thresholds, the latter attributed to Ptolemy.

rule: Planets or significators in fixed signs indicate stable, enduring, and firm outcomes. Those in mutable (common) signs indicate loosening of matters, repetition, or attachment of secondary matters. Those in cardinal (movable) signs indicate rapid change or swift transformation of the matter.
judgment: Fixed: stability and permanence. Mutable: repetition and inconclusiveness. Cardinal: speed of change.

rule: When the Moon is afflicted on a given day, all matters initiated or asked about on that day are likewise afflicted—unless the afflicting malefic is cadent from the Ascendant and weak, and the Moon holds no dignity in the Ascendant. Under those limited conditions, the malefic produces only fear and concern rather than direct bodily harm. If the afflicting malefic is angular or succeedent, it imposes actual physical harm.
conditions: Moon without dignity in Ascendant degree
judgment: Moon afflicted + malefic strong: all matters of the day harmed. Moon afflicted + malefic cadent and weak + Moon undignified in Ascendant: fear only, not harm. Malefic in angle or succeedent: actual physical harm results.

rule: When the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is positioned in the sign directly opposite its own domicile (the seventh sign from its rulership), the person asking the question will experience dread or apprehension concerning the matter, and the situation will be burdensome for them.
judgment: Querent fears the matter; the situation bears heavily upon them.

rule: In a question about stolen goods, the Ascendant and its lord plus the Moon signify the owner-querent; the 7th house and its lord signify the thief; the Midheaven signifies the stolen property itself; the 4th house (angle of the earth) signifies the location of the stolen goods.
judgment: These four chart factors serve as the primary significators in theft questions, each assigned to a specific party or object in the matter.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant applies to conjoin the lord of the 7th, or the lord of the Ascendant is located in the 7th, the querent will apprehend the thief through active investigation.
conditions: lord of Ascendant applies to lord of 7th
judgment: The owner-querent captures or locates the thief.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is joined to the lord of the 7th (indicating apprehension of the thief), but the lord of the 2nd house is simultaneously under the sun's beams, the querent finds the thief but does not recover the stolen property.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to lord of 7th
AND lord of 2nd under the rays
judgment: Thief is caught but stolen goods are not recovered.
notes: The 2nd house is explicitly identified as the house of the querent's substance.

rule: When the lord of the 7th applies to the lord of the Ascendant, or the lord of the 7th is located in the Ascendant, the thief voluntarily returns the stolen items.
conditions: lord of 7th applies to lord of Ascendant
judgment: Thief returns what was stolen.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is joined to the lord of the Ascendant but the lord of the 2nd is under the rays, the thief is found but the stolen goods are not. If the lord of the 2nd has just emerged from combustion, part of the stolen goods will be recovered.
conditions: lord of 7th joined to lord of Ascendant
AND lord of 2nd under the rays
OR lord of 2nd just emerged from combustion
judgment: Thief found but goods lost; partial recovery if lord of 2nd recently left combustion.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant joins an angular planet, the querent locates the thief; best outcome if the planet is in the Midheaven. When the lord of the Ascendant joins a cadent planet that does not aspect the Ascendant, the thief escapes or flees. If the cadent planet does aspect the Ascendant, some hope of recovery remains.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to angular planet
OR lord of Ascendant joined to cadent planet
cadent planet not aspecting Ascendant vs. aspecting Ascendant
judgment: Angular: thief found; cadent without aspect: thief flees; cadent with aspect: hopeful outcome.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is under the sun's beams, this indicates the thief will be discovered; this is reinforced if the lord of the Ascendant simultaneously aspects the combust lord of the 7th.
conditions: lord of Ascendant aspects lord of 7th
judgment: Thief is discovered and comes under the querent's control.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is joined to the lord of the Midheaven, the thief returns the property out of fear of royal or governmental authority. When the lord of the Ascendant is joined to the lord of the Midheaven, the owner threatens the thief through royal or superior authority. If neither the lord of the Ascendant nor lord of the 7th aspect each other, a royal or external authority seizes the stolen property.
conditions: lord of 7th joins lord of Midheaven
OR lord of Ascendant joins lord of Midheaven
OR lord of Ascendant and lord of 7th do not aspect each other
judgment: Thief returns goods from fear of authority; or owner uses authority to threaten thief; or external power takes the goods.
notes: A contradictory follow-on statement says lord of 7th joined to lord of Midheaven aids the thief—the translator flags this as inconsistent with the earlier rule.

rule: When the Moon transfers light between the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 7th (i.e., separates from one and applies to the other), the thief will be found.
conditions: Moon transferring light between lord of Ascendant and lord of 7th
judgment: Thief is located.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is joined to the lord of the 3rd, the thief leaves the region. When the lord of the 7th is in an angular sign relative to the Ascendant, the thief does not depart from his current location.
conditions: lord of 7th joined to lord of 3rd
OR lord of 7th in an angle from Ascendant
judgment: Thief flees the region (3rd lord) or remains in place (angular position).

rule: The aspects of malefic planets to the 7th house or its lord indicate what adverse fate or consequences will befall the thief.
conditions: malefic planets aspecting 7th house or lord of 7th
judgment: Nature and severity of consequences for the thief determined by malefic aspects.

rule: When the Moon applies to a malefic, the stolen goods are taken away permanently. When the Moon applies to a benefic that is itself under the rays or otherwise impeded, the goods are also lost. When the Moon applies to a planet in the Ascendant or 7th that is free from malefics, the stolen goods are recovered.
conditions: Moon joining unimpeded planet in Ascendant or 7th
judgment: Goods lost (malefic or impeded benefic); goods found (unimpeded planet in Ascendant or 7th).

rule: When the two luminaries aspect each other by trine or sextile, the stolen goods or lost item will be found. Aspect by square or opposition indicates eventual recovery but only after difficulty and lost hope. When one luminary aspects the Lot of Fortune or is in the same sign as it, the goods are found—more quickly if the Sun aspects, with delay if it is the Moon. If neither luminary aspects the other, nor aspects the Lot of Fortune or the Ascendant, the stolen goods will never be found.
conditions: luminary aspecting or in same sign as Lot of Fortune
no mutual luminary aspect and no aspect to Lot of Fortune or Ascendant
judgment: Trine/sextile: goods found; square/opposition: goods found with difficulty; luminary-Fortune contact: goods found (Sun faster, Moon slower); no contacts: goods never found.

rule: In a question about whether missing property will be found, if the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the lord of the 2nd, or a third planet transfers light between them, or both apply to a planet heavier than themselves (collection of light), the substance will be recovered. Likewise if the lord of the 2nd is located in the Ascendant, the goods will eventually be recovered. Likewise if the lord of the 2nd is joined to a planet already in the 2nd.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon joined to lord of 2nd
OR light transferred to lord of 2nd
OR collection of light to heavier planet
OR lord of 2nd joined to planet in 2nd
judgment: The querent recovers the missing property.
notes: The 2nd house is the significator of the querent's substance.

rule: If the lord of the 2nd does not make an aspect (is unconnected), the missing property will be permanently lost.
judgment: Property is permanently lost.

rule: When the lord of the 8th is joined to the lord of the 7th (the thief's significator), the stolen goods are lost.
conditions: lord of 8th joined to lord of 7th
judgment: Stolen property is lost.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is joined to the lord of the 2nd, the querent's substance is lost.
conditions: lord of 7th joined to lord of 2nd
judgment: The querent loses their property.

rule: When the lord of the 8th (the thief's substance) is joined to the lord of the 2nd (the querent's substance), the querent recovers his own property and additionally gains part of the thief's goods. This is strengthened if the lord of the Ascendant also aspects both.
conditions: lord of 8th joined to lord of 2nd
judgment: Querent recovers goods and also acquires part of the thief's possessions.

rule: If the lord of the Midheaven aspects the significators, royal or governmental authority will take the goods. If the lord of the 8th is joined to the lord of the Midheaven, the thief appeases the ruling authority with money.
conditions: OR lord of 8th joined to lord of Midheaven
judgment: King or authority seizes the goods; or thief bribes authority.

rule: If the lord of the 2nd neither aspects the Ascendant nor its lord, the property is certainly and permanently lost with no trace.
conditions: lord of 2nd does not aspect Ascendant or lord of Ascendant
judgment: Complete and permanent loss of property.

rule: When the lord of the 2nd is joined to the lord of the 3rd, or to the lord of the 9th, or to a planet located in either of those houses, or is itself in those houses, the stolen goods have left or will leave the region.
conditions: lord of 2nd joined to lord of 3rd or 9th
OR lord of 2nd joined to planet in 3rd or 9th
judgment: Stolen goods have departed from the local region.

rule: When both luminaries are below the horizon at the time of the question, the thief will remain unknown permanently.
conditions: both Sun and Moon below the earth
judgment: Thief's identity is never discovered.

rule: When the Moon is in the Ascendant along with her sign-ruler, and the Sun aspects them—especially by trine—the stolen or missing property will be found and returned quickly.
conditions: lord of Moon's sign in Ascendant
judgment: Stolen goods are quickly found and restored.

rule: When both luminaries aspect the Ascendant, the thief is from the household. When only one luminary aspects the Ascendant, the thief has social contact with the household but is not a member of it. When the lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, or the lord of the 7th is with the lord of the Ascendant, the thief is a resident of the house.
conditions: lord of 7th with lord of Ascendant
judgment: Both luminaries aspecting: household thief; one luminary: social acquaintance; lord of Ascendant in Ascendant or lords together: household member.

rule: When the luminaries are in their own domiciles aspecting the Ascendant and its lord, or in the domicile of the lord of the Ascendant, the thief is a household inhabitant. When in their own triplicities, the thief is a relative who does not reside there. When in their own bounds or faces, the thief is an intimate acquaintance who visits frequently.
conditions: luminaries in own domicile aspecting Ascendant
luminaries in own bounds or faces
judgment: Domicile: household resident; triplicity: relative non-resident; bound/face: frequent visitor or intimate acquaintance.

rule: When a luminary aspects the Ascendant but not the 7th, the thief had not previously entered the house before the theft, unless the luminary is in a common sign—in which case the thief has entered multiple times with the household's knowledge. When a luminary aspects the lord of the Ascendant but not the Ascendant itself, the thief is known to the household but has not previously entered.
conditions: luminary aspects lord of Ascendant not Ascendant
judgment: No prior entry (not common sign); repeated prior entry with knowledge (common sign); known but not previously entered (aspects lord not Ascendant).
notes: The translator notes the apparent contradiction that any planet aspecting the Ascendant would also aspect the 7th.

rule: If the lord of the Ascendant has moved past the exact degree of the Ascendant but another planet in the same sign is closer to that degree, the thief belongs to a specific subset of people within the household.
conditions: lord of Ascendant past Ascendant degree
another planet in same sign closer to Ascendant degree
judgment: Thief is among a particular group of household inhabitants.

rule: The lord of the 7th's position relative to its own domicile indicates the thief's social character: in the 9th from its own domicile, the thief is a foreigner from another region; in the 6th or 8th from its own domicile, the thief is a slave; in its own exaltation, the thief is noble; in its own domicile, the thief is a known household inhabitant; in its own triplicity or bound or face, the thief is unknown in the wider region but known in their own local neighborhood.
conditions: lord of 7th in 9th from own domicile
lord of 7th in 6th or 8th from own domicile
lord of 7th in own triplicity, bound, or face
judgment: 9th: foreign thief; 6th/8th: slave; exaltation: noble; own domicile: known household thief; triplicity/bound/face: locally known but not regionally.

rule: When the thief is established as a household member, the identity is refined by the planet serving as significator: Sun indicates the father; Moon the mother; Venus the wife; Saturn a slave or foreigner; Jupiter the most respected person in the household against whom no suspicion would fall; Mars a son, daughter, or brother; Mercury an intimate friend.
judgment: Each planet maps to a specific social relation within the household.
notes: The significator of the robber is defined as the lord of the 7th.

rule: When the significator of the thief (lord of the 7th) is peregrine and the Lot of Fortune is free from malefics, the thief has no prior theft record. Likewise if the lord of the Ascendant is free from malefics. When Mars has separated from the lord of the 7th, the thief has a prior criminal record known to the victims.
conditions: Lot of Fortune free from malefics
lord of Ascendant free from malefics
judgment: No malefic-Lot contact and no Mars separation: first offense; Mars separated from lord of 7th: prior record.

rule: The method the thief used is shown by the planet that is the lord of the 7th: Saturn indicates theft performed with cunning and skill (if Saturn aspects the Moon or Ascendant); Jupiter indicates the thief entered for another purpose and stole opportunistically; Mars indicates the thief broke in by force (piercing walls, breaking locks, using a key); Venus indicates the thief gained entry under the guise of friendship or social visitation; Mercury indicates the thief entered through cleverness or a specific skill or art.
conditions: Saturn as lord of 7th or aspecting Moon/Ascendant
judgment: Saturn: cunning theft; Jupiter: opportunistic; Mars: forcible entry; Venus: social deception; Mercury: skillful/artful entry.

rule: If the significator of the thief is a benefic planet, the thief is a free person; if a malefic, the thief is a slave. Venus or Mercury as significator indicates a young person (Mercury younger than Venus). Mars indicates a young adult of completed youth. Jupiter indicates someone older than Mars. Saturn indicates a very old or decrepit person; if Saturn is oriental, the thief is of mature middle age.
judgment: Free vs. enslaved status; age indicated by specific planet.
notes: The translator notes this paragraph is a mixture of two Dorothean passages and may be garbled.

rule: When the Moon is the significator of the thief, the lunar phase indicates age: beginning of the month = young person; middle of the month = middle-aged adult; end of the month = old person.
judgment: Moon's phase maps directly to the thief's age.

rule: When the Sun is the significator of the thief, the Sun's position between the angles indicates age: between Ascendant and Midheaven indicates a young person, and age increases progressively as the Sun moves toward the 4th house angle, which signifies the end of life.
judgment: Sun's position between angular houses corresponds to the thief's age on a continuum from young to elderly.

rule: The location of stolen goods is found by examining the 4th house sign: Cancer or its triplicity indicates burial near water; Aries or its triplicity indicates a place of animals or fire; Taurus or its triplicity indicates a place of cattle or cows; Virgo indicates a place of grain or provisions; Capricorn indicates a place of sheep; Gemini or its triplicity indicates the residence itself, a chest or enclosed container, or an elevated location.
judgment: Each sign or its triplicity on the 4th indicates a specific type of location for the stolen goods.

rule: When investigating the location of stolen goods within a house, look to the lord of the 4th and any planet located there: Saturn indicates a washroom or dirty, deep, dark, distant place; Jupiter indicates a grove or place of prayer; Mars indicates the kitchen or a place associated with fire; the Sun indicates an enclosed private space used by the master of the house; Venus indicates the women's quarters; Mercury indicates a place of decorated construction, books, or grain storage (especially in Virgo); the Moon indicates proximity to a well, cistern, or place of washing.
judgment: Each planet maps to a specific room or location within the dwelling.

rule: When benefic planets are in the 4th, the stolen goods are in a clean and attractive place and have been handed to a person of high social standing. When malefic planets are in the 4th, the goods are in a foul or unpleasant location and have been handed to a person of low standing.
judgment: Benefic: clean location, noble recipient; malefic: foul location, ignoble recipient.

rule: To determine whether the stolen item is a single object or multiple, count the number of signs between the Moon and Mercury: an even count indicates multiple items or a combined quantity; an odd count indicates a single item.
conditions: number of signs between Moon and Mercury
judgment: Even: multiple items; odd: single item.

rule: When a specific suspect is being evaluated for guilt, use the same approach as evaluating rumors for truth, with the Moon's testimony emphasized. If the Moon is conjoined to a malefic, the suspect is guilty.
judgment: Suspect is the thief.

rule: To determine whether a named person has stolen something, find the stronger of the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon and examine what planet it has separated from. If it has separated from a malefic (i.e., received the malefic's influence), theft has occurred, especially if the separation is from the lord of the 2nd. If it has not separated from a malefic, no theft occurred.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon (stronger of the two) separated from a malefic
judgment: Separation from malefic: person has stolen; no separation from malefic: person has not stolen.

rule: When the Moon is in the bound of Saturn, the stolen object relates to agricultural work or land cultivation. If Saturn is in the Ascendant or Midheaven in an earth sign, the object is valuable and pertains to land-use. If Saturn is in the 4th or 7th, the object is of another kind of substance. If Saturn is cadent and not aspected by a luminary, or is in Aries, the object is of poor quality or unpleasant nature. If Saturn is in Gemini or its triplicity, there are two stolen objects; if Jupiter in the Midheaven aspects Saturn, one is gold; if Jupiter is in the 4th or 7th, it is silver; if Jupiter is cadent, it is lead or similar base material.
judgment: Nature and quantity of stolen goods determined by Saturn's and Jupiter's conditions.
notes: The translator notes Dorotheus's account is briefer and ignores triplicities.

rule: When the Moon is in the bound of Jupiter: if the aspecting planet or Jupiter is in a fire-triplicity sign, the object is gold, silver, or something made by fire; if Venus aspects Jupiter or Jupiter is in Venus's bound, the object is pearl; if Jupiter is in Taurus or its triplicity, the object pertains to clothing or things useful to the wealthy; if Jupiter is in an air-triplicity sign, the object is animal-derived or animate; if Jupiter is in a water-triplicity sign, the object is extracted from water (e.g., pearl).
conditions: sign position of aspecting planet or Jupiter
Venus aspecting Jupiter or Jupiter in Venus's bound
judgment: Type of stolen object identified by sign triplicity and aspects.

rule: When the Moon is in the bound of Mars, the stolen object has been processed by fire or touched by it in some way. If the Moon aspects Venus, the object has been dyed.
judgment: Object processed by fire; if Moon-Venus aspect, object has been dyed.

rule: When the Moon is in the bound of Venus: in fire-triplicity signs, the object is gold or silver; in Taurus-triplicity or Cancer-triplicity, the object is an ornate or precious multi-colored textile; in Gemini and its triplicity, not of animal origin. The condition of Venus indicates newness: Venus emerging from combustion indicates a new item; Venus retrograde, at the end of her course, or in diminished number indicates an old and worn item.
judgment: Sign triplicity identifies material; Venus's state identifies age and condition of object.

rule: When the Moon is in the bound of Mercury, the stolen object is likely books. If the Moon is in Aries or its triplicity, the objects are coins; in Gemini or its triplicity, the coins are stored in a small covered red-leather vessel.
judgment: Objects are books or coins depending on sign placement.
attribution_in_text: Bonatti (BOA) supplementing gap in source text
notes: The source text breaks off; material supplied from Bonatti.

rule: The Moon's sign position combined with aspects from sign-rulers indicates the nature of the stolen object: Aries = head or face ornament; Taurus = neck jewelry or precious substance; Gemini with Mercury aspect = coins, without = leather goods; Cancer = something from or associated with water or moisture; Leo with Sun aspect = gold or silver, without = iron or brass; Virgo with Mercury aspect = coins, without = textiles; Libra with Venus aspect = items sold by weight with pleasant odor or women's ornaments, without = an animal traded for its blood; Scorpio with Mars aspect = gold or silver, without = raw ore or fire-worked gleaming metal; Sagittarius with Jupiter aspect = multiple or dyed objects, without = something of low value; Capricorn = old, shabby, low-value item; with Saturn aspect = earth products or seeds; Aquarius with Saturn aspect = an animal or animal product, with Jupiter = gold or silver, with Sun and Mercury = coins in leather; Pisces with Jupiter aspect = pearls, amber, or water-derived objects, without = silk in multiple colors.
conditions: ruling planet of that sign aspecting Moon
judgment: Specific material or category of stolen item identified.

rule: The physical description and social character of a thief may be derived from the decan (face) rising at the moment of the question. Each of the 36 decans carries a traditional image that describes the appearance or character of the person in question. The practitioner identifies which decan is ascending and applies the corresponding description.
conditions: decan of Ascendant at moment of question
judgment: The traditional image of the rising decan describes the thief's appearance or character.
notes: The source lists all 36 decan images. The translator notes one would ordinarily expect the decan of the 7th to be used for the thief; Bonatti uses the 7th. The chapter heading's term 'imbrione' is of unknown meaning, possibly from Arabic root meaning 'to appear or manifest.'

rule: In a question about a partnership or business association, the Ascendant represents the querent; the 7th represents the associate; the Midheaven represents the condition or activity of the partnership; the 4th represents the outcome or end of the partnership.
judgment: Four angles serve as significators for the parties and the partnership's trajectory.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant (or Moon) is in movable signs, the partnership will experience instability but ultimately continue. In fixed signs, the partnership will be durable and lasting. In common signs, the partnership will be marked by shared wealth and mutual faithfulness.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon in movable signs
judgment: Movable: unstable but continuing; fixed: durable; common: prosperous and faithful.

rule: Malefic planets in the Ascendant indicate injury, deception, and separation coming from the querent's side. Malefic planets in the 7th indicate the harm comes from the associate.
judgment: Malefics show which party causes harm or deception in the partnership.

rule: When the Moon applies to the lord of her domicile, the partners separate with mutual esteem and good fortune. If the Moon does not aspect her domicile lord, separation occurs through mutual suspicion. Malefics below the earth cause separation through mutual ill-feeling. Benefics in the Midheaven multiply partnership wealth; malefics there diminish it. When the Moon is joined to the lord of her domicile in the same sign and both are joined to a malefic, the partnership ends only at death.
conditions: Moon applies to lord of her domicile
Moon does not aspect her domicile lord
Moon and domicile lord in same sign both joined to malefic
judgment: Various modes of partnership dissolution or continuation.

rule: When asking whether a querent will find a specific notable person at an expected location, examine the lord of the 7th: in an angle, the person is at the expected location; in a succeedent house, the person is nearby; in a cadent house, the person is not at the location.
judgment: Angular: person is present; succeedent: person is near; cadent: person is absent.

rule: In a military question, the Ascendant and its lord plus the planet from which the Moon is separating represent the querent and initiator of the war; the 7th and its lord plus the planet to which the Moon is applying represent the enemy. If the Moon has no separation or application, she is not used in the judgment. Superior planets carry more weight than inferior ones in war questions.
judgment: Significators assigned; Moon excluded if void of course in this matter; superiors outweigh inferiors.
notes: Likely influenced by Theophilus of Edessa and Dorotheus Carmen V.33.

rule: When the two main significators (lord of Ascendant and lord of 7th) are in trine or sextile with mutual reception, peace will occur and the lighter planet initiates it. In square or opposition with mutual reception, peace comes after conflict. If one significator is retrograde or in a debilitated position relative to the receiving planet, that party will betray and act against its partner; the house involved indicates the manner of betrayal (2nd = financial guarantee then seizure of wealth; 6th or 7th = security then capture and punishment; 8th = killing and destruction).
conditions: one significator retrograde or in debilitated position
judgment: Harmonious aspects with reception: peace; discordant with reception: peace after conflict; retrograde/debilitated: betrayal with consequences matching the house.

rule: When one significator is a superior planet received in an angle, its party wins (unless that planet is entering combustion). When the lord of the Ascendant is a superior in a cadent house and the lord of the 7th is a inferior in an angle, the judgment is deferred until examining what the lord of the 7th joins: if it joins an angular planet that receives it, the enemy wins. If the lord of the 7th is strong but joins a cadent impeding planet, the enemy remains strong only while in that sign, then weakens progressively until impeded by malefics or entering combustion, at which point the enemy is destroyed.
conditions: lord of 7th joins angular received planet
lord of 7th joins cadent impeding planet
judgment: Superior angular received: querent's party wins; enemy joins angular received planet: enemy wins; enemy joins cadent impeding planet: enemy weakens as planet changes sign.
notes: Inferior planets are judged by quality of house position, freedom from impediment, and support from superiors only.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th, the querent is in the position of the conquered, especially if the lord of the 7th also aspects it. When the lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant, the querent is strengthened, and if the lord of the Ascendant aspects the lord of the 7th, the querent will capture the enemy.
conditions: lord of 7th aspects lord of Ascendant
lord of Ascendant aspects lord of 7th
judgment: Lord of Ascendant in 7th: querent weakened or conquered; lord of 7th in Ascendant: querent strong and may capture enemy.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th, or is joined to the lord of the 8th (or vice versa), the querent faces death. Conversely, when the lord of the 7th is in the 2nd, or joined to the lord of the 2nd (or vice versa), the enemy faces death—more certainly if the lord of the 2nd is impeded by malefics and does not receive the applying planet.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to lord of 8th
lord of 7th joined to lord of 2nd
lord of 2nd impeded by malefics without reception
judgment: 8th house connections: querent's death; 2nd house connections for enemy: enemy's death.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is joined to the lord of the Midheaven (or vice versa) and the lord of the Ascendant is in the Midheaven, the querent is dominant in the conflict and will capture the enemy, especially if the receiver is angular (making the querent unconquerable). Conversely, when the lord of the 7th is in the 4th or joined to its lord (with the receiver angular), the enemy is unconquerable and the querent's position is threatened.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to lord of Midheaven
lord of 7th in 4th or joined to lord of 4th
judgment: Querent's Midheaven connection: querent dominant and unconquerable; enemy's 4th house connection: enemy unconquerable.

rule: When one significator is joined to a planet in an angle or to the lord of an angle (especially if the significator itself is in an angle), the party it represents is strong. When that significator is in a fixed sign and free from malefics with reception, the party is secure. When in a movable sign, the party's death after initial success is feared.
conditions: significator joined to angular planet or lord of angle
judgment: Angular and fixed with reception: strong and stable; movable: death feared after success.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is in the 12th, the querent's side flees or retreats. When the lord of the 7th is in the 6th, the enemy flees.
judgment: 12th: querent's party flees; 6th: enemy flees.

rule: A retrograde significator indicates the defeat and weakness of the party it represents.
judgment: Party of that significator is weakened and suffering defeat.

rule: When the lord of the 10th is in the Ascendant, royal authority aids the querent. When the lord of the 10th is in the 7th, royal authority aids the enemy.
judgment: Kingly or governmental support goes to the party whose angle contains the lord of the 10th.

rule: When one of the luminaries pushes its disposition (applies) to a significator, the party represented by that significator receives strength and royal aid. When the Moon separates from the lord of the Ascendant and applies to the lord of the 7th, the enemy gains victory.
conditions: Moon separates from lord of Ascendant and applies to lord of 7th
judgment: Luminary application: that party strengthened and aided by king; Moon moving to enemy: enemy victorious.

rule: When Saturn is in an angle at the time of the question and lacks any dignifying testimony, the war will be prolonged until Saturn leaves the angle. If Saturn is also retrograde, the war will be repeatedly renewed.
judgment: Long war (Saturn angular); repeated or recurring war (Saturn retrograde).

rule: When the Moon is with Mars and the benefics are cadent from the Moon, the querent will be killed or captured.
judgment: Querent killed or captured.

rule: When the Sun is with the North or South Node at the time a war begins, there will be massive casualties in both armies and no peace will be established between them. When both the lord of the Ascendant and lord of the 7th are with the South Node, almost total annihilation of both armies is indicated.
conditions: Sun conjunct North or South Node
lord of Ascendant and lord of 7th both with South Node
judgment: Sun-node: massive casualties, no peace; both lords with South Node: near-total destruction of both armies.

rule: The house position of Mars at the time of the question indicates the cause of the war: 1st = sustenance or way of life; 2nd = wealth/substance; 3rd = faith or religion; 4th = land; 5th = substance, kinship between commanders or possible agreement, or a woman or city (especially if Moon joins Mercury from dignity); 6th = a minor cause with many casualties; 7th = ancient enmity, not for material gain; 8th = an old matter with blood vengeance (if Moon aspects lord of Midheaven, it concerns a kingdom's wealth); 9th = religious faith; Midheaven with Moon square or opposite Mars or conjunct = honor or aggrandizement of the king or acquisition of a kingdom; 11th = on behalf of friends or subordinates; 12th = ancient enmity but actual war will not occur (Mars cadent from angles).
conditions: Mars in each of the 12 houses
judgment: House of Mars identifies the underlying cause or motive for the war.

rule: When the Moon is in the Ascendant and Mars is in the 7th, or conversely Mars is in the Ascendant and the Moon is in the 7th, the party that initiates and begins the battle will be killed.
conditions: Moon in Ascendant and Mars in 7th
OR Mars in Ascendant and Moon in 7th
judgment: The instigator of the battle is killed.

rule: In military questions, each house from the Ascendant carries specific significations: 1st = the initiating party and justness of their cause; 2nd = whether war will arise and whether it will be profitable or harmful; 3rd = weapons used and which weapons will bring victory; 4th = terrain and geography of the battlefield; 5th = morale, readiness, and boldness of the soldiers; 6th = the animals and mounts of the soldiers; 7th = the enemy, siege engines, and whether war is conducted with skill; 8th = plague, capture, death, and the defeat and flight of the losing party; 9th = intelligence, scouts, enemy intelligence, and strategic deception; 10th = conduct and character of the commanders; 11th = battle organization, formation, and advance; 12th = the besieged city and its inhabitants.
conditions: each of the 12 houses in a military horary chart
judgment: Each house maps to a specific dimension of military activity.
notes: The 5th and 12th house assignments differ from other uses mentioned earlier in the chapter.

rule: Benefics in or aspecting the 2nd and its lord in a good condition indicate the strength and loyalty of the querent's soldiers. The 8th and its lord similarly indicate the enemy's soldiers. Benefics in common signs or signs of many offspring or movable signs in the 2nd or 8th indicate a large number of soldiers. An oriental planet in the 2nd or an oriental lord of the 2nd indicates the querent's soldiers are loyal; a retrograde lord of the 2nd indicates the soldiers will disobey. A malefic in the 11th or a retrograde lord of the 11th indicates the king's servants and allies are traitors, especially when combined with a malefic or Mercury in the 8th from the Sun and the South Node with the Sun.
conditions: lord of 2nd or 8th in good position
benefics in common, fruitful, or movable signs
malefic in 11th or retrograde lord of 11th
malefic or Mercury in 8th from Sun
judgment: Each condition modifies assessment of troop loyalty, quantity, and quality for each side.

rule: When a peace mediator between warring parties is indicated, the planet facilitating this mediates characteristics: if it is in its own domicile the mediator is native to one of the parties; otherwise a foreigner. Saturn: old man; Jupiter: noble and great; Mars: a military commander who wishes ill and is dishonest; Sun: a king or head of an organization; Venus: a man without professional discipline or skills; Mercury: a scholar, scribe, or wise man; Moon: a man who mediates with genuine goodwill and justice.
judgment: Planet's nature and domicile condition describe the mediator's character and origin.

rule: Mercury impeded under the rays by both significators indicates mutual betrayal and cunning between the warring parties. When Mars is also with Mercury, the betrayal becomes public and cannot be concealed. The Moon and Saturn witnessing the Ascendant indicates betrayal has occurred or will occur. Jupiter witnessing the Moon and Ascendant indicates good outcomes. Venus witnessing does not indicate betrayal. Mercury aspecting the Ascendant or Moon indicates cunning and betrayal; if Mercury is under the rays and the Moon is with Mars or the planet Mars separated from, the mediator is captured. Mercury oriental: the mediator escapes difficulty. Mercury in a common sign: multiple mediators. A malefic overcoming Mercury (in the 10th whole-sign from Mercury): severe punishment for the mediator. A benefic overcoming: escape.
conditions: Mercury impeded under rays by both significators
Mercury under rays with Moon with Mars
judgment: Various outcomes for betrayal, cunning, and the mediator's fate.
notes: The translator notes the phrase 'under the rays from both planets' is unusual; may refer to besiegement by the two significators.

rule: The planet from which Mars separates represents the war's initiator; the planet to which Mars applies represents the adversary. If Mars separates from benefics, the initiator seeks just cause; if from malefics, the initiator does not seek justice. If Mars applies to benefics, the enemy seeks just cause; if to malefics, the enemy does not.
judgment: Identifies which party has just cause in the war.

rule: A significator in a movable sign indicates weakness and risk of flight for that party. A significator in a common sign indicates perseverance and sustained engagement in the war. A significator in a fixed sign indicates stability and steadfastness.
judgment: Movable: weak, flight risk; common: perseverant; fixed: stable.

rule: Among the five dignities, exaltation confers more strength than domicile; domicile more than triplicity; triplicity more than bound; bound more than face. A planet aspecting its own domicile lord doubles its strength. A planet in its descension or detriment whose domicile lord does not aspect it is at its weakest. The dignity also indicates the social rank of the commander: exaltation = king; domicile = royal relative or household member; triplicity = noble's son; bound = below that; face = below that.
conditions: planet in descension or detriment without domicile lord aspect
judgment: Dignity level determines party's military strength and commander's social rank.

rule: Mars in his own exaltation or the Sun's exaltation indicates a famous and manifest war; if also in the Midheaven, the war's fame spreads widely. Mars in the Ascendant produces a lesser conflict. Mars in the 7th angle indicates cunning and sustained battle. Mars in a fixed sign but not angular produces a smaller conflict. In a common sign, the war is repeated and multiplied. In a movable sign, the war is intense. In his own domicile or triplicity, middling war. In his own descension, the war quickly dissipates.
conditions: Mars in own exaltation or Sun's exaltation
Mars in fixed sign off angles
Mars in own domicile or triplicity
judgment: Each condition indicates the intensity, fame, duration, and nature of the war.

rule: To determine whether an army is large or small, count the number of signs between the Moon and Mercury: even count = large army; odd count = small army.
conditions: number of signs between Moon and Mercury
judgment: Even: large army; odd: small army.

rule: In a question about whether an absent person is alive or dead, indicators of death include: the lord of the Ascendant or Moon in the 4th or 8th; they are combust, in their own descension, or with the lord of the 8th or 4th; if both indicators are present, examine malefic and benefic aspects to modify the judgment. A retrograde lord of the Ascendant in its own descension or in the 8th that is moving toward combustion indicates death. Moon applying to a planet below the horizon indicates death; to a planet above the horizon, life. Lord of Ascendant in the 12th with malefics aspecting and one luminary impeded indicates death. Malefics with both luminaries without benefic aspect indicate death. Moon with Mars in the 4th without benefic aspect indicates death. Lot of Fortune with malefics in the 4th, 6th, or 12th without benefic aspect indicates death.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon in 4th or 8th
Moon applying below or above horizon
lord of Ascendant in 12th with malefics
Lot of Fortune with malefics in 4th, 6th, or 12th
judgment: Cluster of malefic conditions: death indicated; life indicated when planets are above earth and free from malefic impediment.
notes: The translator notes ambiguity about whether all conditions must coexist or function as independent indicators.

rule: If the lord of the Ascendant is combust and no benefic aspects it, and the Moon is below the earth and cadent (in the 3rd or 6th), death is indicated for the absent person—especially if the Moon is in the 3rd degree of Scorpio and afflicted by Saturn, as this combination inherently signifies death.
conditions: lord of Ascendant combust without benefic aspect
Moon below earth cadent in 3rd or 6th
judgment: Death of the absent person is confirmed.
notes: Saturn is identified as naturally signifying death in this specific configuration.

rule: In a question about foreign travel, the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon signify the querent; the 9th house and its lord signify the foreign journey itself.
judgment: Standard significator assignments for travel questions.

rule: Travel will occur when: the lord of the Ascendant or Moon is in the 9th; one of them is joined to the lord of the 9th; the lord of the 9th is in the Ascendant or joined to the lord of the Ascendant; a third planet transfers light between the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 9th; or both the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 9th apply to a heavier planet that aspects the 9th house (collection of light with 9th house aspect). If none of these conditions obtain, travel will not occur.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon in 9th
lord of 9th joined to lord of Ascendant
collection of light with 9th house aspect
judgment: Presence of connection: travel occurs; absence: travel does not occur.

rule: A peregrine malefic in the Ascendant impeding the lord of the Ascendant or lord of the 9th blocks travel for reasons originating with the querent himself. A malefic in the 7th indicates obstruction from the destination or the matter sought. A malefic in the Midheaven indicates obstruction from a superior authority or the king.
judgment: Source of travel impediment identified by which angle holds the malefic.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant joins the lord of the 9th after having joined a malefic by opposition, conjunction, or square, difficulties will follow the journey. The nature of those difficulties depends on which house the malefic rules: 6th = illness; 4th = imprisonment or sorrow; 8th = death; 7th or 12th = trouble from thieves or enemies. If the malefic aspects from the Ascendant, killing is feared; from the 2nd, financial loss; from the 4th (square from Ascendant), bodily harm; from the 10th (second square), loss of substance.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joins lord of 9th after joining malefic
malefic's position by aspect from Ascendant
judgment: Specific type of misfortune after the journey determined by malefic's house rulership and position.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant or in its own domicile and is not joined to the lord of the 9th, travel will not occur—especially if the sign involved is fixed, since fixed signs are inimical to journeys.
conditions: lord of Ascendant in Ascendant or own domicile
judgment: No travel; the querent remains at home.

rule: When the Moon is received, the journey proceeds with ease. When the Moon is not received, the journey is slow, unproductive, and unwelcoming at the destination. If the lord of the Ascendant aspects the Moon from opposition, it reinforces the same indication.
conditions: lord of Ascendant in opposition to Moon
judgment: Reception: easy journey; no reception: slow, difficult, fruitless journey.

rule: In a travel question: the Ascendant represents the traveler's physical and mental condition; the Midheaven represents the things the traveler seeks; the 7th represents the destination; the 4th represents the end of the matter. Benefics in the Ascendant: good physical and mental condition; benefics in the Midheaven: successful outcome of sought matters; benefics in the 7th: satisfaction at the destination; benefics in the 4th: the end of the matter fulfills the querent's wishes. Malefics in the Ascendant or Midheaven or 6th: illness, wasted effort, and loss.
judgment: Benefics in each angle: favorable for that dimension; malefics in Ascendant, Midheaven, or 6th: adverse for that dimension.

rule: Once travel is confirmed, the Moon's application identifies who the traveler is visiting: Moon applying to Sun = nobles or king; to Saturn = lowly or ignoble people; to Jupiter = nobles; to Venus = women; to Mercury = scholars, merchants, or wise men; Moon void of course = someone already known to the traveler. Moon separating from Saturn = traveling because of debt pressure; Moon separating from Mars = traveling as a fugitive or under duress from authority.
judgment: Planet receiving Moon's light identifies type of person being visited; separation from Saturn or Mars identifies motivation for travel.
notes: Translator notes Mars is omitted from both manuscript versions; Bonatti adds that Moon-Mars indicates travel to warriors or pirates.

rule: The planet receiving the Moon's light, if in its own domicile, indicates the person being visited is a citizen of the region. If in its own triplicity, that person is a resident but not a native. If the lord of the planet's domicile aspects it, the person is well-known locally; if not, unknown. Aspect from square = moderately regarded; from opposition = disliked and contentious; from trine or sextile = esteemed; conjoined in same sign = someone who takes wealth by force.
conditions: planet receiving Moon's light in own domicile
lord of domicile aspecting or not
square, opposition, trine, sextile, or conjunction
judgment: Describes the social standing, reputation, and character of the person the traveler goes to meet.

rule: The sign holding the malefic that impedes the lord of the Ascendant or Moon identifies the type of danger on the journey: human signs (Gemini and its triplicity) = robbers or highway criminals; water signs = shipwreck; animal signs = danger from beasts or their attacks; signs of seeds = danger from trees, thorns, heights, or poisoned food; Leo specifically = wolves; Scorpio specifically = reptiles; Pisces specifically = aquatic creatures. Mars represents greater danger on land; Saturn represents greater danger at sea.
judgment: Nature of travel danger determined by sign element and specific sign of the malefic.

rule: When a traveler enters a city, erect a chart for that moment and examine the lord of the 2nd: retrograde = quick return without completing business; in second station (turning direct) = moderate speed of return with business completed after difficulty; in first station (about to go retrograde) = slow return without completing business; in Ascendant, Midheaven, or 11th = sound and successful journey; in 7th = difficulty and conflict on the journey; in 9th or 3rd = the traveler will not rest and will move on to another land; in the 4th with a malefic aspecting or conjunct = death in this region, final journey.
conditions: lord of 2nd in Ascendant, Midheaven, or 11th
judgment: Lord of 2nd's condition indicates quality, duration, and outcome of the foreign stay.
notes: The 2nd house is used because it is the sign immediately following the Ascendant, showing what comes next to the traveler.

rule: When the Moon is joined to the lord of the 2nd in the same sign, or lord of the 2nd aspects the Moon, or the Moon is joined to Mercury in one sign, or Mars aspects the Moon, the traveler will encounter injuries, illness outbreaks, or severe troubles. If this occurs with the Moon in the 4th, death in that region is indicated. If Moon is in another angle, the damage or illness persists as a permanent mark. If benefics aspect the Moon, there will be recovery; if benefics do not aspect, the traveler dies from those conditions.
conditions: Moon joined to lord of 2nd in same sign
Moon joined to Mercury in same sign
judgment: Combination indicates injury/illness; angle placement determines severity; benefic aspect determines survival.

rule: In a question about a ruler's journey and the condition of those left behind, a malefic in the 2nd without testimony or reception indicates harm to those remaining after departure. Mars in the 2nd without reception indicates conflict, war, or fire among those left behind; Saturn without reception indicates robbers, illness, or shipwreck. If the malefic is received, harm is mitigated. If the malefic is in its own descension, harm is completed or magnified; if also retrograde, dissolution and destruction are indicated.
judgment: Nature and severity of harm to those left behind determined by specific malefic and its reception/dignity status.
notes: The translator notes Bonatti's interpretation differs: reception mitigates regardless of descension; retrograde with reception still diminishes malice somewhat.

rule: The position of a malefic relative to the horizon indicates when harm occurs during a royal journey: a malefic above the earth between the Ascendant and 10th indicates harm on the return trip; between the 7th and 10th indicates harm at departure; a malefic below the earth between the Ascendant and 4th indicates harm in things acquired during the outward journey; between the 4th and 7th indicates harm in things acquired on the return journey.
judgment: Position of malefic relative to angles identifies timing and type of harm during the journey.
notes: The translator notes Bonatti believes this passage contains errors from the Latin translator.

rule: When deciding whether to remain or depart, if the Moon is separating from a malefic, leaving is better. If the Moon is separating from a benefic, staying is more beneficial. If the condition of the lord of the Ascendant is favorable, staying is better; if the condition of the lord of the 7th is superior, departing is better.
judgment: Moon-malefic separation: leave; Moon-benefic separation: stay; lord of Ascendant strong: stay; lord of 7th stronger: go.

rule: For any general question about whether to proceed with an intended action, if both the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are separating from malefics and applying to benefics, advise proceeding with the plan. If both are separating from benefics and applying to malefics, advise against proceeding.
conditions: lord of Ascendant and Moon separating from malefics and applying to benefics
lord of Ascendant and Moon separating from benefics and applying to malefics
judgment: Benefic application: proceed; malefic application: do not proceed.

rule: Questions about imprisoned or captured persons are treated analogously to foreign travel questions, since both involve exit from a current location. When lords of the angles are in their own domiciles in the angles, this provides an initial indication that the person will remain imprisoned in that period.
conditions: lords of angles in own domiciles in angles
judgment: Initial indication of continued imprisonment.

rule: For a captive, if the lord of the Ascendant is in an angle, imprisonment is prolonged (more so in the 4th, especially with the lord of the 12th or a malefic aspecting it, adding punishment to imprisonment). If the lord of the Ascendant is cadent but joined to an angular planet, imprisonment is extended despite hope of escape. If the lord of the Ascendant is in an angle but joined to a cadent planet, liberation comes after lost hope.
conditions: lord of Ascendant in angle with lord of 12th or malefic aspecting
lord of Ascendant cadent joined to angular planet
lord of Ascendant in angle joined to cadent planet
judgment: Angular: prolonged imprisonment; cadent joined to angle: prolonged despite hope; angular joined to cadent: liberation after despair.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant joins a malefic in the 4th, or the lord of the 8th is in the Ascendant, the captive will die in prison.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to malefic in 4th
judgment: Captive dies in prison.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins a planet in the 3rd or 9th (one that is not the lord of any angle), liberation is indicated. If the lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins the lord of the 3rd or 9th, liberation comes through the prisoner's own effort. If conversely the lord of the 3rd or 9th joins the lord of the Ascendant, liberation comes through someone else's efforts without the prisoner's own striving.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon joined to planet in 3rd or 9th not lord of angle
lord of Ascendant or Moon joined to lord of 3rd or 9th
lord of 3rd or 9th joined to lord of Ascendant
judgment: 3rd/9th planet: liberation; querent applies to 3rd/9th lord: self-liberation; 3rd/9th lord applies to querent's lord: liberation by another's effort.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant joins the lord of the 12th and that lord is on the left (below-horizon) side of the Ascendant, this indicates the captive flees from prison. Likewise when the lord of the 3rd or 9th is with the lord of the 12th.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joins lord of 12th on left of Ascendant
lord of 3rd or 9th with lord of 12th
judgment: Prison escape by flight.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant joins the lord of the 3rd or 9th but the receiving (heavier) planet is in an angle, the captive will not be freed until that receiver leaves the angular sign and enters a succeedent sign.
conditions: lord of Ascendant joined to lord of 3rd or 9th
judgment: Liberation delayed until receiving planet changes sign from angular to succeedent.

rule: The Moon's sign indicates the speed of liberation for a captive: movable signs indicate quick liberation with many allies (Cancer is slow despite being movable because it is the Moon's own domicile; Aries and Libra are faster than Capricorn which indicates slowness, solitude, and enemy interference). Fixed signs indicate slow exit (Aquarius is slowest). Common signs indicate prolonged imprisonment if the captive is not freed before the Moon leaves that sign, especially if it is a domicile of Jupiter without Jupiter aspecting it. In Mercury's domiciles, the captive finds good conditions within the prison.
conditions: Moon in common sign in Jupiter's domicile without Jupiter's aspect
judgment: Sign quality and specific sign determine liberation speed and prison conditions.

rule: When the Moon is in an angle and joins a planet on the left of the Ascendant with the lord of the Ascendant testifying, liberation is indicated. When the Moon is cadent and joined to an angular planet, imprisonment is prolonged unless that planet is the lord of the 3rd or 9th—in which case liberation comes when the planet changes signs. If the Moon is cadent and joined to a cadent planet that is a lord of an angle, hope persists until that planet enters an angle, at which point hope is lost. If the receiving planet is a lord of an angle in the 3rd or 9th, liberation is easier. When the Moon joins the lord of the Ascendant specifically, liberation is delayed.
conditions: Moon angular joined to planet on left of Ascendant with lord of Ascendant testifying
Moon cadent joined to angular planet
angular planet is lord of 3rd or 9th
Moon cadent joined to cadent planet who is lord of an angle
Moon joined to lord of Ascendant
judgment: Varied liberation timing depending on Moon's placement and the nature of the receiving planet.

rule: When the lord of the Ascendant is entering combustion and a malefic is in the 4th, the captive rarely survives. If the malefic is Mars specifically, the captive is killed after leaving prison. If the lord of the Ascendant has already passed through combustion, the captive will suffer severe illness. The further a malefic in an angle is from the Sun's degree, the milder the captive's illness and the sooner recovery occurs. When the lord of the Ascendant joins the lord of the 8th or a malefic in the 4th, the captive dies in prison. Saturn with or aspecting from strength: prolonged imprisonment, sorrow, loss of substance and bodily harm. Mars: bondage and physical restraint. Moon impeded at the same time: great distress without physical punishment. Moon aspects her own domicile lord: easier outcome; if not, harder.
conditions: lord of Ascendant entering combustion with malefic in 4th
malefic in angle far from Sun
lord of Ascendant joined to lord of 8th or malefic in 4th
Saturn with or aspecting lord of Ascendant
Moon aspects or does not aspect her domicile lord
judgment: Combustion with Mars in 4th: death after release; past combustion: severe illness; Saturn: prolonged imprisonment; Mars: physical bondage; Moon not aspecting domicile lord: worse outcome.
