rule: When the lord of the Ascendant and lord of the 7th aspect each other by trine or sextile, the opposing party pursues the captive with patience and seeks peace. When the aspect is by square or opposition, the opposing party pursues with severity and persistence in demanding justice.
conditions: lord of Ascendant and lord of 7th in trine or sextile
judgment: Harmonious aspects: moderate pursuit; inharmonious aspects: severe and persistent pursuit.

rule: When asked about the arrival of an absent person, examine the lord of the Ascendant: in the Ascendant or 10th (or committed to a planet there) = arrival indicated; in the 9th or Midheaven (or committed to a planet there) = arrival indicated; in the 7th or 4th = arrival is delayed and the person has not yet left their current location; in the 9th or 3rd joined to a planet in the Ascendant = on their way back; in the 8th or 2nd joined to a planet in the 10th = same indication; cadent without aspect to an angle or the Ascendant = slow return; retrograde lord of Ascendant aspecting the Ascendant, or the lord of the Ascendant or Moon joined to a retrograde planet = arrival indicated; lord of Ascendant impeded = duress and delay.
conditions: lord of Ascendant in various houses
committed disposition to planet in angle
retrograde lord of Ascendant aspecting Ascendant
judgment: House of lord of Ascendant determines whether and how quickly the absent person will arrive.
notes: Translator notes ambiguity about distinction between 'tenth' and 'Midheaven' in Sahl's text.

rule: As a secondary indicator for the absent person's arrival, examine the Moon: if she commits her disposition to the lord of the Ascendant in or near the Ascendant (within 2 degrees), the return is quick. If the lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th or 8th, the return is prolonged. If the Moon separates from the lord of the 4th, 7th, 9th, or 3rd and joins the lord of the Ascendant, arrival is indicated. If the Moon separates from a planet below the horizon (left of Ascendant) and joins one above the horizon (right of Ascendant), arrival is indicated. If the Moon is cadent and joins an above-horizon planet in the 10th, arrival comes with delay. If the Moon is above the horizon (right of Ascendant), she is impeded, indicating duress and delayed arrival.
conditions: Moon commits disposition to lord of Ascendant near Ascendant
Moon separates from lord of 4th, 7th, 9th, or 3rd and joins lord of Ascendant
Moon separates from below-horizon planet and joins above-horizon planet
Moon cadent joining above-horizon planet in 10th
judgment: Various Moon conditions indicate presence, speed, or delay of return.
notes: Manuscript variant (BN) adds that Moon on the left of Ascendant (below horizon) would be quicker than the right.

rule: To evaluate a dream or vision, examine the houses in priority order for a planet to serve as significator: 9th first, then 10th, then Ascendant, then 7th, then 4th, then 3rd. The first house found containing a planet provides the significator. If no planet is found in any of these six houses, the vision is illusory, deceptive, or forgotten.
conditions: no planet found in any of these
judgment: First planet found in sequence becomes the dream significator; no planet found = invalid or forgotten dream.
notes: Chapter absent from BN manuscript; contains grammatical errors suggesting later addition.

rule: The nature of the dream significator planet indicates what was seen: Saturn or South Node = frightening vision; examine the house it rules for the specific domain of fear. Jupiter = kings and exalted persons. Mars = hunting, combat, legal disputes, conflict, flesh, blood, or weapons. Venus = clothing, pleasant or fragrant things, pearls, women, or young people. Mercury = aromatic or mixed things, speeches, coins, imagery, voices, commercial activity, or disputes. Sun = flight between earth and sky, light, fire, or kings. Moon = women, the sea, old destitute women, or flowing water. South Node = darkness, dust, whispers, or murmurs. North Node = greenery, pleasant fragrance, and gold.
conditions: identity of planet serving as dream significator
judgment: Planet's traditional nature maps to specific dream content.

rule: When the dream significator is a malefic and is in a feminine sign, the frightening content involves heights, cliffs, falling, or violent winds. In an earth sign: being buried, besieged, falling into a pit, or trapped in a dark confined space with eventual escape. In a fire sign: hanging, burning, flame, fire, gloom, or blackness. In a water sign: drowning, flooding, the sea, or mortal danger from water.
judgment: Sign's element and gender identify the specific type of terrifying dream content.

rule: After finding the dream significator, examine what planet the lord of the Ascendant and the significator are applying to: if they apply to a benefic, the threatening elements of the dream will not pursue the dreamer. If they apply to a malefic, harm will come to the dreamer in the area of life ruled by that malefic's house (e.g., lord of 2nd = financial harm; lord of 7th = harm through women or partners; lord of 5th = harm through children). The same principle applies to favorable dreams: the house lord of the planet joined with the significator identifies where the benefit will materialize.
conditions: lord of Ascendant and dream significator apply to benefic
house ruled by the malefic or benefic joined
judgment: Benefic application: harm averted; malefic application: harm in domain of that house; favorable dream: benefit in domain of joined planet's house.

rule: In a question about attaining a position of authority or kingdom, the lord of the Ascendant or Moon joined to the lord of the 10th, with the receiver aspecting the Midheaven, indicates success obtained through the querent's own effort. The lord of the Ascendant or Moon in the 10th without impediment: same. If the lord of the Midheaven is in the Ascendant or joins the lord of the Ascendant, or joins a benefic in the Ascendant, the position will be obtained without effort or inconvenience. A planet transferring light between the significators indicates success obtained through an intermediary acting on the querent's behalf.
conditions: lord of Ascendant or Moon joined to lord of 10th with receiver aspecting Midheaven
lord of Ascendant or Moon in 10th unimpeded
lord of Midheaven in Ascendant or joining lord of Ascendant
lord of Midheaven joining benefic in Ascendant
judgment: Various modes of attaining the kingdom or position of authority.

rule: Malefic planets impede a question about attaining authority from square or opposition (destroying the question) but impede less from trine or sextile.
conditions: malefic in square or opposition to significators
malefic in trine or sextile to significators
judgment: Square/opposition: question destroyed or severely impeded; trine/sextile: minor impediment.

rule: When both the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the Midheaven are joined to the same planet in the Ascendant or Midheaven (collection of light), subsequently examine the Moon: if she is joined to the lord of the 10th, success is indicated. If the Moon joins neither but is free from malefics, the querent attains it with broad support. If the Moon is not free but another planet carries light toward the Midheaven while free from malefics, and the lords of the Ascendant and 10th both join it before it leaves that sign, the querent fully attains the position.
conditions: lord of Ascendant and lord of Midheaven both joined to same planet
Moon free from malefics but not joined to significators
other planet carrying light to Midheaven free from malefics while lords of Ascendant and 10th join it
judgment: Progressive conditions indicate full, partial, or supported attainment.

rule: The dignity of the lord of the Ascendant indicates the scope of the authority obtained: in its own domicile = authority over the land where the querent currently is; in its own exaltation = authority over many lands and a prestigious position; in its own triplicity = important role but not in the querent's own land; in no dignity = the querent is unknown in the land they govern.
conditions: lord of Ascendant in own domicile
judgment: Domicile: local authority; exaltation: broad/prestigious authority; triplicity: authority elsewhere; no dignity: obscure ruler.

rule: When a single planet is simultaneously the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the 10th (e.g., Ascendant Virgo and 10th house Gemini, both ruled by Mercury), the querent attains the position if that planet is received and the Moon commits her disposition and strength to it from an angle.
conditions: single planet rules both Ascendant and 10th
judgment: Attainment of the position is confirmed.

rule: When the lord of the 10th is joined to the lord of the 4th and the lord of the 4th is joined to the lord of the Ascendant, the querent attains the position. When the lord of the Ascendant is joined to the lord of the 4th and the lord of the 4th is joined to the lord of the Midheaven, the querent attains it after losing hope.
conditions: lord of 10th joined to lord of 4th joined to lord of Ascendant
lord of Ascendant joined to lord of 4th joined to lord of Midheaven
judgment: First chain: attainment; second chain: attainment after losing hope.

rule: For any question about attaining a sought matter: when the lord of the Ascendant and lord of the 10th are conjoined and the Moon commits her strength to one of them with reception and freedom from malefics, attainment is expected. If the Moon commits to neither but is received, attainment is slower. If the Moon is neither received nor impeded, examine the receiver of the disposition: free from malefics and aspecting its own domicile = partial attainment; impeded = no attainment. When the lord of the Ascendant receives the Moon's disposition, the seeking of the matter is easier.
conditions: lord of Ascendant and lord of 10th conjoined
Moon commits to one with reception and no malefic impediment
Moon received but commits to neither
receiver free from malefics and aspects own domicile
lord of Ascendant receives Moon's disposition
judgment: Degrees of attainment from full to partial to none; reception of Moon's disposition by lord of Ascendant eases the quest.

rule: When the primary significator is received and the Moon is likewise received and occupying a favorable house, and either body applies to the house of the matter or to the significator's own domicile, the querent obtains at least a portion of what was sought.
conditions: aspect to house of matter or significator's domicile
judgment: Querent attains part of the sought matter

rule: When the significator lacks reception and the Moon is afflicted, the querent fails to obtain the sought matter.
judgment: Matter is not attained

rule: When Leo rises and the Ascendant lord cannot aspect the 10th-house lord (as when the angles occupy the same degree of Leo, making a Sun-Venus aspect impossible), one evaluates the Sun and Venus individually: if both are received and apply to the Midheaven, success is indicated; if only one is received, one then examines whether the Moon transfers disposition to the unreceived one; if neither is received and the Moon is afflicted, but the planet receiving the Moon's disposition aspects the Midheaven unimpeded, partial success obtains.
conditions: Sun and Venus cannot aspect each other
reception status of Sun and Venus
judgment: Degree of success varies from full to partial depending on reception and Moon's condition
notes: Footnote explains that Leo rising with corrected angles places the MC also in Leo, making Sun-Venus aspect geometrically impossible; this forces the use of alternate significators

rule: When a planet in an angle applies to the lights of two significators and does not leave its sign before the aspect completes, this collects their light and indicates success and attainment of the sought matter.
conditions: does not change sign before perfection
judgment: Matter is perfected; querent succeeds
notes: Footnote identifies this as collection of light

rule: If the Moon is received and applies to the Midheaven, or conjoins the Midheaven lord's body while also aspecting the Midheaven, the matter is perfected. Alternatively, if the domicile lord of the sign containing the Moon aspects her and both aspect the 10th, attainment follows.
conditions: Moon applies to Midheaven or conjoins MC lord bodily
both Moon and MC lord aspect 10th
judgment: Querent attains the sought matter

rule: If the Moon forms no aspect to any planet before leaving her current sign, the matter fails unless both the Ascendant lord and the matter's house lord possess strength and testimony in the relevant places and both aspect the house of the matter.
conditions: Moon makes no aspect before sign change
Ascendant lord and matter lord have strength and mutual aspect to matter's house
judgment: Matter fails absent the specified exception; with the exception, partial hope remains

rule: Affliction to the Moon or to the Midheaven lord reduces the quality of the outcome. If the planet receiving the Moon's disposition is also impeded, this indicates outright detriment to the matter.
conditions: Moon impeded OR MC lord impeded
judgment: Matter is diminished; if receiver also impeded, matter suffers detriment

rule: When the Midheaven lord transfers strength and disposition to a receiving planet that is strong in both its own and the matter's places, but that receiving planet does not aspect the Midheaven, the matter will not be perfected in the manner desired.
conditions: MC lord pushes disposition to receiver
judgment: Matter is not completed in the intended way

rule: When a significator occupies the 12th, 2nd, 6th, or 8th sign from its own domicile, it is in an antagonistic relationship to that domicile, indicating duress and complications in pursuing the matter. Placement in the 7th sign from its domicile (opposition) signifies direct contrariety.
conditions: significator in 12th, 2nd, 6th, or 8th from its own domicile
judgment: 12th/2nd/6th/8th: duress and complication; 7th: direct contrariety
notes: This extends the classical concept of aversion and detriment to include relative house positions from the planet's own domicile

rule: In questions about a ruler: the Ascendant and its lord signify the ruler's personal reputation (praise and blame); the 7th and its lord signify the actions of the populace; the 10th and its lord signify events within the kingdom (good or ill); the 11th and its lord signify those who succeed the ruler in office; the 9th and its lord signify predecessors; the 4th and its lord signify the end or outcome of the reign.
conditions: mundane or horary question about a king or ruler
judgment: Each house and its lord carry the specified signification

rule: The planet ruling the house of substance indicates how a ruler disburses collected wealth: Mars indicates expenditure on warfare, debauchery, and harmful acts; Saturn indicates mental disturbance and wasteful spending of one's own and others' resources; Jupiter indicates charitable and pious spending; the Sun indicates spending for parental honor and acquiring noble status; Venus indicates devotion to pleasures; Mercury indicates commercial activity and wealth-seeking; the Moon operates according to the planet she is joined to; if the Moon is void of course, resources are exhausted entirely.
judgment: Nature of spending matches the ruling planet's signification

rule: The Ascendant lord signifies the end of a ruler's reign (being the 4th from the 10th). If the Ascendant lord occupies the 12th, 6th, or 8th, the manner of deposition is disgraceful—most disgraceful in the 6th or 12th, bringing resentment and mistrust leading to revolt by the successor. Reception of the Ascendant lord mitigates the harm (no martyrdom or conquest); lack of reception combined with affliction makes the post-deposition condition worse than the deposition itself.
judgment: Disgraceful deposition; reception removes harm; lack of reception worsens post-deposition fate

rule: When the 12th-house lord joins the Ascendant lord without receiving it, the ruler is conquered. The angle in which this occurs modifies the manner: in the 10th, publicly before all; in the 1st, less dramatically; in the 4th, secretly yet with honor; in the 7th, handed over to the people with punishment. If the conjunction is in a cadent house on the right of the Ascendant, conquest occurs after being taken to a foreign land; on the left (below earth), conquest occurs on a journey.
conditions: angular or cadent placement of conjunction
judgment: Conquest or defeat; location modifies public/private nature of the event

rule: If after separating from the 12th-house lord the Ascendant lord next applies to the 8th-house lord, the ruler dies while imprisoned. If instead the Ascendant lord next applies to the Midheaven lord, the ruler attains a kingdom after imprisonment.
conditions: next applies to 8th lord OR next applies to MC lord
judgment: 8th lord next: death in captivity; MC lord next: kingdom after captivity

rule: When the Ascendant lord is impeded by Saturn, punishment comes through imprisonment and beating with wooden implements; when impeded by Mars, it comes through chains, iron instruments, and whipping.
conditions: Ascendant lord impeded by Saturn OR by Mars
judgment: Saturn: imprisonment and blows with wood; Mars: chains, iron, and whips

rule: If the Ascendant lord applies to the lord of its own descension (detriment), the ruler performs an action that leads to ruin. Conversely, if the lord of the Ascendant's descension applies to the Ascendant lord, lies are told about the ruler that persist throughout their life.
conditions: Ascendant lord applies to lord of its descension
OR lord of descension applies to Ascendant lord
judgment: Active direction: self-destructive action; passive direction: persistent slander

rule: If the Midheaven lord applies to the lord of its own descension, the ruler or commander destroys their own territory. If the lord of that descension applies to the Midheaven lord, the territory is destroyed by external forces.
conditions: MC lord applies to lord of its descension
OR lord of descension applies to MC lord
judgment: Active: ruler destroys own domain; passive: domain destroyed from outside

rule: When the Ascendant lord transfers its disposition to a planet in an angle, the ruler endures in power. Angles other than the 4th are preferable for this condition, because the 4th opposes and controverts the 10th.
conditions: Ascendant lord in applying aspect to angular planet
judgment: Ruler remains in power; receiver in 4th is less favorable

rule: If the Ascendant lord applies to a planet in the 9th or 3rd, the ruler's departure from power is certain. However, if that same Ascendant lord subsequently joins a planet in an angle, the ruler returns to power after departing. If the Midheaven lord is in its own domicile and the Moon applies to it, the ruler does not withdraw.
conditions: MC lord in own domicile and Moon applies to it
judgment: 9th/3rd: departure; later angular application: return; MC lord in own domicile with Moon applying: stability

rule: Jupiter placed in an angle with some essential dignity, or receiving the Moon or Ascendant lord, preserves the ruler in power until Jupiter encounters a malefic, enters combustion, or moves into the next sign.
conditions: Jupiter in angle with dignity OR receiving Moon or Ascendant lord
judgment: Ruler remains in power until Jupiter's condition deteriorates

rule: When the Ascendant lord and Midheaven lord are joined, and the receiving planet (the slower of the two) does not aspect the Midheaven, the ruler is established over a foreign or another's kingdom rather than their own. If the receiver does aspect the Midheaven, the ruler remains stable in their own kingdom.
conditions: Ascendant lord and MC lord joined
receiver aspects or does not aspect the Midheaven
judgment: No MC aspect: rule over a foreign kingdom; MC aspect: stable in own kingdom

rule: When both the Ascendant lord and the Moon occupy angles in movable signs and the Moon lacks reception, the king departs or is removed from power.
conditions: Ascendant lord in angle in movable sign
Moon in angle in movable sign
judgment: Ruler departs from kingdom

rule: The Moon applying to a peregrine planet in the 9th or 3rd, or to a lord of a foreign-travel house placed in such a house, indicates departure from the kingdom. If the peregrine planet is in the 4th in a movable sign, removal is more certain. If the Moon applies to the lord of the 4th and that lord is not in its own domicile, removal is indicated; if in its own domicile, the condition is improved. Moon applying to a planet in its own descension or in opposition to its domicile further confirms removal.
conditions: Moon applies to peregrine planet in 9th or 3rd
Moon applies to 4th lord not in domicile
Moon applies to planet in descension or opposition to domicile
judgment: Removal or departure from kingdom; domicile placement of 4th lord mitigates

rule: When the Moon is powerful in her position yet void of course, the kingdom is cut off or abruptly terminated.
judgment: Kingdom is severed or ended

rule: For a question about whether an absent ruler returns: if the Ascendant lord and Midheaven lord are joined and the receiving planet aspects the Midheaven, return is confirmed. If the receiver does not aspect the Midheaven but the Moon applies to a planet in the Midheaven, return is still indicated. A retrograde Ascendant lord also indicates return. Moon in a movable sign accelerates the return. Moon applying to the Ascendant lord, or the Ascendant lord applying to a planet in the Ascendant or Midheaven, likewise supports return.
conditions: Ascendant lord and MC lord joined
OR Moon applies to planet in MC
OR Moon applies to Ascendant lord
judgment: Absent ruler returns
notes: Footnote compares this to Abū Ma'shar's rendering of light

rule: When the Midheaven lord applies to the lord of its own descension (detriment), the ruler's absence or remoteness is indicated, even if the Midheaven lord occupies an angle. Similarly, the Ascendant lord applying to the lord of its own descension indicates remoteness.
conditions: MC lord applies to lord of its descension
OR Ascendant lord applies to lord of its descension
judgment: Ruler is remote or absent

rule: If the Midheaven lord is placed in its own domicile, an absent or remote ruler will return to the kingdom.
judgment: Absent ruler returns

rule: When the 4th-house lord applies to the Midheaven lord, the ruler perseveres in the current kingdom and additionally receives a second kingdom. When the 4th-house lord applies to the Ascendant lord, the ruler is not displaced and a kingdom comes to them unsought.
conditions: OR 4th lord applies to Ascendant lord
judgment: 4th to MC lord: existing kingdom plus additional kingdom; 4th to Ascendant lord: stability plus unsolicited kingdom

rule: Moon applying to a planet in the 9th indicates the ruler's withdrawal. If that planet is a benefic in a movable or fixed sign, return to the kingdom follows. In a common sign, the ruler goes to a different kingdom and rules for approximately three years until the Moon's receiver reaches the 12th; in the second year conditions improve unless a malefic transits and retrogrades in the Midheaven before that time. Moon applying to a planet in the 10th indicates no withdrawal and two years of rule; in the 11th, one year; in the 5th (with no retrograde malefic in the MC), two years with withdrawal in the third; in the 4th, one year with removal in the second.
conditions: Moon applies to planet in specified house
presence of retrograde malefic in Midheaven
judgment: Duration and nature of rulership varies by house and modality of receiver
notes: A profection-like timing technique is implied: the receiver's movement from the 9th to the 12th tracks the duration

rule: If the Moon and Midheaven lord are simultaneously afflicted by bodily conjunction in an angle, the ruler never returns to power. If they are afflicted in common signs, the ruler's position is elevated and they are powerful, and if they departed they return.
conditions: Moon and MC lord both impeded by conjunction in angle OR in common signs
judgment: Angle: permanent removal from position; common signs: elevation and return if departed

rule: For a question of whether someone will attain a kingdom: if the Ascendant lord and the Moon both apply to the Midheaven lord or the Sun, or occupy the Midheaven, the answer is affirmative; otherwise negative.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Moon apply to MC lord or Sun
judgment: Yes, a kingdom will be attained; otherwise no

rule: For a question about attaining a hoped-for matter (honors, royal grants): if the 11th-house lord applies to the Ascendant lord or vice versa, the matter is attained. Trine or sextile indicates ease; square or opposition indicates difficulty. If the 11th lord is angular and the Moon is received, the matter is perfected as desired.
conditions: 11th lord applies to Ascendant lord OR Ascendant lord applies to 11th lord
judgment: Matter attained; ease or difficulty depends on aspect type

rule: The modality of the sign containing the Moon's dispositee modifies the outcome of a hoped-for matter: common sign yields partial attainment; movable sign brings difficulty; fixed sign yields full and perfect attainment. If the receiver itself is afflicted, the matter is destroyed after initial attainment. If the receiver is itself received, the querent obtains more than hoped for. If the Ascendant lord is received, the querent obtains everything desired.
conditions: receiver of Moon's disposition in common, movable, or fixed sign
judgment: Modality determines completeness; reception amplifies; affliction destroys after initial success

rule: For a question of whether the querent will be reunited with a friend: if the Ascendant lord and Moon apply to the 11th-house lord, or the 11th lord applies to the Ascendant lord, reunion occurs. Trine or sextile indicates the reunion is joyful and harmonious; square or opposition indicates conflict and discord in the reunion, with opposition producing the stronger conflict.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Moon apply to 11th lord OR 11th lord applies to Ascendant lord
judgment: Reunion occurs; nature of reunion depends on aspect type

rule: For a generic question about an unspecified hoped-for matter: if the Ascendant lord and Moon apply to benefics from angles or succeedents, attainment is promised; if no such application exists, the answer is negative. Once the querent names the matter specifically, the relevant house and its significators should be consulted.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Moon apply to benefics in angles or succeedents
judgment: Unspecified matter attained if application present; if querent names matter, consult appropriate house

rule: For a question about which beast wins a race: the placement of the lord of the hour indicates finishing position. In the Ascendant: first place. In the Midheaven or 11th: second. In the 7th: middle of the field. In the 4th: last place.
conditions: lord of hour in Ascendant, Midheaven, 11th, 7th, or 4th
judgment: Finishing position corresponds to angular placement

rule: If the lord of the hour is in its own descension, the rider is thrown and falls from the beast. If a malefic also aspects the lord of the hour, a body part corresponding to the sign involved is injured. If a malefic opposes or conjoins the lord of the hour and the Ascendant lord is in the 8th from the Ascendant, the rider dies from the fall, especially if the 8th-house lord or Moon is also afflicted.
conditions: lord of hour in own descension
malefic aspect to lord of hour
judgment: Fall: rider thrown; with malefic aspect: body part injured; with Ascendant lord in 8th: rider dies

rule: When someone without a beast in a race asks which beast will win: a planet in the Ascendant, Midheaven, or 11th signifies the winning beast's color by the color of that planet. The beast's lineage is indicated by the planet's essential dignity: domicile or exaltation indicates noble and well-known stock; triplicity indicates obscure origin; bound or face indicates local recognition without distinguished lineage; descension indicates malign temperament and poor stock.
judgment: Color of planet = color of winning beast's designation; dignity level = quality of beast's stock

rule: The age of the winning beast is indicated by the significator's solar orientation: oriental position indicates a young beast (two teeth); occidental indicates full maturity; intermediate position indicates middle age (four teeth).
judgment: Oriental: young; intermediate: middle-aged; occidental: fully mature
notes: Applies to animals whose age can be tracked by dentition

rule: The rising sign's domicile ruler indicates the social class of the beast's owner: Sun's domicile = royal beast; Saturn's domicile = old, possibly low-bred beast; Jupiter's domicile = beast belonging to a high official near the ruler; Mars's domicile = beast of a military commander; Venus's or Mercury's domicile = beast of a noble, the ruler, a woman, or a writer; Moon's domicile = beast belonging to a merchant being offered for sale.
conditions: Ascendant sign identified by planetary domicile ruler
judgment: Domicile ruler indicates type and social status of owner

rule: For a question about enemies in general, use the 12th house and its lord. If a specific individual enemy is named, use the 7th house and its lord. Evaluate their condition through applying and separating aspects in the usual manner.
judgment: House and lord assignment determines the enemy significator

rule: When a matter cannot be assigned to any of the twelve houses, use the intrinsic nature of the planets themselves as the basis for judgment, since planetary significations exceed what the twelve houses can categorize.
conditions: matter has no clear house assignment
judgment: Fall back to planetary natures for judgment

rule: For a question about a letter or messenger: the sender is signified by the Ascendant and the planet from whom the Moon is separating; the recipient is signified by the 7th and its lord. The hopes, fears, and conditions of each party are read from their respective significator's placement and aspects from benefics and malefics.
conditions: Ascendant and Moon's separation planet = sender
judgment: Each party's condition, status, and intent is read from their significator

rule: Whichever significator (sender or recipient) occupies an angle or a place of reception and aspects its own sign is of higher standing than the other. The dignity level of the planet from whom the Moon separates indicates the sender's social rank: exaltation = royalty; domicile in angle = honored household member with dignity; cadent from angles = has lost a former kingdom or office; descension in angle = of low birth but honored at court; descension and cadent = unknown and low-born; no aspect to Ascendant or own domicile lord = without resources.
conditions: aspect to Ascendant or own domicile lord
judgment: Rank and social standing of letter writer determined by dignity and angularity

rule: The planet from whom the Moon separates indicates the character of the letter's sender: Saturn = person with some defect or vice; Jupiter = noble; Mars = warrior dealing in blood and weapons; Sun = king; Venus = woman; Mercury = writer or merchant.
judgment: Sender's character and profession identified by separating planet's nature

rule: The planet to whom the Moon is applying indicates the type of person to whom the letter is directed: Saturn = an old man; Jupiter = a noble; Venus = a woman; and so on according to each planet's nature.
judgment: Recipient's nature identified by applying planet

rule: The planet from whom Mercury separates indicates what the letter contains: separation from benefics = good content; separation from malefics = harmful or negative content. Mercury governs all writing; the Moon governs rumors.
conditions: Mercury separating from benefic or malefic
judgment: Benefic separation = good letter content; malefic separation = bad content

rule: The stronger of Mercury or the planet from whom Mercury is separating, taken as the significator, indicates the topic of the letter by its house placement: 1st = health and profit; 2nd = financial matters; 3rd = a sibling, friend, or journey; 4th = land, older relative, or ancient matter; 5th = hoped-for things or children; 6th = a slave or an ill person; 7th = a woman; 8th = death or inheritance; 9th = spiritual admonition, travel, or news of the king; 10th = the king or nobles; 11th = a friend with pleasing news; 12th = dispute or enemy.
conditions: stronger of Mercury or its separation planet identified
judgment: House placement indicates the letter's subject

rule: The first conjunction of Mercury (already examined for the original letter's content) signifies what arises from the original letter; the second conjunction of Mercury after that signifies the content of the response letter.
conditions: Mercury's second applying conjunction after the first
judgment: Second conjunction indicates the response letter's nature

rule: A letter is completed if the Moon is applying to Mercury. If the Moon has already passed Mercury by up to 2-3 degrees, it is still completed; beyond that separation, not.
conditions: Moon applying to Mercury OR recently separated by 2-3 degrees
judgment: Letter is completed if application or recent separation within 2-3 degrees

rule: A letter is sealed if the Moon applies to Mercury. If the Moon has separated from Mercury by approximately 2 degrees but has not transited beyond the bound, it is already sealed. If Mercury is with the Sun and both aspect the Ascendant, it is sealed.
conditions: OR Moon separated from Mercury by ~2 degrees within same bound
OR Mercury conjunct Sun both aspecting Ascendant
judgment: Letter is sealed

rule: A letter originates from a king or prince if Mercury is recently separated from the Sun or from the Midheaven lord by a small separation.
conditions: Mercury recently separated from Sun or MC lord by small arc
judgment: Letter originated with the king or ruling authority

rule: A letter will reach the king if Mercury is applying to the Sun or to the Midheaven lord.
conditions: Mercury applying to Sun or MC lord
judgment: Letter reaches the king

rule: Rumors are true when the stronger of the Ascendant lord or Moon is angular and free from malefics and does not apply to a cadent planet. If the angular significator applies to a cadent unreceipted planet, the rumors were mentioned but will not be fulfilled. If the Ascendant lord is not angular but applies to an angular benefic, the rumors are true and will appear; to an angular malefic without reception, the rumors are false. Applying to a cadent planet renders rumors false unless that planet receives the significator.
conditions: Ascendant lord or Moon in angle, free from malefics
application target: cadent, angular benefic, angular malefic, cadent with/without reception
judgment: Truth or falsity of rumors varies by placement and reception

rule: Rumors are false when: (a) the Ascendant lord is in a movable sign or the Ascendant itself is movable and malefics aspect it; (b) the Moon is void of course; (c) the Moon applies to a retrograde planet even if it receives her; (d) the Moon applies to a cadent planet, especially a malefic—lying is indicated even with reception; (e) the Moon is in an angle, afflicted, and the malefic does not receive her.
conditions: movable Ascendant or Ascendant lord in movable sign with malefic aspect
Moon in angle afflicted without reception
judgment: Rumors are lies or will not materialize

rule: If the Moon applies to an angular planet that receives her, this alone confirms the rumors are true without need for further testimony. If the receiver is additionally free from malefics and retrogradation, the rumors are perfected and improve further. If the receiver is a benefic in the Midheaven or Ascendant, the truth of the rumors is strongest. Affliction of the receiver by an unreceipting or retrograde planet signals destruction of the rumors after the retrograde planet turns direct.
conditions: Moon applies to angular received planet
receiver free from malefics and retrogradation
receiver a benefic in Midheaven or Ascendant
OR receiver afflicted by non-receiving or retrograde planet
judgment: Received angular application: rumors true; afflicted receiver: rumors destroyed after direct station

rule: When the Moon transfers her disposition to a planet in an angle, the rumors are true. In the Midheaven: already publicly known. In the Ascendant: beginning to emerge. In the 7th: already public and visible. In the 4th: secret.
conditions: Moon pushes disposition to planet in specific angle
judgment: MC: publicly known; Ascendant: emerging; 7th: fully visible; 4th: secret

rule: For a question about a feared matter: if the Ascendant lord is angular and free from malefics, the fear is groundless. If the Ascendant lord is in the 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th, the feared matter has already begun. If malefics also testify (aspect), the querent falls into the feared outcome; without malefic testimony, the fear subsides. Malefics in angles aspecting from angles worsen the condition.
conditions: Ascendant lord in angle or in adverse houses
judgment: Angular free: unfounded fear; adverse house: fear has entered; malefic testimony: outcome materializes

rule: When the malefic afflicting the Ascendant lord is also the 8th-house lord, death or destruction is indicated. If it is the 12th-house lord, punishment and imprisonment are feared. If it is the 2nd-house lord, the querent is captured or held for ransom.
judgment: 8th lord: death; 12th lord: imprisonment/punishment; 2nd lord: capture for money

rule: If the Ascendant lord is in the 12th and neither the 7th-house lord nor the 12th-house lord aspects it, the querent escapes and is freed. If the Moon additionally applies to a malefic, the malefic exposes the querent unless the malefic is lord of the Moon's domicile—in that case labor in flight is indicated rather than exposure; if not the domicile lord, exposure occurs.
conditions: 7th and 12th lords do not aspect it
malefic is or is not Moon's domicile lord
judgment: No aspect from enemies' lords: escape; Moon-malefic application with domicile lordship: difficult flight; without domicile lordship: querent exposed

rule: For a question about whether a killed or injured person will be avenged: if the Ascendant and 4th are in movable signs and the Moon is in a movable sign, no action is possible. If the Ascendant lord aspects the Ascendant and the Moon's domicile lord aspects the Moon, the matter is swiftly accomplished. If additionally the 4th-house lord aspects the 7th, the querent achieves vengeance. If the Moon applies to benefics and those benefics are not subsequently joined to malefics, peace holds; if the benefic joins a malefic, the querent is killed—unless the benefic-malefic aspect is a trine or sextile, in which case the querent suffers but survives.
conditions: Ascendant and 4th in movable signs and Moon in movable sign
Moon's benefic applies then joins malefic
judgment: Movable signs: no action; aspects fulfilled: swift vengeance; benefic then malefic conjunction: death of querent; trine/sextile: suffering without death

rule: If the malefic is in a fixed sign, the offender dies in prison. If in a movable sign and the sign's domicile lord is swift and aspects the malefic, the offender is released quickly.
conditions: malefic in fixed or movable sign
domicile lord of malefic's sign swift and aspecting
judgment: Fixed: death in prison; movable with swift aspecting domicile lord: quick release

rule: When the planet to whom the Moon applies is in a movable sign and aspects its own domicile lord by a harmonious aspect, the subject escapes freely. A square or opposition aspect indicates escape through battle or conflict. A bodily conjunction in the same sign indicates rapid release or flight.
conditions: Moon's conjunction planet in movable sign
aspect to its domicile lord: friendly, square, opposition, or conjunction
judgment: Friendly aspect: free escape; square/opposition: escape through battle; same-sign conjunction: swift release or flight

rule: A benefic in the Ascendant at the time of the question indicates the matter will be settled through hired agents or allies. If the Moon additionally applies to a strong malefic in its own place, royal intervention replaces private agents. A malefic in the Ascendant with the Moon made fortunate indicates the killer's allies and the king jointly hinder the querent. If the Ascendant lord aspects the Ascendant, allies achieve the result despite royal opposition; if the Ascendant lord does not aspect the Ascendant but the Moon's domicile lord aspects the Moon, the king acts without the allies' consent.
conditions: Moon applies to strong malefic in own place
malefic in Ascendant with Moon fortunate
Ascendant lord aspects or does not aspect Ascendant
judgment: Benefic: private agents; Moon to malefic: king acts; malefic in Ascendant: opposition from king and allies; Ascendant lord aspecting Ascendant: allies prevail; domicile lord of Moon aspecting Moon: king acts alone

rule: Mars signifies punishment involving iron implements and whipping; Saturn signifies punishment involving wooden implements, prolonged imprisonment, and distress.
judgment: Mars: iron and whipping; Saturn: wood, extended imprisonment, suffering

rule: For a question of whether something is genuine or counterfeit: if the Ascendant lord and Moon are free from malefics, the item is genuine and valuable; if impeded, it is fake. For gold specifically, the Sun serves as an additional witness; for silver, the Moon.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Moon free from malefics
judgment: Free: genuine; impeded: fake; Sun for gold, Moon for silver

rule: For questions comparing multiple options (which item is best, which rumor is true, which person succeeds): the Ascendant lord's house placement determines which named option prevails. Angular and free from malefics with reception: first option is best and attained; angular but impeded: first option is attained then lost. In a succeedent with Ascendant lord aspecting the Ascendant, free and received: second option prevails; if impeded: second option succeeds then fails. Cadent, free, and received: third option prevails; cadent and impeded: all three fail. Apply the same analysis to the Moon.
conditions: Ascendant lord in angle, succeedent, or cadent
judgment: Position in angles/succeedents/cadents selects which numbered option succeeds
notes: Footnote notes the implicit rule that the Ascendant lord must aspect the Ascendant to select succeedent and cadent options; all angles already aspect the Ascendant

rule: When a querent asks about several unrelated matters simultaneously, the Moon serves as the general significator and the planets as the individual matters. The sequence of the Moon's upcoming conjunctions corresponds to the sequence in which the querent named each matter; the first conjunction answers the first matter, the second answers the second, and so on.
conditions: Moon's sequential conjunctions mapped to each matter in order named
judgment: Each successive lunar conjunction provides the answer for the correspondingly numbered matter

rule: For a hunt question: evaluate the relationship between the Ascendant sign's nature (quadruped, etc.) and the 7th sign and the placement of the 7th lord relative to the Ascendant lord. A trine or sextile between them indicates easy capture of the prey; square or opposition indicates capture with effort; no applying aspect indicates the hunt fails entirely.
conditions: 7th sign nature and its lord's aspect to Ascendant lord
judgment: Trine/sextile: easy catch; square/opposition: catch with labor; no aspect: no catch

rule: If the 7th sign is a quadruped sign and its lord or the lord of the hour is in it or in an angle made fortunate, the hunt succeeds. During the hour of Jupiter or when Jupiter is in an angle, the prey consists of deer or roebuck.
conditions: lord of 7th or lord of hour in 7th or angle, made fortunate
Jupiter in angle or hour of Jupiter
judgment: Hunt succeeds; Jupiter indicates deer/roebuck specifically

rule: If Mars is the 7th-house lord and has strength there, the hunter catches prey, but a companion interferes causing the prey to escape. Cadent benefics in this context fail to prevent the interference. If Jupiter aspects Mars and Jupiter is lord of the hour or Ascendant, the hunter is protected from all feared outcomes and hunts easily.
conditions: Jupiter aspects Mars and is lord of hour or Ascendant
judgment: Mars 7th lord: catch with interference; Jupiter aspecting Mars: easy hunt without impediment

rule: If the 7th is an airy or earthy sign with a benefic in it but a malefic as the lord of the sign or lord of the hour, prey is frightened and flees; the hunter labors without full success unless Jupiter or Mercury accompanies the malefic lord of the hour, which reduces but does not eliminate the harm. Mercury has notable partnership with Mars in hunting matters.
conditions: malefic as 7th sign lord or lord of hour
Jupiter or Mercury with malefic lord of hour
judgment: Prey flees; partial hunt with labor; Jupiter or Mercury with malefic mitigates impediment

rule: For quantity of catch: Mars in the Midheaven or as its lord, aspected by Mercury or Jupiter (or one of them, with the other or the Ascendant lord as lord of the hour), yields a large catch with no labor. Saturn aspecting Mars from an angle, being in the Midheaven, or being MC lord overrides this and brings sorrow and diminished catch. If Jupiter is additionally cadent from Mars and Saturn is in that configuration, the hunter finds bodily impediment and travel delays, and the hunt fails entirely, since Saturn destroys hunts on land.
conditions: Saturn aspecting from angle or in MC
judgment: Mars-Mercury/Jupiter: abundant catch; Saturn involvement: sorrow and failure; Saturn on land hunt: total destruction

rule: For a sea or water hunt with a watery Ascendant: if the Moon applies to Mars, or the lord of the hour applies to Mars, and Venus is cadent from the Moon's aspect, the hunt has no strength or usefulness (only impediment). If the Moon applies to Saturn and Venus aspects the Moon, the catch is multiplied. Saturn does not impede a water hunt unless Mars also aspects the Moon. If Mars aspects Venus (enmity), Venus is weakened; if Saturn aspects the Moon as well, shipwreck and hazards from water are feared.
conditions: Moon applies to Mars OR lord of hour to Mars with Venus cadent
Moon applies to Saturn with Venus aspecting Moon
Mars aspects Venus with Saturn also aspecting Moon
judgment: Moon-Mars with Venus cadent: poor hunt; Moon-Saturn with Venus aspecting: abundant catch; Mars on Moon with Saturn: shipwreck risk

rule: The Ascendant's modality indicates the number of food courses at a banquet: movable sign = many appetizers; fixed sign = one course; common sign = two courses.
conditions: Ascendant in movable, fixed, or common sign
judgment: Movable: many courses; fixed: one; common: two

rule: The planet occupying the Ascendant indicates the flavor character of the meal: Moon = salty; Mars = bitter; Jupiter = sweet; Sun = sharp/pungent (like peppery herbs); Venus = light or delicate in taste, rich or fatty; Mercury = acidic or mixed; Saturn = harsh and unpleasant.
judgment: Each planet indicates the dominant flavor quality of the food
notes: Footnote notes Bonatti attributes the pungent-sharp description to the Sun rather than to Venus; this extraction follows that correction

rule: If the Moon separates from a malefic and applies to a benefic by square or opposition, the banquet is held on a social occasion (wedding, circumcision, or similar celebration). If the application is by trine or sextile, it is a conference, reconciliation, or similar gathering. If the planet to whom the Moon applies is in an angle, the banquet lasts one day; in a common sign, more than one day.
conditions: applying to benefic by square/opposition or trine/sextile
receiver in angle or common sign
judgment: Square/opposition: festive occasion; trine/sextile: conference or reconciliation; angle: one day; common sign: multiple days

rule: The planet to whom the Moon applies at the time of a banquet question characterizes the banquet: Jupiter = noble banquet with many dishes; Sun = clean, beautiful dishes or abundance of sharp foods; Venus = beautiful foods, much sweetness, entertainment, laughter, fragrance; Mercury = performances, wise discourse, many dishes, stories, and bird meats; Saturn = unclean foods, many fish dishes; Mars = quarrels among guests, all hot dishes; if Mars is in the Midheaven, quarrels are certain.
judgment: Each planet characterizes the type and atmosphere of the banquet

rule: If the Moon is with Mars in one sign or applies to Mars from an angle, avoid the banquet because conflict will follow. If the Moon is with Saturn, the food will be unclean and unpleasant. If with Venus or Mercury, attend because the experience will be pleasing; likewise if with Jupiter, which also indicates abundance of grain dishes.
conditions: Moon with Mars or applying to Mars from angle
OR Moon with Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter
judgment: Moon-Mars or Moon-Saturn: avoid banquet; Moon-Venus/Mercury/Jupiter: attend

rule: If the lord of the hour is in the Ascendant or Midheaven at the time of seating, food is served at the beginning. If removed from those two places, food is delayed until the planet moves away from them. If in the 7th or 4th, food is not served until the venue is full.
conditions: lord of hour in Ascendant or Midheaven
judgment: Early service, delayed service, or service dependent on filling the venue

rule: The Moon's sign at a banquet indicates specific foods: watery sign with Saturn in trine or sextile = trout; Libra = grains or legumes; Gemini or Aquarius = bird meats; Saturn in square or opposition to Moon = cold meat; Sun joined to Mars = all food is burnt; Moon in Libra or its square aspect = avoid cooked or raw vegetables; Moon in Virgo or Libra = avoid grains; Moon in Scorpio with South Node = avoid lard; Moon in Leo = avoid meat; Moon in Sagittarius = avoid wild animal meats; Moon in Pisces = avoid all fish.
judgment: Each condition specifies likely food type or dietary warning
notes: Final dietary warnings apply only when the Moon is in those signs in a square or opposition to a malefic per footnote

rule: The Ascendant's domicile ruler indicates the reason for the banquet: Venus's domicile = wedding or nuptials; Mercury's domicile = celebration for a child or children; Jupiter's domicile = a friend is hosting the event.
conditions: Ascendant ruled by Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter
judgment: Domicile ruler identifies the occasion

rule: The 2nd sign from the Ascendant signifies the drinking vessels and furnishings. Common sign in the 2nd = colored vessels. Mars in the 2nd = copper in the vessel; Venus = silver; Jupiter = silver and gold; Moon = glass; Saturn = wood or earthenware. Benefic in the 2nd indicates beautiful decoration; if the benefic is peregrine, decoration belongs to another household; if it has dignity, it belongs to the household.
judgment: Each condition specifies material or nature of vessels and decor

rule: In a banquet question, the houses from the Ascendant each govern an aspect of the event: 3rd = guests present; 4th = venue location (common sign: portico; Sun or Jupiter: interior or southern room); 5th = beverages (common sign: diverse; Jupiter or Mercury: date beverages; Mars: acidic drinks; Mars impeded by Saturn: vinegary; Sun: bitter and acidic; Venus: date fermentation; Moon: water); 6th = servers; 7th = butlers; 8th = bakers and cooks; 9th = those who bring the dishes; 10th = quality of food and whether host enjoys the guests (benefics: enjoyment; malefics: hatred); 11th = brothers and friends; 12th = hidden disposition of the host.
conditions: planets or sign modality in each house
judgment: Each house governs the specified role or element of the banquet

rule: In a banquet chart, any house containing a benefic whose lord is also fortunate indicates good and joy for those signified by that house. Any house containing a malefic, or whose lord is afflicted, indicates destruction of everything pertaining to that house's banquet signification.
conditions: benefic or malefic in specific house
lord of that house fortunate or impeded
judgment: Benefic with fortunate lord: good; malefic or afflicted lord: destruction

rule: The planetary hour in which a querent arrives indicates the probable subject matter of the consultation, divided by thirds of the hour. Sun hour: first third = king, master, or great threat; middle = grave fear or illness; final third = livelihood or commerce. Venus hour: first = taking a wife or women's matters; middle = women's clothing or adornment; final = a friendship that cannot be realized. Mercury hour: first = legal matter, personal fortune, or something engraved; middle = suitable clothing or the querent's own soul; final = loss. Moon hour: first = travel, illness, or a blemished matter; middle = a matter out of hand, a returning traveler, a dying person, or a beast; final = completion of something or an agricultural matter. Saturn hour: first = a fleeing slave; middle = a powerful partnership, travel, or petition; final = an evil cause from which the querent has escaped. Jupiter hour: first = a public or named matter; middle = a garment to be fitted or an ill person recovering; final = a person who earned money and is now losing it. Mars hour: first = stolen red, gold, or copper goods or a garment; middle = an injured or heat-afflicted ill person; final = a deception or matter worked in fire.
conditions: third of the hour in which querent arrives
judgment: Probable topic of consultation identified by hour and third
notes: This section is absent from one manuscript (BN) and the Latin style differs; its attribution to Sahl is uncertain. Captured as a technique nonetheless.

rule: For a question about the relationship between a ruler and the one who appointed him: if the 7th-house lord receives the Ascendant lord or pushes its own strength to it by trine or sextile (or square), their affairs are joined in the best way. If the Moon translates light between them and commits disposition to the receiver from a place of dignity, she serves as a mediator. If the two significators are not joined and no planet translates light, the relationship is not as either party desires. Malefics operate craftily from square and opposition; benefics operate from square and opposition as well.
conditions: 7th lord receives Ascendant lord or applies by trine/sextile/square
Moon translates light with dignified commitment
judgment: Joined with reception or easy aspect: harmonious relationship; Moon translating: mediated concord; no application: relationship falls short of expectations

rule: To determine what land a ruler originates from, examine a planet in the Midheaven: if in its own domicile, the ruler is from the middle class of that land; if in exaltation, from the nobility; if in triplicity, from a lower station. If the planet has no dignity in that sign, the ruler is a foreigner. Solar orientation further specifies direction of origin: eastern of the Sun = from the east; western of the Sun = from the west; in the 4th from the Sun = from the north; in the 10th from the Sun = from the south. A peregrine planet not aspecting its own domicile or exaltation indicates base origin. If no planet is in the Midheaven, apply the same rules to the Midheaven lord.
conditions: no planet in Midheaven: use MC lord
judgment: Dignity level and solar orientation specify geographic origin and social class of ruler
notes: Footnote notes this is a version of the Hellenistic east/west solar orientation doctrine described by Schmidt

rule: For the chart of a ruler's formal entrance into power (electional or event chart): if the entrance is by day and the Sun is with Saturn, the ruler is deposed quickly. If benefics aspect the Sun and the Ascendant lord and the Sun are in a favorable house in a fixed sign, the reign is prolonged. If malefics aspect the Sun and Mars overrides from the Midheaven and the Sun is in the Ascendant in a movable sign, citizens revolt or the end comes through death and killing. Jupiter in the Midheaven made fortunate with the Sun in a strong place indicates increase, fame, and wealth accumulation. If the Sun is in the 8th or 6th but the Ascendant lord is in the Ascendant or Midheaven and is a benefic, the prince's own affairs are excellent but this signifies the death of the one who appointed him.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Sun in good house in fixed sign
Sun in Ascendant in movable sign
Sun in 8th or 6th with benefic Ascendant lord angular
judgment: Multiple specific outcomes based on combination of conditions

rule: For a night entrance into power, use the Moon instead of the Sun. Moon free from malefics and in a good place = bodily health of the ruler. Moon with or applying to malefics = rapid deposition with great justified complaint. Moon within 4 degrees of the Nodes = no profit in that office; beyond 4 degrees, impediment is reduced until the Moon moves 12 degrees from liberation.
conditions: Moon with or applying to malefics
judgment: Free Moon: healthy ruler; malefic Moon: quick deposition; within 4 degrees of Nodes: no profit

rule: In an entrance chart, examine the Ascendant, Moon, and their domicile lords with benefic and malefic aspects: if benefics aspect them and their lords are in good places, and malefics are cadent while benefics are in the Midheaven, the ruler sees favorable outcomes. If the Moon and her domicile lord are in bad places, the ruler finds evil in that domain.
conditions: benefics aspect Ascendant and Moon and their lords
OR Moon and Moon's lord in bad houses
judgment: Benefics favorable and angular: prince sees what he loves; Moon and lord in bad places: evil in the region

rule: In an entrance chart, the bound (term) containing the Ascendant degree modifies the ruler's career: if the degree falls in a malefic's bound and the malefic aspects that bound, the ruler is weak in the position and faces severe accusations. If it falls in a benefic's bound and the benefic aspects it, the office is well completed and the ruler departs with honor, praise, and wealth.
conditions: Ascendant degree in malefic bound aspected by that malefic
OR in benefic bound aspected by that benefic
judgment: Malefic bound with aspect: weakness and accusation; benefic bound with aspect: honorable and wealthy completion of office

rule: In an entrance chart: malefic in the Ascendant = difficulty and possible death in office; benefic in Ascendant with malefic in 4th = praiseworthy beginning but bad end; malefic in Ascendant with benefic in 4th = bad beginning but good end. South Node in the Ascendant with Ascendant lord in a bad place and a malefic in any angle and Moon afflicted = ignoble subordinates who undermine the ruler, causing perpetual sadness and fear.
conditions: benefic in Ascendant with malefic in 4th
malefic in Ascendant with benefic in 4th
South Node in Ascendant with Ascendant lord in bad place, malefic in angle, Moon afflicted
judgment: Each configuration specifies the quality of the beginning and end of the reign, or quality of subordinates

rule: Benefic in the Ascendant, or Ascendant lord in the Midheaven with the Midheaven lord strong and free from malefics = good condition of the prince and prolonged tenure. Malefic in the Ascendant with both a malefic Ascendant lord and the Midheaven lord in a bad place = quicker deposition. Both Ascendant lord and Midheaven lord in the 12th or 6th = hastened deposition unless Jupiter is oriental in the Ascendant or Midheaven, which slows the deposition somewhat.
conditions: benefic in Ascendant OR Ascendant lord in MC with MC lord free from malefics
malefic in Ascendant with malefic Ascendant lord and MC lord in bad place
Jupiter oriental in Ascendant or Midheaven
judgment: First: good and prolonged; second: quick deposition; third: hastened fall; Jupiter mitigates third case

rule: In an entrance chart, the Midheaven lord in an angle with benefics aspecting indicates good conditions. A benefic in the Midheaven brings elevation, worthy advancement, strong rule, and multiplied wealth. Malefics in the Midheaven bring great difficulties and loss of earnings through imprisonment, binding, and angry royal deposition. A benefic aspecting the Midheaven without a malefic there = advantage and good; malefic aspecting = destroys the work. Both benefic and malefic aspecting the Midheaven = the one with more degrees overcomes, but the other takes a share.
conditions: MC lord in angle with benefics aspecting
both benefic and malefic aspecting MC
judgment: Varies from elevation and wealth to destruction; stronger by degree wins when both aspect

rule: Mercury and Jupiter together in the Midheaven (especially if one aspects the Moon): wisdom, counsel, and renown; reputation and lasting work in the domain of rule. Sun additionally with them in the Midheaven without malefic aspect: prolonged fame, full attainment of goals, and long life in office. Jupiter with Moon in the Midheaven and Venus in a favorable place: similar excellent results. A benefic in the Midheaven generally decreases difficulty.
conditions: Sun also in Midheaven without malefic aspect
Jupiter and Moon in Midheaven with Venus in good place
judgment: Wisdom and fame; full attainment of goals; long tenure

rule: In an entrance chart, Mars in the 7th without a benefic in the Ascendant indicates the ruler dies in office. Saturn in the 7th with a benefic in the Ascendant or 7th: no death or killing in office. A benefic in the 7th alone = honorable and healthy deposition.
conditions: Mars in 7th, no benefic in Ascendant
Saturn in 7th with benefic in Ascendant or 7th
judgment: Mars without benefic in Ascendant: death in office; Saturn with benefic: survives; benefic in 7th: honorable departure

rule: In an entrance chart: benefic in the 4th = physical health and end according to the ruler's wishes; malefic in the 4th = evil after deposition including prison and prolonged captivity; benefic aspecting the 4th malefic = eventual escape after tribulations; no benefic aspecting the 4th malefic = conquest and death in prison. If the 4th lord is in the Ascendant or 10th or another favorable house, free from malefics, and the Moon's domicile lord is similarly placed, the end of the reign is good.
conditions: benefic aspects or does not aspect 4th malefic
4th lord in Ascendant or 10th free from malefics
Moon's domicile lord in good place
judgment: Benefic in 4th: good end; malefic in 4th: imprisonment and possible death; aspected by benefic: escape; no benefic: death in prison; 4th lord and Moon's lord well-placed: good end

rule: For a question about whether a king remains in power or withdraws: if the Ascendant lord and Midheaven lord are joined and the heavier of them (the receiver of disposition) is in an angle, the king does not move. If the receiver is in the 3rd or below the horizon (left of Ascendant), the king departs. If the receiver is also received, return is swift and honorable.
conditions: Ascendant lord and MC lord joined
receiver of disposition in angle OR below horizon
judgment: Receiver in angle: stability; receiver below horizon: departure; received: swift honorable return

rule: If the Ascendant lord and Midheaven lord have already separated from each other, this indicates the king has already begun to move away from his kingdom.
conditions: Ascendant lord and MC lord separating
judgment: King is departing or has already departed

rule: If the Moon transfers her disposition to a slower planet in an angle, the king remains in his kingdom until that planet enters combustion, is otherwise afflicted in its place, or moves into the next sign—at which point the loss of the kingdom is indicated.
conditions: Moon applies to slower planet in angle
slower planet then becomes combust, afflicted, or changes sign
judgment: King remains until planet's condition deteriorates; deterioration signals end of reign

rule: The Moon functions as the primary significator for all matters in a chart. Her condition—whether strong or afflicted—reflects the condition of whatever matter is under examination. She transmits the quality of her own state to the planet she is applying to join, and that planet becomes the receiver of her disposition.
judgment: The Moon's strength or debility indicates the soundness or damage of any matter; the receiving planet takes on and carries forward the disposition she commits to it.
notes: The Moon is described as analogous to human growth from small to mature; the receiver of disposition accepts what she has committed and is named for that role.

rule: Malefic planets produce harmful outcomes because their natures are characterized by an excess or overflow of cold or heat, which disrupts balance. Benefic planets, being of a temperate and balanced complexion, naturally incline toward good outcomes regardless of reception, though reception improves their effects.
judgment: Malefics incline to harm; benefics incline to benefit; reception strengthens benefic effects but is not required for benefit.
notes: Reception is noted as more useful for benefics but not strictly necessary.

rule: A malefic's harmful quality is reduced when a benefic occupies the malefic's own domicile or exaltation, because the malefic receives the benefic and withholds its destructive nature toward it. Similarly, if a malefic aspects another planet by trine or sextile, its harm is restrained because these are aspects of amity rather than enmity.
conditions: benefic in malefic's domicile or exaltation
malefic aspecting by trine or sextile
judgment: Malefic restrains its harm when receiving a planet in its dignities, or when its aspect to another planet is trine or sextile.

rule: When a malefic aspects a benefic by square or opposition, the benefic's positive signification is diminished. When a benefic aspects a malefic, the malefic's harmful signification is reduced.
conditions: malefic aspecting benefic by square or opposition
judgment: Square/opposition from malefic reduces benefic fortune; benefic aspect to malefic reduces malefic harm.

rule: A planet is considered impeded when a malefic casts its rays over that planet's degree within the malefic's orb. If a planet is in the bound of a malefic without the malefic's ray reaching it by orb, it is said to 'regard' the malefic but is not fully impeded.
conditions: malefic ray within orb of the subject planet
planet in malefic's bound without full ray contact
judgment: Ray within orb produces full impediment; bound-only contact produces a weakened, partial condition.
notes: Orb limits are referenced but not specified numerically in this passage.

rule: If a malefic has moved past a planet by a complete degree, it can no longer impede that planet but still produces a condition of fear or anxiety. Likewise, if a benefic has similarly moved past a planet by a full degree, hope remains but the matter is not brought to completion.
conditions: malefic separated from planet by one full degree
benefic separated from planet by one full degree
judgment: Malefic: fear without active harm. Benefic: hope without perfection.
notes: Integer degree rule: the degree itself is counted as whole, so separation begins when the faster planet enters the next degree.

rule: A malefic that is cadent from the Ascendant produces fear but cannot fully impede. Similarly, a benefic that is cadent from the Ascendant raises hope but cannot perfect the matter.
judgment: Cadent malefic: fear only, no active obstruction. Cadent benefic: hope only, no completion.

rule: When a planet is in conjunction with a malefic, or in the fourth, seventh, or tenth sign from it, it is positioned to resist the evil descending upon it—like someone defending themselves against adversity. Once the malefic has moved a full degree past this planet, the malefic can do nothing further than cause fear.
conditions: planet in 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th from a malefic
judgment: Planet actively contends with the tribulation; after full degree of separation, malefic can only instill fear.
notes: Described as a secret of questions.

rule: When the Moon is void of course—applying to no planet before leaving her current sign—the matter under inquiry tends toward futility, cancellation, or reversal of intent.
conditions: Moon forming no applying aspect to any planet
judgment: The matter will be frustrated, cancelled, or turned back.

rule: The planet the Moon is applying to join indicates forthcoming events and what is hoped for, colored by the nature of that planet—good if benefic, harmful if malefic.
judgment: Signifies what is yet to come, qualified by the receiving planet's nature.

rule: The planet the Moon has most recently separated from indicates what has already occurred or passed, its quality determined by the nature of that planet.
judgment: Signifies what has already taken place, qualified by the nature of the planet left behind.

rule: A planet occupying its own sign of descension (fall) signifies sorrow, confinement, and distress for the matters and persons it represents.
judgment: Sorrow, imprisonment, and hardship are indicated.

rule: A retrograde planet signifies contrariness, reversal or withdrawal of actions, contradiction, and conflict or divergence in affairs.
judgment: Disobedience, reversal, taking back, discord.

rule: A planet at its first station (about to turn retrograde) signifies dissolution of purpose, disobedience, slowness, and the destruction of undertakings. A planet at its second station (about to turn direct) signifies renewed forward movement and the strengthening of actions after delay or difficulty.
judgment: First station: destruction, slowness, dissolution. Second station: renewal, forward momentum, strengthening of matters.

rule: Malefic planets in general signify difficulty, pressure, and urgency or haste in undertakings.
judgment: Difficulty, pressure, haste.

rule: A planet moving slowly through the zodiac delays the timing of its promised outcomes—whether good or bad. The same slowing applies when a planet is placed in the domiciles of Saturn or Jupiter. Conversely, placement in the domiciles of the faster planets (lights and inner planets) accelerates timing.
conditions: planet in Saturn's or Jupiter's domicile
judgment: Delay in timing or fulfillment of promise; placement in swift-planet domiciles hastens.

rule: When the Moon has completed an exact conjunction with a planet (applying to within one minute of arc), the astrologer should look to the next planet the Moon will join for indications of what is forthcoming in the matter.
conditions: Moon within one minute of exact conjunction with a planet
judgment: Future developments are read from the next planet to which the Moon applies.

rule: A planet in the final degree of a sign has its effective strength already in the next sign, not the current one—like a person stepping out through a doorway. A planet in the 29th degree (28°00'–28°59') still has its full strength within that sign. Every planet's virtue is spread across three degrees: the degree it occupies, the degree behind it, and the degree ahead.
conditions: planet in last degree of sign
judgment: Final degree: strength effectively in next sign. 29th degree: strength still in current sign. Three-degree orb of virtue applies in all cases.
notes: Related to out-of-sign conjunction allowances.

rule: If an applying planet cannot perfect its conjunction before leaving a sign, and no other planet intervenes, the conjunction may still perfect in the next sign. However, if the receiving planet forms a bodily conjunction with a third planet before the applying planet reaches it (even in the next sign), the matter fails because the receiving planet's light has been mixed with another. An aspect does not prevent a bodily conjunction from perfecting, but a bodily conjunction does interrupt an aspect-based joining.
conditions: applying planet crosses sign boundary before conjunction
receiving planet joins third planet before original conjunction perfects
intervening bodily conjunction vs. aspect-only contact
judgment: No intervening conjunction: matter perfects in next sign. Receiving planet joins another first: matter fails. Bodily conjunction overrides aspect; aspect does not cut off bodily conjunction.

rule: A malefic that is oriental (rising in the morning ahead of the Sun), in its own domicile or exaltation, and free from malefic affliction, is more potent and reliable as a significator than a retrograde and afflicted benefic.
conditions: malefic oriental, in own domicile or exaltation, unafflicted
benefic retrograde and impeded for comparison
judgment: Well-placed oriental malefic outperforms a debilitated retrograde benefic.

rule: When malefic planets rule the matter in question and the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins them from a square or opposition, the matter initially progresses but is ultimately ruined. If the malefic is instead the one applying to a benefic (committing its own disposition), outcomes improve compared to when the malefic is the receiver.
conditions: malefic is lord of the matter
Lord of Ascendant or Moon joins malefic by square or opposition
judgment: Matter proceeds but is destroyed in the end; malefic pushing to benefic is better than malefic receiving.

rule: A malefic occupying the Ascendant in its own domicile or exaltation is restrained from expressing full malice. If the same malefic is also retrograde in the Ascendant, its harmful effects are intensified and its variability multiplied.
conditions: malefic in Ascendant in own domicile or exaltation
judgment: In own dignity: malice restrained. Retrograde: malice amplified and varied.

rule: A planet placed in a sign whose nature matches its own produces harmonious results, like compatible substances blending. Placement in a sign contrary to the planet's nature is disruptive, like incompatible substances that cannot mix. For example, Saturn benefits from cold signs; Mars benefits from hot signs.
conditions: planet in sign of matching elemental/modal nature
planet in sign contrary to its nature
judgment: Concordant placement: compatible and productive. Contrary placement: disruptive and harmful.

rule: Jupiter's aspect to Saturn converts Saturn's malice to good; Jupiter's conjunction with Saturn dissolves Saturn's binding effect. Venus similarly dissolves Mars's negative influence. However, Venus alone cannot counteract Saturn's severity—Jupiter must be involved for that. Each outer malefic is neutralized by the corresponding benefic of the same sect.
judgment: Jupiter neutralizes Saturn; Venus neutralizes Mars. Venus cannot overcome Saturn without Jupiter.

rule: When a malefic commits its disposition to another malefic, evil simply transforms into a different form of evil. When a malefic commits to a benefic, the evil converts to good. When a benefic commits to a malefic, good is followed by evil. Outcomes from mixed commitments should be blended accordingly.
judgment: Malefic→malefic: evil persists in changed form. Malefic→benefic: evil turns good. Benefic→malefic: good followed by evil.

rule: If the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant is afflicted by a malefic's conjunction, square, or opposition, and a benefic then joins from a square aspect, the person escapes destruction entirely. If the benefic aspects from a trine, the person may escape one harm but fall into a lesser one, or narrowly escape but not fully.
conditions: Moon/Lord of Ascendant afflicted by malefic
benefic applying by square to afflicted significator
benefic applying by trine to afflicted significator
judgment: Benefic square to afflicted significator: full liberation. Benefic trine: partial escape or narrow escape with residual harm.
notes: Rationale involves whole-sign aspects—a benefic in square to the afflicted planet opposes the malefic directly.

rule: A planet that holds no dignity (not in domicile, exaltation, triplicity, bound, or joy) and is cadent from the angles produces purely negative signification with no beneficial component whatsoever.
judgment: Entirely negative signification; no good whatsoever in the planet's testimony.

rule: A planet that is occidental and under the Sun's rays has weakened strength and reduced light. If it is a malefic in this state, its impediment is lessened. If it is also retrograde while occidental, it is sluggish in all its actions.
judgment: Weakened signification overall; malefic harm diminished; retrograde adds further slowness.

rule: Any planet within 12 degrees of the Sun is considered under the rays and thus weakened in its signification. The sole exception is a planet in the exact degree of the Sun (cazimi), which gains strength from that conjunction.
conditions: planet in exact same degree as Sun (cazimi)
judgment: Within 12°: weakened. Cazimi (exact degree): strengthened.

rule: A planet that is 12° from the Sun in the morning (oriental, rising before the Sun) is strong. At 15° oriental separation it reaches maximum strength. A planet that is occidental (in a later degree, setting after the Sun) begins weakening within 15° of the Sun, reaching minimum strength as it approaches the Sun's degree. Once at exact conjunction (cazimi), it again becomes strong.
judgment: 12° oriental: strong. 15° oriental: peak strength. 7°–15° occidental: weakening. Cazimi: strong again.

rule: A planet in none of its own dignities (peregrine) becomes cunning or unreliable in its significations. However, if it is direct and in an angular or 11th-house position from the Ascendant, it may still signify good.
conditions: peregrine planet direct and angular or in 11th
judgment: Peregrine: cunning and unreliable. Direct and well-placed angularly: may still produce good outcome.

rule: The planet receiving the Moon's disposition is weak and unable to fulfill its judgment if it is occidental and within 12° of the Sun. If it is oriental (rising ahead of the Sun), it is strong and effective in its judgment.
conditions: receiver of disposition occidental within 12° of Sun
judgment: Occidental within 12°: weak, matter unfulfilled. Oriental: strong, matter accomplished.
notes: Metaphor of a fallen building that is rebuilt when re-emerging from the beams.

rule: A benefic placed in the 8th house from the Ascendant neither produces good nor evil. A malefic in the same place has its harmful signification amplified.
judgment: Benefic in 8th: neutral, ineffective. Malefic in 8th: increased harm.

rule: A planet newly entered into a sign remains weak until it has traversed 6 degrees of that sign. Regarding angles: a planet falls away from an angle only after 5 degrees have elapsed past the angle's exact degree. A planet within 5 degrees before the angle's degree is considered cadent.
conditions: planet in first 6° of a sign
planet within 5° before the exact angle degree
judgment: Early degrees: weak. Before 5°: cadent (not in the angle).
notes: The 5-degree rule before an angle is derived from longevity doctrine. See also Judgment 45.
