rule: Any planet located within 15 degrees past (in zodiacal sequence after) the exact angle degree is treated as if it were in that angle. Beyond 15 degrees past the angle, the planet no longer counts as angular. A variant attribution extends this orb to 25 degrees past the angle.
judgment: Treated as angular and retains angular strength.
notes: Two versions: 15° (Sahl) and 25° (Ptolemy). Conflict noted in text.

rule: Planets or significators in fixed signs indicate firmness, durability, and stable conditions in the matter. Those in common (mutable) signs indicate things that recur, are repeated, or that acquire additional components. Those in cardinal (movable) signs indicate rapid change or transformation of the matter into something different, for better or worse.
judgment: Fixed: stability and permanence. Common: repetition or doubling of the matter. Cardinal: swift change or transformation.

rule: Malefic planets that lack any essential dignity in their occupied sign increase their evil and their affliction becomes greater. If malefics occupy signs in which they hold some form of testimony (domicile, exaltation, triplicity, bound), their destructive quality is restrained and impediment is removed entirely.
conditions: malefic with testimony in occupied sign
judgment: Peregrine malefic: increased harm. Malefic with testimony: harm restrained.

rule: When malefic planets are in their own domicile, exaltation, triplicity, or bound, and are placed in angles or succeedent houses, and are the rulers of the matter in question, their effective strength becomes equivalent to that of benefics.
conditions: malefic is lord of the matter
judgment: Malefic functions with the strength of a benefic.

rule: A benefic planet placed in a sign where it holds no testimony has its fortunate signification reduced. When placed in a sign where it holds testimony (domicile, exaltation, triplicity, bound), its fortune is maximized and matters are perfected more fully.
conditions: benefic in sign with no testimony
judgment: No testimony: reduced benefit. Testimony present: increased benefit, matter more likely to perfect.

rule: Any planet—whether benefic or malefic—that is under the rays (combust) or in a traditionally harmful house loses its capacity to produce either good or evil fully. Benefics in this state produce only a small amount of good; malefics in this state produce only a reduced amount of harm.
judgment: Both benefic and malefic significations are reduced to minimal levels.

rule: Any planet—benefic or malefic—that occupies its own domicile, exaltation, or triplicity has whatever evil is present in it turned toward good.
conditions: planet in own domicile, exaltation, or triplicity
judgment: Evil within the planet is converted to good.

rule: Malefics placed in angles and afflicting another planet from a square or opposition aspect achieve maximum harmful power, especially if the malefic is stronger (holds more dignity) than the afflicted planet. Malefics in angles but aspecting by trine or sextile are restrained from full harm.
conditions: malefic aspecting by square or opposition
malefic aspecting by trine or sextile
judgment: Square/opposition from angle: maximum harm, especially if malefic is more dignified. Trine/sextile from angle: harm reduced.

rule: Although a malefic planet always inclines to evil by nature, if it is in a sign of its own nature or dignity, in its sect light, in its own domicile or exaltation or triplicity, or in a favorable house from the Ascendant, it signifies good despite its malefic nature.
conditions: malefic in sign matching its own nature
malefic in good house from Ascendant
judgment: Malefic signifies good when multiple ameliorating factors are present.
notes: 'Own light' refers to sect membership—being of the diurnal sect in a day chart or nocturnal sect in a night chart.

rule: A benefic planet that is out of sect (a nocturnal planet in a day chart or a diurnal planet in a night chart), or is peregrine, or is cadent from the Ascendant, or is under the rays, loses its beneficial quality and instead impedes and produces no profit.
judgment: Benefic becomes unhelpful and obstructing rather than fortunate.

rule: Benefic planets that are cadent from the Ascendant or retrograde are impeded and operate like malefics in their effects.
judgment: Benefic loses positive quality and functions as a malefic.

rule: When a planet is received (in the domicile, exaltation, or other dignity of the planet it applies to), benefics in this state produce stronger good, while malefics in this state produce lesser harm.
conditions: planet received in the place to which it applies
judgment: Received benefic: stronger fortune. Received malefic: reduced harm.

rule: In any horary question, the Ascendant, its lord, and the Moon represent the querent; the house corresponding to the topic of the question and its lord represent the quaesited matter.
judgment: Querent: Ascendant + its lord + Moon. Quaesited: relevant house + its lord.

rule: All matters in horary are perfected by one of three methods: (1) Direct joining—the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon applies to the Lord of the matter, or vice versa; (2) Transfer of light—a third planet separates from one significator and applies to the other, carrying light between them; (3) Collection of light—both significators apply to a single heavier planet, which gathers their combined light. The method of perfection indicates the manner in which the outcome occurs: direct joining means through the querent's own effort or directly; transfer means through a third party or intermediary; collection means through a judge or arbitrator.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant/Moon joining lord of matter (or reverse)
third planet separating from one significator and joining the other
both significators applying to one heavier planet
judgment: Method 1: matter perfects directly through querent or quaesited. Method 2: matter perfects through legates/intermediaries. Method 3: matter perfects through a judge or mediator.

rule: A matter may also perfect when the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon is placed in the house of the matter, or when the Lord of the matter is placed in the Ascendant, provided the Ascendant is not simultaneously impeded and its lord in fall or combust.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon in house of the matter
Ascendant not impeded and its lord not in fall or combust
judgment: Matter perfects through location of significators in each other's houses.

rule: If the planet receiving the final disposition (the heaviest planet in the chain) is retrograde, the matter will be dissolved or reversed after the querent believes it has been successfully obtained.
judgment: Matter appears to perfect but is then undone.

rule: If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter are in trine or sextile aspect, the matter is attained with ease. If they are in square or opposition, the matter comes about with difficulty, obstacles, and delay.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant and Lord of matter in trine or sextile
Lord of Ascendant and Lord of matter in square or opposition
judgment: Trine/sextile: easy attainment. Square/opposition: attainment after difficulty and prolonging.

rule: When the querent's significator (Lord of Ascendant or Moon, as the lighter planet) applies to the Lord of the matter, the querent must make active effort to obtain the outcome. When the Lord of the matter applies to the querent's significator, the outcome comes without the querent's striving—the other party comes to them.
conditions: querent's significator is lighter and applying
lord of matter is lighter and applying
judgment: Lighter querent significator applying: querent must strive. Lord of matter applying: matter comes to querent without effort.

rule: If the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon is in the house of the matter (perfection by location), the outcome requires effort and application by the querent. If the Lord of the matter is in the Ascendant, others will bring the matter to the querent voluntarily and diligently.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon in house of matter
judgment: Querent's significator in house of matter: requires querent's effort. Lord of matter in Ascendant: matter brought without querent's striving.

rule: When the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant joins a planet that is in the descension (fall) of the applying planet itself, or when a significator applies to a planet in its own descension, the matter is damaged and will not perfect. This indicates the querent is in an objectively poor condition for the matter.
conditions: Moon or Lord of Ascendant applying to planet in its own descension
significator applying from its own descension sign
judgment: Matter is harmed and will not be perfected.
notes: Example: Moon joining Mars from Cancer (Mars's fall); Lord of Ascendant as Mars joining from end of Cancer.

rule: When the Lord of the matter is a malefic that does not receive the querent's significator, and the querent's significator joins it by square or opposition, the querent will come to wish the matter had never been pursued due to the evils and tribulations it brings. A trine or sextile reduces this effect.
judgment: Querent will regret pursuing the matter. Trine/sextile: regret reduced.

rule: When the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter are the same planet, the matter perfects if that planet is received (applying to its own domicile or exaltation lord) and free from malefics. If not, the matter fails. The Moon's safe application to this planet also confirms perfection.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant = Lord of matter (same planet)
planet received and free from malefics
Moon safely applying to same planet
judgment: Matter perfects if conditions met; otherwise fails.

rule: The stability of the angles (specifically the Ascendant being a fixed or common sign, and the Midheaven falling in the tenth sign from the Ascendant rather than the ninth) is a positive testimony supporting the perfection of matters.
conditions: Ascendant in fixed or common sign
MC in exact 10th sign from Ascendant
judgment: Stable angular configuration supports perfection of the matter.
notes: Sahl notes that if angles are unstable (MC in 9th sign rather than 10th), this is a negative testimony.

rule: The three witnesses for a matter's completion are the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the matter. If two of these are free from affliction, two-thirds of the desired outcome is obtained. If only one is free, one-third is obtained. If all three are free from retrogradation, combustion, malefic aspect, and fall, the full matter is obtained. If the receivers are also received, the querent gains even beyond what was sought.
conditions: one, two, or all three of: Lord of Ascendant, Moon, lord of matter free from affliction
all three free and receivers are also received
judgment: One free: 1/3 of matter obtained. Two free: 2/3 obtained. Three free: full matter obtained. Receivers also received: exceeds expectation.

rule: Beginning from the principal significator, the astrologer examines the planet it is joined to; if that planet is afflicted (joined to a malefic without reception, retrograde, cadent, combust, or involved in a cutting-off of light), the matter is corrupted. If the first joining is to a sound planet, the examination continues along the chain of conjunctions until an affliction or a safe conclusion is reached. A matter is corrupted after an initial success if any planet in the chain carries an affliction. A planet joined to an afflicted planet but receiving it without square or opposition may still allow the matter to complete when the affliction condition no longer applies.
conditions: significator joined to malefic without reception
significator joined to retrograde, cadent, or combust planet
chain of conjunctions with intervening affliction
transfer of light or collection with afflicted intermediary
judgment: Affliction in chain: matter corrupted. Safe chain: matter complete. Afflicted intermediary in transfer/collection: matter corrupted. Partial reception in affliction: matter delayed until affliction lifts.
notes: This section appears to be an interpolation in the Latin text, possibly from a different translator or source.

rule: For a question about whether the querent will obtain a specific sum of wealth or substance, perfection is indicated by joining between the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon and the Lord of the 2nd house, or by the Lord of the 2nd joining the Lord of the Ascendant, or by the Moon transferring light between them. Benefics placed in the 2nd house indicate the querent will find substance. Malefics in the 2nd indicate loss. A void-of-course Moon indicates the querent will lack substance until death.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant/Moon joining Lord of 2nd
Lord of 2nd joining Lord of Ascendant
judgment: Joining conditions: wealth obtained. Benefic in 2nd: substance found. Malefic in 2nd: substance lost. Void Moon: permanent poverty.

rule: The house in which the receiver of disposition is placed indicates the source or nature of the wealth that will be obtained. Each house corresponds to a different source: 1st/2nd=own labor; 3rd=brothers or friends; 4th=father, parents, land, real estate; 5th=children or trusted associates; 6th=illness, slaves, low-status persons; 7th=women (if feminine sign) or war/contention (if masculine sign); 8th=inheritances and old things; 9th=foreign travel, religion, rhetoric; 10th=kings, nobles, magistrates; 11th=friends, trade, commerce; 12th=enemies, and if sign of quadrupeds, animals, and if sign of humans, prisons.
conditions: house placement of receiver of disposition in 2nd-house question
judgment: House of receiver indicates the domain from which wealth or substance will come.

rule: For questions about a sibling, the 3rd house and its lord signify the brother. Lord of the 3rd in the 6th or joined to the Lord of the 6th indicates the sibling is ill. Lord of the 3rd in the 5th or 2nd indicates the sibling is absent (traveling). Lord of the 3rd impeded in the 12th indicates illness and sorrow; entering combustion indicates the sibling will not escape.
conditions: Lord of 3rd in 6th or joined to Lord of 6th
judgment: 6th connection: sibling ill. 5th or 2nd: sibling absent. 12th impeded: illness and sorrow. Combustion: no escape.

rule: For questions about obtaining land, houses, or real estate, the matter perfects when the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins the Lord of the 4th, or vice versa, or either significator is placed in the other's house, or the Moon transfers light between them.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon joining Lord of 4th
Lord of 4th joining Lord of Ascendant
Lord of Ascendant or Moon in 4th
judgment: Any of these conditions: querent obtains the property.

rule: The sign on the 4th house indicates the nature of the land in question. Fire signs (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius): mountainous, hard to cultivate. Earth signs (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn): flat. Air signs (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius): mixed, both mountainous and level. Water signs (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces): watery or near water. Common signs in the 4th: land has both mountains and flat fields.
conditions: sign occupying 4th house in question about land
judgment: Sign type indicates physical character of the land.

rule: In a question about a property sale or rental, the Ascendant signifies the seller, the 7th signifies the buyer, the Midheaven signifies the purpose/goal of the transaction, and the 4th signifies the outcome. Benefic or malefic placement in each angle describes the qualities and fate of the corresponding party or aspect of the deal.
judgment: Benefic in Ascendant: willing, suitable seller. Malefic in Ascendant: seller reluctant or deceptive. Benefic in 7th: willing, suitable buyer. Malefic in 7th: buyer withdraws or quarrels. Malefic in 10th: deal fails. Malefic in 4th: bad ending. Benefic in 4th: good ending.

rule: A benefic in the Midheaven indicates an abundance of trees on the property; if direct, trees are strong and fruitful; if retrograde, the trees suffer and the fruits will be sold off. A malefic in the Midheaven indicates few trees; if retrograde, what remains is sold. If no planet is in the Midheaven, the Lord of the Midheaven is examined: if it aspects the 10th, trees are present; if oriental, newly planted; if occidental, old planting. If the Lord of the Midheaven does not aspect the 10th (being in 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th from it), the land has no trees.
conditions: Lord of Midheaven oriental or occidental
Lord of Midheaven direct or retrograde
judgment: Presence, age, and condition of trees on property.

rule: The 7th house signifies what is on the land that is smaller than trees—grasses, herbs, and small plants.
judgment: Indicates small vegetation on property.

rule: In a question about land, the Ascendant signifies the farmers who work it. A malefic in the Ascendant indicates dishonest farmers; if direct, they remain; if retrograde, they flee. A benefic in the Ascendant indicates honest farmers; if direct, they stay; if retrograde, they leave.
judgment: Malefic: dishonest farmers. Benefic: honest farmers. Direct: remain. Retrograde: depart.

rule: For a question about whether a querent will have a child with a particular woman, the matter perfects when the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins the Lord of the 5th, or vice versa, or either is placed in the other's house, or a planet transfers light between the Lord of the Ascendant and Lord of the 5th. A transfer of light in the 5th specifically may indicate a delay.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant/Moon joining Lord of 5th (or reverse)
significator in house of the other
planet transferring light between them in 5th
judgment: Joining/location: child will come. Transfer in 5th: child with delay.

rule: In a child question, after confirming the child will be born, the receiver of the final disposition is examined for the child's survival. If it is free from malefics and neither cadent nor combust, the child will live. If it is retrograde, combust, or cadent, the child will perish.
conditions: receiver of disposition free from malefics, not cadent or combust
judgment: Free receiver: child survives. Afflicted receiver: child dies.

rule: Jupiter in a good, unimpeded place indicates pregnancy. A malefic with Venus denies pregnancy. The Moon joining malefics denies impregnation. A benefic in the 5th indicates the woman will become pregnant. Malefics in the 5th, or aspecting it from square or opposition, deny pregnancy.
judgment: Jupiter well-placed: pregnancy likely. Malefic with Venus or Moon: pregnancy denied. Benefic in 5th: pregnant. Malefic in/aspecting 5th: not pregnant.

rule: For an absolute question about whether the querent will ever have children, benefics in the Ascendant or the Lord of the Ascendant in the 1st, 10th, 11th, or 5th with Jupiter in a good place indicates a child will come. Lord of the Ascendant in the 4th or 7th with Jupiter well-placed: child comes after delay. Malefic in the Ascendant or aspecting it by square/opposition, Lord of Ascendant in a bad place, and Jupiter cadent, in the 8th, or combust: few children and short-lived.
conditions: benefic in Ascendant or Lord of Ascendant angular/5th with Jupiter well-placed
Lord of Ascendant in 4th or 7th with Jupiter well-placed
malefic afflicting Ascendant and Jupiter afflicted
judgment: Strong conditions: child born soon. Angular/7th with good Jupiter: child born with delay. All afflicted: scarcity and short life of children.

rule: Jupiter oriental and angular indicates a child will come quickly. Jupiter occidental (evening rising) in an angle with Lord of Ascendant in suitable place indicates a child will come slowly, after delay.
conditions: Jupiter occidental in angle with Lord of Ascendant well-placed
judgment: Oriental Jupiter: quick birth. Occidental Jupiter: delayed birth.

rule: For a question about whether a woman is pregnant, the strongest indication is the Lord of the Ascendant and Moon both in the 5th while the Lord of the 5th is in the Ascendant and free from malefics. The Lord of the Ascendant and Moon committing their disposition to the receiver also indicates pregnancy, especially if received. Application to a cadent planet instead indicates a failed pregnancy, especially if the Ascendant is movable, a malefic is in an angle, or the Moon joins a malefic.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant and Moon in 5th, Lord of 5th in Ascendant
Ascendant movable or malefic angular or Moon joining malefic
judgment: Strong angular confirmation: pregnant. Committed and received: pregnant. Cadent reception: pregnancy fails.

rule: For a question about whether a pregnancy is real or will come to term, if the Lord of the Ascendant joins a cadent planet that does not receive it, or joins a retrograde planet, the pregnancy is false or will fail—unless the Moon is received or the Lord of the Ascendant is well-placed from the Ascendant, in which case the pregnancy is confirmed.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant joining cadent planet without reception
Lord of Ascendant joining retrograde planet
Moon received or Lord of Ascendant in good place despite above
judgment: Cadent/retrograde joining: pregnancy fails. Reception or good placement overrides: pregnancy real.

rule: A pregnant woman carries twins when the Ascendant is a common sign, or when two benefics are in the Ascendant or 5th house, or when both luminaries are in common signs.
conditions: Sun and Moon both in common signs
judgment: One or more of these conditions: twins expected.

rule: The sex of a child is determined by the signs occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant and Lord of the 5th. If both are in masculine signs, the child is male; if both in feminine signs, the child is female. If they differ, the Moon's sign and the sex of the planet she joins determine the sex. Mercury is masculine when oriental and feminine when occidental.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant and Lord of 5th in masculine signs
Moon's sign and the planet joined
judgment: Concordant masculine: male child. Concordant feminine: female child. Mixed: Moon and her applying planet determine sex. Mercury oriental: masculine. Mercury occidental: feminine.

rule: In illness questions, the Ascendant signifies the doctor, the 10th house signifies the patient, the 7th house signifies the disease or infirmity, and the 4th house signifies the medicine. Benefic or malefic planets in each of these houses determine whether each element is beneficial or harmful.
judgment: Ascendant: doctor's effectiveness. 10th: patient's compliance. 7th: nature/change of disease. 4th: effect of medicine. Benefic: beneficial in each role. Malefic: harmful.

rule: The stronger of the Lord of the Ascendant and Moon (the one angular and aspecting the Ascendant) is examined in illness questions. If it is free from malefics, not in aspect to the Lord of the 8th, not under the rays, and joined to a benefic, it signifies recovery. If the benefic is retrograde, illness is prolonged but recovery follows.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon angular and aspecting Ascendant
free from malefics and Lord of 8th
judgment: Free and joined to direct benefic: recovery. Joined to retrograde benefic: prolonged illness but eventual recovery.

rule: In illness: Moon above the earth and joined to a planet above the earth indicates health, unless the receiver of disposition is entering combustion (then death). Moon above the earth joined to a malefic below the earth indicates death. Moon below the earth joined to a planet in the 9th (cadent) indicates death. Moon joined to the Lord of the Ascendant with the Lord increasing in light and number indicates quick recovery.
conditions: Moon above earth joining planet above earth
Moon above earth joining malefic below earth
Moon below earth, joined to planet in 9th
Moon joined to Lord of Ascendant, Lord increasing
judgment: Above/above free: health. Above/above with receiver entering combustion: death. Above/below malefic: death. Below/9th cadent: death. Moon joins increasing Lord of Ascendant: quick recovery.

rule: Multiple configurations involving the Lord of the 8th indicate death in illness questions: (1) Lord of Ascendant joined to Lord of 8th with Moon impeded; (2) Moon transferring light from Lord of Ascendant to Lord of 8th; (3) Lord of Ascendant joined to Lord of 8th from trine, and Lord of 8th reaches the exact ascending degree; (4) a planet transfers the Lord of Ascendant's light to Lord of 8th with Lord of Ascendant cadent and Lord of 8th angular; (5) Lord of 8th in Ascendant with Lord of Ascendant or Moon impeded; (6) Lord of Ascendant entering combustion (within 12° of Sun) and not received; (7) Lord of Ascendant below earth joined to Lord of 8th in 4th.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant joining Lord of 8th with Moon impeded
Moon transferring light to Lord of 8th
Lord of Ascendant trine Lord of 8th and Lord of 8th reaches Ascendant degree
planet transfers Lord of Ascendant's light to angular Lord of 8th, Lord of Ascendant cadent
Lord of 8th in Ascendant, Lord of Ascendant or Moon impeded
Lord of Ascendant entering combustion, unreceived
judgment: Any of these configurations in illness: death indicated.

rule: In illness questions, if the 6th house is a movable sign, the patient will alternately improve and worsen. A common sign in the 6th indicates the illness transforms into a different ailment. A fixed sign in the 6th indicates the condition remains stable.
judgment: Movable: fluctuating illness. Common: changes to different disease. Fixed: constant condition.

rule: Moon separated from an oriental planet indicates a new or recent illness. Moon separated from an occidental planet indicates a prolonged illness already in progress. Moon applying to an oriental planet indicates speed (of recovery or change). Moon applying to an occidental planet indicates the illness will be prolonged. Moon applying to a retrograde planet indicates long-lasting disease. Moon applying to a slower planet indicates worsening and fear.
judgment: Separation from oriental: new illness. Separation from occidental: old illness. Joining oriental: speed. Joining occidental: prolongation. Joining retrograde: long-lasting. Joining slower planet: worsening.

rule: Critical days in illness are the 7th, 14th, 21st, and 28th days from onset. These are found by advancing the Moon's natal position by 90°, 180°, 270°, and 360° respectively. On days when the Moon reaches a malefic or the Lord of the 6th, the patient worsens. On days when the Moon reaches benefics or they aspect her, rest and improvement occur. The more times the Moon contacts a benefic on these days, the more often the patient improves; malefic contacts correspond to increases in pain.
conditions: Moon's position on 7th/14th/21st/28th day from illness onset
Moon reaching malefic or Lord of 6th on critical day
Moon reaching benefic or aspected by benefic on critical day
judgment: Malefic contact on critical day: worsening. Benefic contact: rest and improvement.
notes: Days measured from decumbiture or from time of consultation.

rule: To determine whether a person is currently ill, examine whether the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon is in the 6th house, joined to the Lord of the 6th, in its own fall, or combust under the rays. Any of these indicates illness; absent these conditions, the person is not ill.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon in 6th
judgment: Any condition present: person is ill. None present: person is not ill.

rule: For a question about whether a slave will be freed, if the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon is separated from the Lord of the Midheaven, the Sun, or the malefics and has not joined any of these, freedom is indicated.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon separated from Lord of Midheaven, Sun, or malefics
judgment: Slave will be freed.

rule: If a slave asks whether to leave the current master, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle not joined to a cadent planet, the slave will not leave. If the Lord of the Ascendant joins a planet in the 9th or 3rd, departure is indicated. If the Lord of the Ascendant is angular but afflicted by opposition, conjunction, or square of malefics, or entering combustion, the slave will die before leaving.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant in angle, not joining cadent planet
Lord of Ascendant joining planet in 9th or 3rd
Lord of Ascendant angular but afflicted or entering combustion
judgment: Angular, unafflicted: slave stays. Joining 9th/3rd: slave departs. Angular and afflicted/combustion: slave dies before leaving.

rule: For a question about whether a current master or a new one would be better for a slave: if the Lord of the Ascendant is received in its current sign (joining its domicile or exaltation lord), the current situation is better. If the Lord of the 7th is received, the new master is better. The Moon's separation and application also indicate direction: separation from a benefic favors the current situation; applying to a planet that receives the Moon favors the new. If no reception is found, advancing either planet to the next sign to check for reception reveals which future direction is better.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant received in current sign
judgment: Lord of Ascendant received: current situation better. Lord of 7th received: new master better. Moon separation/application: indicates direction of benefit.

rule: For any question about whether the current condition or a future/changed condition is better—whether regarding travel, work, housing, or any change of circumstances—apply the same method as for the slave question: examine reception of the Lord of the Ascendant in the current sign vs. the next sign, and the Moon's applications.
conditions: any question comparing current vs. changed condition
judgment: Reception in current sign: stay is better. Reception found in next sign: change is better.

rule: For a question about purchasing a slave, the matter is perfected when the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins the Lord of the 6th, or vice versa, or when either significator is in the other's house, or when a planet transfers light between them.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant/Moon joining Lord of 6th
Lord of 6th joining Lord of Ascendant
judgment: Any condition: purchase completed.

rule: For a question about obtaining a slave-girl from a specific person, the Ascendant represents the querent, the 7th represents the person holding her, and the 11th represents the slave-girl herself. Perfection is assessed by the joining of the Lord of the Ascendant and Moon with the relevant lord, or through light transfer.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant and Moon examined vs. Lord of 7th and Lord of 11th
judgment: Joining or transfer with relevant significator: slave-girl obtained.
notes: Why 11th and not 6th: possibly construed as the 5th from the 7th (pleasure from the seller).

rule: For a question about whether a master will inherit the estate of a deceased slave, the relevant house is the 7th from the Ascendant (being the 2nd from the 6th house of slaves). Perfection is indicated when the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins the Lord of the 7th, or vice versa, or by location or transfer of light.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon joining Lord of 7th
Lord of 7th joining Lord of Ascendant
judgment: Any condition: master obtains the estate.

rule: For a question about whether a slave will obey his master or whether possession (i.e., control) of the slave will be obtained, the 3rd house from the Ascendant is used, as it is the 10th from the 6th house (the 10th of slaves). Joining conditions between Lord of Ascendant or Moon and Lord of the 3rd, or location or transfer of light, indicate the master will obtain the possession or compliance.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon joining Lord of 3rd
Lord of Ascendant or Moon in 3rd
judgment: Possession/obedience of slave obtained.

rule: For a marriage question, the Ascendant, its lord, and Moon represent the querent; the 7th house and its lord represent the potential spouse. The matter perfects by joining (querent's significator to Lord of 7th or reverse), by location (significator in other's house), or by transfer of light. When the Lord of the 7th applies to the querent's significator, the woman's desire exceeds the man's.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon joining Lord of 7th
Lord of 7th joining Lord of Ascendant
Lord of 7th as the applying planet
judgment: Any joining condition: marriage perfects. Lord of 7th applying: woman desires it more than man.

rule: The nature and house rulership of the malefic impeding the marriage indicates the source of the impediment. Lord of 2nd or 8th impeding: financial/dowry issues. Lord of 12th impeding: criticism of the woman's lineage. Lord of 6th impeding: issues with the man's lineage. Lord of 4th impeding: trouble from fathers or parents. Lord of 3rd impeding: trouble from brothers. A planet cutting off (prohibiting) the conjunction identifies the source by its own house rulership, and a malefic bearing light between significators indicates problems from the intermediaries.
conditions: planet cutting off conjunction is lord of specific house
judgment: House rulership of the impeding or cutting planet identifies source of marital impediment.

rule: The aspect between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 7th describes the quality of the relationship. Opposition: serious conflict and contention. Square: generally good relationship with occasional conflict. Trine or sextile: mutual esteem and good quality. The lord that is angular and the heavier (receiver of disposition) rules and dominates. The cadent or applying lord is subject. Both lords in one sign: mutual contention. Moon impeding the Ascendant with malefic aspect: verbal insults between spouses.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant and Lord of 7th in opposition
judgment: Opposition: much conflict. Square: good with occasional strife. Trine/sextile: good esteem. Angular/heavier: dominant. Cadent/lighter: subject. Same sign: contention. Afflicted Moon on Ascendant: verbal strife.

rule: In a marriage question, an impeded Sun harms the man; an impeded Venus harms the woman; an impeded Moon harms both parties.
judgment: Sun afflicted: man harmed. Venus afflicted: woman harmed. Moon afflicted: both harmed.

rule: For a woman who has left her husband's house, if the Moon is past the full (waning, in second half of lunar month), her return will be hastened. If the Moon is waxing (increasing, first half of month), her return will be slower. If Venus was retrograde and occidental at the time of departure, the woman returns of her own accord, penitent. If Venus was oriental and emerging from under the rays, retrograde, the husband is penitent for her leaving but the woman is less so.
conditions: Moon waning at time of query
Venus retrograde and occidental at departure
Venus oriental and retrograde at departure
judgment: Waning Moon: quick return. Waxing Moon: slow return. Venus retrograde/occidental: woman penitent, voluntary return. Venus retrograde/oriental: husband penitent.

rule: For a question about a woman's virginity: if the Ascendant, its lord, and Moon are in fixed signs, she is virgin and free from the accusation. If in movable or common signs, she is not a virgin. If the Moon is in a common or movable sign but the Ascendant and lord are in a fixed sign, she has been compromised but not fully violated. Moon with Mars in movable/common: virginity taken in friendship with men. Saturn in Ascendant with Moon in common or fixed sign: someone used her unnaturally. Mars in opposition or square to Venus with Moon impeded by Mars and Venus in Scorpio: not a virgin.
conditions: Moon in movable/common but Ascendant fixed
Saturn conjunct Moon in Ascendant in common/fixed
Mars in square/opposition to Venus, Moon impeded by Mars, Venus in Scorpio
judgment: Fixed: virgin. Movable/common: not virgin. Moon movable/Ascendant fixed: compromised partially. Mars with Moon: active relationships. Saturn with Moon: unnatural acts. Mars-Venus configuration: not virgin.

rule: Venus and Mercury in Aquarius or Leo together: woman has never given birth. Venus and Mercury in Scorpio or Taurus: woman has a child. Mars and Moon or Venus in a common sign (other than Sagittarius): woman has a child. Sagittarius indicates the woman will never have a child; if she has had one, the child died. Malefics in movable signs: child conceived outside of marriage. Benefics in common signs: child conceived in lawful union.
conditions: Venus and Mercury in Aquarius or Leo
Venus and Mercury in Scorpio or Taurus
Mars and Moon or Venus in common sign except Sagittarius
judgment: Specific sign combinations indicate presence/absence of children and legitimacy.

rule: In a question about whether a pregnancy is legitimate or from fornication: if Mars, Saturn, or Mercury aspects the 5th house, the pregnancy is from fornication. If benefics aspect the 5th, the pregnancy is legitimate.
conditions: Mars, Saturn, or Mercury aspecting 5th house
judgment: Malefic aspect: fornication. Benefic aspect: legitimate.

rule: For a question about whether a woman has a current or past male lover, examine the Lord of the Ascendant and Moon in relation to Mars: exact conjunction (within one degree) = man in her house; same sign but not degree = nearby neighbor; separation from Mars = former lover now dismissed; application to Mars in his domicile = man who actively seeks her and she wants him. Application to Jupiter = she has loved a higher-status man. Application to Mercury = she loves a young, educated man. Application to Venus = she is attracted to women. Jupiter aspecting Venus = she has left relationships for religious reasons. Sun aspecting = a high-status man gazed upon her and she dismissed him. Venus aspecting = she has accepted him sexually.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or Moon conjunct Mars within one degree
applying to Mars in his domicile
judgment: Specific applications and aspects describe the nature and status of the woman's relationships.

rule: If Mercury and Saturn are in one sign and aspect the Moon or Lord of the Ascendant (by sign), the woman has taken a man matching the described character into a betrothal or similar arrangement. If the Moon applies to Mercury and Saturn, the woman loves an effeminate man of the described character.
conditions: Mercury and Saturn in same sign aspecting Moon or Lord of Ascendant
Moon applying to Mercury and Saturn
judgment: Woman has accepted an effeminate partner or one of mercurial-saturnine character.

rule: For a question about who wins a dispute, the Ascendant/its lord/Moon represent the querent; the 7th and its lord represent the opponent. Trine or sextile between the lords: they will agree before fighting. Square or opposition: agreement comes only after contest. Both lords in the same sign: direct peace without intermediary. Lord of Midheaven aspecting them with a prior conjunction to one lord: dispute goes to the king. Moon transferring light between them: peace through intermediaries.
conditions: Lord of Midheaven aspecting both with prior joining
judgment: Trine/sextile: pre-fight agreement. Square/opposition: agreement after contest. Same sign: direct settlement. Midheaven lord: goes to king. Moon transfer: through intermediary.

rule: In a dispute, the party whose significator is in an angle is stronger. The party whose significator is received has more allies. The Lord of the 7th in the Ascendant indicates the querent's strength. The Lord of the Ascendant in the 7th indicates the opponent's strength. A retrograde significator indicates weakness, flight, deception, and broken promises from the party represented. A retrograde Lord of the Midheaven indicates an unjust judge and prolonged dispute. A luminary joined to a significator or in its domicile strengthens that party.
conditions: luminary joined to or in domicile of significator
judgment: Angular: stronger. Received: more allies. Lord of 7th in Ascendant: querent's strength. Lord of Ascendant in 7th: opponent's strength. Retrograde: weakness and deception. Retrograde Midheaven lord: unjust judge.

rule: The judge or king in a dispute is represented by the Lord of the Midheaven. Whichever disputant's significator the Lord of the Midheaven aspects determines which party the judge favors. If a peregrine planet is in the Midheaven and neither it nor the Lord of the Midheaven aspects either significator, the parties will arrange their own private judge. Saturn as Lord of Midheaven in the Midheaven: unjust judge. Mars in Midheaven: quick and sharp judge. Jupiter in Midheaven: just judge. Venus in Midheaven: agreeable, lenient judge. Mercury in Midheaven: perceptive judge. Common sign on Midheaven: first judge will not finish, a second judge will be required.
conditions: Lord of Midheaven aspecting one significator
peregrine planet in Midheaven not aspecting either
judgment: Midheaven lord aspect determines judicial favor. Specific planets in Midheaven describe judge's character. Common sign: multiple judges required.

rule: For a purchase/sale question, joining between the Lord of the Ascendant and Lord of the 7th indicates agreement. The applying (lighter) planet initiates the deal. Transfer of light through a third planet indicates agreement through an intermediary. Lord of Ascendant in the 7th: buyer pursues seller. Lord of the 7th in Ascendant: seller pursues buyer. Benefic in Ascendant: seller honest and easy; malefic: slow and dishonest. Benefic in 7th: buyer honest and easy; malefic: contrary.
judgment: Joining: agreement. Lord of Ascendant in 7th: buyer pursues. Lord of 7th in Ascendant: seller pursues. Benefic placement: honesty/ease. Malefic: dishonesty/difficulty.

rule: In a sale question, if the Moon has not separated from any planet but is applying, the seller will sell but the buyer will not receive the item from him directly, or buys without paying. If the Moon is separated but not applying to any planet, there is a delay and tentative agreement only. If the planet from whom the Moon separates enters combustion, the seller will die before transferring ownership.
conditions: planet from whom Moon separated entering combustion
judgment: No separation/applying: item not received from seller directly. Separated/not applying: delay. Seller's significator entering combustion: seller dies before transfer.

rule: For a fugitive or lost item question, the Ascendant, its lord, and Moon represent the owner/master; the 7th and its lord and Moon represent the fugitive or lost thing. Lord of Ascendant joining Lord of 7th: owner finds by active search. Lord of Ascendant in 7th: same. Lord of 7th joining Lord of Ascendant or in Ascendant: fugitive returns voluntarily before leaving the region. Moon separated from Lord of Ascendant and joining Lord of 7th: an informant reveals the location. Moon separated from Lord of 7th and joining Lord of Ascendant: fugitive sends a message seeking terms. Lord of 7th angular and joined to a malefic: fugitive caught. Lord of 7th under the rays: discovery of fugitive.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant joining Lord of 7th
Lord of 7th joining Lord of Ascendant or in Ascendant
Moon separated from Lord of Ascendant joining Lord of 7th
Moon separated from Lord of 7th joining Lord of Ascendant
Lord of 7th in angle joined to malefic
judgment: Various conditions indicate manner and success of recovery of fugitive or lost item.

rule: Moon joining a malefic in a fugitive question: fugitive caught. Moon joining a retrograde planet: fugitive returns voluntarily. Moon joining a stationary planet in angle or succeedent: fugitive does not move until caught. First station: caught and bound in fetters. Second station: caught, bound, but later escapes. Moon joining direct planet: returned without fetters. Moon under rays joining Mars: fugitive dies by fire. Moon under rays joining Saturn: fugitive dies by water. Moon aspecting Lord of her own domicile: fugitive's possessions are captured. Moon increasing in light: capture slowed. Moon decreasing: capture hastened. Lord of 7th joined to benefic (unafflicted): fugitive not caught. Benefic entering combustion: fugitive dies. Benefic entering combustion after joining malefic: corpse found.
conditions: Moon joining stationary planet (first or second station)
Moon aspecting lord of her domicile
judgment: Multiple fate indicators for the fugitive based on Moon's applying planet and condition.

rule: A malefic in the 9th house in a fugitive question indicates the fugitive will be caught and returned. A benefic in the 9th indicates the fugitive cannot be caught.
judgment: Malefic in 9th: fugitive caught. Benefic in 9th: fugitive not caught.

rule: The direction in which a fugitive has fled is indicated by the Moon's angular house position: Moon in Ascendant = east; Moon in Midheaven = south; Moon in Descendent (7th) = west; Moon in 4th = north. If the Moon is not angular, the direction is determined by the sign and direction of the planet the Moon is in or applying to.
judgment: Angular Moon: cardinal direction indicated. Non-angular Moon: direction from sign/planet.

rule: For a fugitive asking whether to return or continue: if the Moon is separating from malefics, returning is bad. If separating from benefics, returning is better. If applying to benefics, continuing on is better. If applying to malefics, continuing on is bad.
judgment: Separating from malefic: don't return. Separating from benefic: return. Applying to benefic: continue. Applying to malefic: don't continue.

rule: Horary inquiry is valid when the querent comes with genuine concern, necessity, or distress. Questions from those testing the astrologer, or asked with craft or deception, do not produce reliable charts. The chart's configuration reflects the degree of the querent's genuine involvement and the nature of their situation. Multiple questions of the same type asked under one Ascendant yield overlapping or identical answers; multiple distinct questions under one Ascendant are permissible.
conditions: querent genuinely concerned or in necessity
judgment: Genuine concern: valid chart. Testing/craftiness: unreliable result. Same-type multiple questions: answers merge. Distinct multiple questions: individually permissible.

rule: The scope of the chart's validity corresponds to the querent's actual intent: if asking about the whole lifetime, the planetary configuration at the question's hour signifies conditions for the entire life. If asking about a year, month, or day, the chart signifies accordingly. The astrologer should determine the querent's true intent before analyzing the chart.
conditions: querent's intention covers year, month, or day
judgment: Chart's planets signify the period covered by the querent's actual concern.

rule: A person for whom benefics meet or aspect the Lord of the Ascendant and Moon will be made fortunate; one whose significators are met by malefic impediments will be obstructed. Querents asking about fortune are those in a fortunate condition; those asking about impediment are those who are already impeded.
conditions: benefic aspecting or conjoining Lord of Ascendant and Moon
malefic impeding Lord of Ascendant and Moon
judgment: Benefic aspects: fortune. Malefic impediment: obstruction. Questioner's circumstance mirrors the chart's configuration.

rule: An elected chart derives its strength from the native's birth chart. When the natal root is strong, it reinforces weak planets in an election. Without a viable root, an election cannot overcome a fundamentally adverse fate.
judgment: Election efficacy is proportional to the quality of the natal root; a destroyed natal root cannot be compensated by even an optimally constructed election.
notes: Text implies a hierarchy: kings have inherently strong roots and benefit even from weak elections; low-status clients require examination of nativity, solar return, and children's charts before electing.

rule: Before constructing an election, the astrologer should consult available root charts in this descending order of preference: (1) the client's nativity; (2) the annual solar return of the nativity; (3) a horary question cast for the client; (4) the moment of the client's arrival as a substitute root when no other chart is available.
judgment: The more root charts available and favorable, the more reliable and potent the election; if all substitute roots are also afflicted, the astrologer should decline to elect.
notes: Text specifically warns: if the horary substitute root shows a bad outcome, do not proceed to election.

rule: Do not construct an election for a client whose natal chart or substitute root (horary) indicates destruction or death regarding the matter sought. Even placing all benefics in angular houses and all malefics in cadent houses will not help if the root itself is ruined.
conditions: natal or horary significator destroyed or afflicted
matter signified by root as impossible
judgment: Election cannot overcome a destroyed root; the astrologer should refrain from electing.
notes: Particular caution advised for low- and middle-class clients where the natal Ascendant or relevant sign may be unknown and thus the election Ascendant may accidentally be inimical to the client's root.

rule: When multiple people begin a journey or enterprise at the same elected moment, different outcomes will occur for each according to their individual nativities and their current primary directions in those nativities. A single election chart cannot override individual natal fate.
judgment: Outcomes for group members under a shared election diverge according to each individual's natal condition and predictive timing indicators.
notes: Text cites primary directions (qisma) as the key predictive technique differentiating outcomes.

rule: When a significator is configured with a malefic by square or opposition—or in the same sign—yet good results follow, this occurs because the malefic in question is a lord of the natal Ascendant, a divisional ruler of that period, or the Ascendant lord of the solar return, making it more agreeable to the significator despite its generally harmful nature.
conditions: significator joined to or aspected by malefic
malefic is lord of natal Ascendant or divisional ruler or solar return Ascendant lord
judgment: Malefic produces good rather than harm when it holds significant rulership in the root or timing charts.
notes: Text uses 'first lords of the Ascendant' with some ambiguity; may also refer to triplicity lords.

rule: Align the election Ascendant or the election significators with the Ascendant of the client's nativity, the horary question, or the sign of the annual profection. This produces a superior election because the astrologer can identify which planets are in harmony with those root factors.
judgment: Election is more reliable and effective when its Ascendant or Lord corresponds to root chart indicators.

rule: Movable (cardinal) signs signify rapid change, impermanence, and lack of duration in elected matters. They are favorable for: sowing seed, buying and selling, betrothals, recovery from illness, resolution of disputes, return of fugitives, and foreign travel. They are unfavorable for: laying foundations, long-term planting, medical treatment, and any enterprise requiring stability. Promises made under movable signs will not be kept. Dreams and rumors are false under them.
conditions: Moon or Ascendant in a cardinal sign at election
judgment: Matters begun under movable signs proceed quickly but do not last; suitable for fast transactions, unsuitable for foundations and stable enterprises.
notes: Aries and Cancer are faster and more mobile among the cardinals; Libra and Capricorn are stronger and more temperate.

rule: Fixed signs are appropriate for enterprises requiring durability and permanence: building construction, laying foundations, celebration of weddings (after engagement in a movable sign), agreements, and legal claims. Under fixed signs, divorces are final, imprisonment is prolonged, anger is slow to dissipate, and judgments are firm but require benefic testimony for confidence. Fixed signs resist change and produce lasting outcomes whether good or bad.
conditions: Moon or Ascendant in a fixed sign at election
judgment: Matters begun under fixed signs endure; suitable for building and lasting commitments, unsuitable for quick resolution or change.
notes: Among fixed signs: Scorpio is lighter, Leo is most fixed, Aquarius is slowest and worst, Taurus is most even.

rule: Common (mutable) signs are useful for partnerships and matters that will be repeated. They indicate trickery and deception in buying and marriage. Imprisonment under common signs is unstable. Legal judgments are indeterminate. Travel arrangements change. Promises are broken. Illness follows a relapsing pattern. Deaths under common signs are followed by a second death nearby. All good and evil is doubled. Suitable for: changing residence, washing, purification of metals, sending children to school.
conditions: Moon or Ascendant in a mutable sign at election
judgment: Matters under common signs are unstable, doubled in effect, and prone to repetition or reversal.
notes: The doubling principle applies to both good and bad outcomes. Also appropriate for alchemical or repeated works.

rule: Sign categories carry the following correspondences for elections: watery signs correspond to hunting by land and sea; royal signs correspond to matters involving kings; signs with voices correspond to music and singing; fiery signs correspond to all matters involving fire; equinoctial signs (where day and night are equal) correspond to truth-telling, honest dealing, and work with scales; tropical signs (where day and night begin to change) correspond to change and transitions from one state to another.
conditions: Moon or Ascendant placed in a sign of a given category
judgment: Election is strengthened when the sign category matches the nature of the matter sought.

rule: For any elected matter, align the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant with the planet whose natural signification matches the subject of the election. The governing planetary correspondences are: Sun for kings, princes, nobles, public figures, administrators of cities, and matters of public justice; Jupiter for persons of elevated station; Saturn for farmers and lowest-class people; Mars for military commanders and fighters; Venus for women; Mercury for merchants, scribes, writers, and businesspeople; Moon for queens and feminine matters involving women.
conditions: type of person or matter involved in election
judgment: Strengthening the relevant planet increases the efficacy of the election for that category of person or matter.

rule: In any election, the four primary factors to adapt are: (1) the Ascendant, (2) its Lord, (3) the Moon, and (4) the Lord of the house governing the matter being elected. All four should be free from impediment and strengthened as much as possible.
judgment: Well-disposed Ascendant, its lord, Moon, and house lord of matter indicate successful outcome.

rule: There are ten conditions that constitute impediment of the Moon in elections, listed in descending severity: (1) combustion within 12° of the Sun, either applying or separating (applying is worse); (2) placement in the degree of the Moon's own fall (descension); (3) placement in exact opposition to the Sun; (4) conjunction with a malefic, or reception of a malefic's square or opposition rays; (5) conjunction with the Head or Tail of the Dragon within 12° (eclipse boundary); (6) placement in the final degrees of a sign, specifically the bounds of malefic planets; (7) cadency from an angular house, or placement in the burnt path (end of Libra/beginning of Scorpio)—this is the worst impediment, especially for marriage, matters of women, commerce, and travel; (8) placement in the twelfth sign from Cancer (i.e., Gemini) with a malefic, or in opposition to Cancer, or otherwise disconnected from Cancer by whole-sign aspect; (9) slower-than-average daily motion, specifically less than 12° per day—described as resembling Saturn's pace; (10) void of course.
conditions: Moon's position and aspect pattern at time of election
judgment: Any of these ten conditions weakens or destroys the election; the seventh (cadent or burnt path) is identified as the most severe.
attribution_in_text: Dorotheus (conditions 1–9 cited collectively); Masha'allah (condition 10, void of course)
notes: Condition 8 may alternatively refer to the Moon's twelfth-part falling with a malefic; the Latin and Arabic versions differ on this point.

rule: Placing the Moon in the Ascendant is generally to be avoided because it correlates with bodily illness for the inceptor. The exception is when the Lord of the Ascendant or a benefic aspects the ascending degree, which can neutralize the harmful tendency.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant or benefic aspecting Ascendant
judgment: Moon in Ascendant without mitigating aspect from Ascendant lord or benefic risks illness; mitigating aspect removes or reduces this danger.
notes: Analogical rule appended: a planet not aspecting its own domicile is like an absent householder who cannot protect the home; a planet aspecting its domicile is like a present guardian who deters intruders.

rule: A planet that aspects its own domicile by sign acts as a protective ruler over that place, deterring intrusion by malefics. A planet that does not aspect its domicile is functionally absent from it and unable to prevent harm.
conditions: planet in aspect vs. not in aspect to its own sign
judgment: Planet aspecting own domicile protects it; planet not aspecting own domicile leaves it vulnerable.
notes: Used to explain why the Lord of the Ascendant aspecting the Ascendant prevents Moon-in-Ascendant illness.

rule: When the Lord of the Ascendant in an election is a malefic planet, ensure that it aspects the Ascendant by trine or sextile rather than by square, opposition, or without aspect.
conditions: malefic is Lord of Ascendant in election chart
judgment: Trine or sextile aspect from malefic Ascendant lord to Ascendant mitigates potential harm.

rule: Avoid placing a malefic Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon in an angular house when malefics are also aspecting the Moon. Malefics should not be placed in angular houses when the Moon is afflicted.
judgment: Malefics in angles with an afflicted Moon amplify harm to the election.
notes: Latin text somewhat garbled; principle reconstructed from Arabic parallel.

rule: In all elections and horary questions: (1) the Lot of Fortune should not be cadent from the Moon's aspect or conjunction; (2) the Lord of the Lot of Fortune should receive attention; (3) if the Lot aspects both the Ascendant and the Moon, it need not be angular; (4) placing the Lord of the Ascendant in conjunction with the Lot is highly beneficial for wealth outcomes; (5) the Moon must never be placed in the 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th sign from the Lot of Fortune, as these positions are harmful.
judgment: Lot of Fortune well configured increases wealth outcomes; Moon in 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th from Lot is severely adverse.

rule: Place the Ascendant and Moon in signs of straight ascension for elections requiring ease and forward progress. Signs of crooked ascension indicate difficulty, complication, and slowness.
judgment: Straight ascension signs favor smooth outcomes; crooked ascension signs indicate obstacles and delays.
notes: A contrary attribution appears in a note referencing Dorotheus, who reportedly states the opposite; the text as extracted follows the primary rule given.

rule: In any election, the Ascendant and the fourth sign from it together signify what will happen to that election—the Ascendant indicating the beginning and the fourth indicating the end. The strength and weakness of benefics and malefics in these positions reveals how the matter will begin and conclude.
conditions: benefics and malefics in Ascendant and 4th house
judgment: Strong benefics in these positions indicate good beginnings and endings; strong malefics indicate adverse outcomes at beginning or end accordingly.
notes: Arabic version also includes the Lord of the fourth sign as a factor.

rule: When the Moon is unavoidably afflicted yet the matter cannot be postponed, the following procedure applies: remove the Moon from the Ascendant and place her in a cadent house, then place a benefic in the Ascendant and strengthen both the Ascendant and its Lord.
judgment: Sidelining the afflicted Moon while fortifying the Ascendant and its lord offers the best available outcome when an election cannot be postponed.

rule: For elections concerning the lending or borrowing of money: place the Moon in Leo, Pisces, Scorpio, Sagittarius, or Aquarius; Moon should be decreasing in light; both benefics (Jupiter and Venus) should be decreasing and aspecting the Moon or Ascendant; Mercury should be free from Mars; Moon should be joined to Jupiter or Mercury and free from all malefics; Mercury should not be in square aspect to malefics nor in bodily conjunction with them; benefics must not be cadent. Moon conjunct Mars at such a time brings labor, worry, and contention; Moon impeded by Saturn brings prolonged delay and distress before resolution.
judgment: Properly configured election produces successful loan or borrowing; afflictions from Mars or Saturn bring conflict or delay respectively.
notes: Dorotheus specifically warns against Moon in the first degree of Leo, Gemini, or Sagittarius, or those signs ascending, as particularly harmful for loans.

rule: To keep a financial transaction secret, place the Moon under the Sun's rays moving toward conjunction with a benefic after separating from the Sun. This makes the matter easier for the inceptor and keeps it from becoming public. If instead the Moon is emerging from combustion and moving toward Mars, the matter will become widely known and reach unwanted ears. Avoid placing the Moon at the Nodes or in the burnt path for such elections.
conditions: Moon under rays applying to benefic
Moon not at Nodes or burnt path
judgment: Moon under rays moving to benefic produces a secret transaction; Moon moving to Mars on exit from combustion makes it public.

rule: For elections initiating a partnership in goods or labor, the Moon should be free from malefics and joined to benefics, placed in common signs (to multiply the partnership's productivity), or in Leo or Taurus. Avoid signs of southern declination, especially Libra (due to the burnt path) and Aquarius. Reception of the Moon by trine or sextile from the benefic ensures an amicable dissolution of the partnership; square aspect brings quarrels at separation; opposition brings open conflict. Avoid malefics in angular houses.
conditions: Moon in common signs or Leo or Taurus
Moon received by benefic from trine or sextile
judgment: Benefic reception by trine or sextile ensures good partnership and peaceful separation; square or opposition reception produces discord at dissolution.

rule: In a partnership election: the Ascendant represents the inceptor (or the junior partner); the 7th house represents the other partner; the 10th house signifies the dealings between them and the abundance or scarcity of wealth; the 4th house reveals the outcome of the partnership.
judgment: Reading benefic/malefic placements in these four houses reveals the quality of the partnership and its eventual conclusion.

rule: In a partnership election, if the Lord of the Ascendant does not aspect the Ascendant, or the Lord of the Moon's domicile does not aspect the Moon, one partner will deceive the other and the matter will deteriorate at dissolution.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant not aspecting Ascendant
Lord of Moon's domicile not aspecting Moon
judgment: Absence of these aspects signals deception and worsening of the partnership, especially at its end.

rule: For elections involving investment or dispatching wealth to generate profit: adapt the Moon, Mercury, the Lord of the 2nd house, and the Lord of the 11th house degree; join Moon to Mercury; keep Mars cadent from both Moon and Mercury. If Mercury is retrograde, instead adapt Moon and the 11th house degree, keep Mercury cadent from Mars's rays, and ensure Mercury is not cadent from Venus or the Lord of the 11th. Mars and his light should always be cadent from Mercury and the Moon in such elections.
conditions: Mars cadent from Moon and Mercury
judgment: Properly configured election for investment produces profitable return; Mars's interference brings loss.

rule: For a purchase election, place the Lot of Fortune in a domicile of Jupiter, joined to benefics—this favors the buyer. If the Moon is in a sign of straight ascension, increasing in light and number, and joined to benefics, this favors the seller (the buyer is likely to lose on the purchase). Keep Mars cadent from Moon and Mercury, as Mars signifies dispute and difficulty in commercial transactions. The South Node should also be cadent from the Moon. For a sale election, place the Moon in her own exaltation or triplicity, separating from benefics and in aspect to malefics but not joined to them.
conditions: Lot of Fortune in Jupiter's domicile for buyer
Moon increasing in straight ascension signs for seller
Moon in exaltation or triplicity separating from benefics for seller
judgment: Election favoring buyer emphasizes Lot of Fortune and benefics; election favoring seller emphasizes Moon in dignity separating from benefics; Mars cadent protects both parties from dispute.

rule: For a building election: adapt the Moon, her Lord, the Ascendant and its Lord, the Lot of Fortune, and Mercury. Keep Mars cadent from all these significators. If Mars cannot be made cadent, strengthen Venus, give her authority over Mars, and join her to Mars by trine or sextile (Venus's friendship for Mars neutralizes his harm). Keep Saturn cadent from Venus, Mars, and the Moon when they mutually aspect each other from esteem. Moon should be increasing in light and number. Moon joined to Jupiter by square is better than opposition and signals a beautiful, completed structure. Avoid Moon with Saturn or the South Node, and avoid Saturn in the Ascendant or 4th house, as these signify delays, failure to complete, ongoing fears, illness, theft, and structural collapse for inhabitants. If Mars aspects the Moon and is ascending in the apogee portion of his epicycle, fire and collapse are feared; then Moon increasing in light is protective.
conditions: Mars cadent or neutralized by Venus
Moon free from Saturn and South Node
judgment: Properly configured building election yields a beautiful, completed, stable structure; Saturn or South Node with Moon or in angles brings danger to inhabitants and the building.

rule: In a building or property election, the Lord of the Moon's domicile must aspect the Moon, and the Lord of the Ascendant must aspect the Ascendant, and both must be free from malefics. If these aspects are absent, the owner will not remain in the property.
conditions: Lord of Moon's sign aspecting Moon
judgment: Mutual aspects of house lords to their respective factors keep the owner in the property; absence of these aspects drives the owner away.

rule: For an election to demolish or destroy a building: place Moon descending in her cycle, separating from malefics and joining benefics; the benefic should be oriental or ascending direct. Alternatively, join Moon to the Lord of her domicile by trine or sextile for easier demolition; square or opposition from that lord makes demolition more difficult.
conditions: Moon joining benefic oriental or ascending
Moon in trine or sextile to Lord of her domicile
judgment: Trine or sextile to Lord of Moon's domicile eases demolition; square or opposition makes it harder.

rule: For an election to purchase land or enter into a land-rental arrangement: place Saturn in his own exaltation, triplicity, or bound; have Jupiter in angular aspect to Saturn by trine; keep Mars cadent from both. Moon should be in the early part of the lunar month, aspecting Saturn by esteem and increasing in number, and also in aspect with Jupiter. If Jupiter's aspect to Saturn is unavailable, substitute Venus and also strengthen the watery signs with benefics (watery signs in such elections are superior to airy signs). Moon should be in her own exaltation or the Midheaven, with Lord of Ascendant aspecting her; Moon and Ascendant should be free from malefics and defects.
conditions: Jupiter or Venus in trine to Saturn
judgment: Election signifies populated, productive land with good yield; favorable for land acquisition and tenancy.

rule: For an election to divert a river or dig a well: Saturn should be oriental; Moon should be below the horizon in the 3rd or 5th house, free from malefics, received and fortunate. Avoid malefics in the Midheaven (risks collapse of the well or the river running dry). Place Saturn in the 11th house from the Ascendant; Moon should join a benefic in a fixed sign, with the benefic ascending in its epicycle. Jupiter is the preferred benefic. If Jupiter cannot be placed as described, placing Jupiter in the Midheaven maximizes the durability and stability of the water project.
conditions: Moon in 3rd or 5th below horizon, free from malefics
Moon joining benefic in fixed sign
judgment: Properly configured election produces a lasting, stable river course or well; malefic in Midheaven risks failure of the construction.

rule: For an election to plant trees: Moon should be in a fixed sign with the Lord of her domicile aspecting her from a watery sign. Ascendant should be fixed or common, and the Lord of the Ascendant should be ascending and oriental. The combination of oriental/occidental and ascending/descending of the Lord of the Ascendant governs the speed of sprouting and fruiting: ascending and oriental = fast sprout, fast fruit; ascending but not oriental = fast sprout, delayed fruit; oriental but descending = slow sprout, fast fruit; occidental and descending = both slow. Both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Moon's domicile must aspect their respective factors and be free from malefics and combustion.
conditions: Lord of Moon's sign in watery sign aspecting Moon
Lord of Ascendant orientation and course
judgment: Sprouting speed and fruiting speed governed by orientation (oriental/occidental) and course (ascending/descending) of Lord of Ascendant.

rule: For a sowing election: Ascendant should be a common sign; its Lord should be in a movable sign, aspecting the Lord of its own domicile, and free from malefics (malefic aspect to the Ascendant lord harms the seed). Moon must be increasing in light and number; a Moon under the rays and decreasing in number causes the seed to vanish without sprouting. Moon increasing in number but less than ideally configured produces thin sprouting proportional to what is sown.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant in movable sign aspecting its domicile lord
Moon increasing in light and number
judgment: Properly configured sowing election yields full crop; Moon under rays and decreasing in number destroys the seed entirely.

rule: For an election to conceive a male child: Ascendant and its Lord, Moon and Lord of the 5th house, should all be in masculine signs and in a masculine quadrant of the chart; only masculine planets should be placed in the Ascendant or 5th house. For a female child, use feminine signs and a feminine quadrant for these same significators. When significators are mixed between masculine and feminine signs, weigh the evidence and add in the Lord of the Hour and the planet receiving the Moon's disposition; the outcome follows whichever gender has greater testimony.
conditions: Ascendant, Ascendant lord, Moon, 5th lord in masculine or feminine signs and quadrant
Lord of Hour and Moon's dispositor as tiebreakers
judgment: Majority of significators in masculine indicators produces male child; feminine indicators produce female child.

rule: For an election to extract a deceased fetus: Moon should be decreasing in light, descending from the Midheaven toward the 7th house, aspecting benefics by trine or square and also receiving Mars's aspect. Best conditions: Moon and Ascendant in feminine signs of straight ascension; crooked signs should be avoided.
conditions: Ascendant in feminine signs of straight ascension
judgment: This configuration facilitates extraction; feminine signs of straight ascension provide the most favorable conditions.
notes: The Arabic may indicate the Moon should also be in southern ecliptical latitude (descending in belt).

rule: For an election to begin a child's education or apprenticeship: Moon should aspect Mercury and both should be free from malefics. Ascendant should be Gemini or Virgo. Mercury must be oriental and ascending—not descending, not retrograde, not at his first station, not in his own fall, and not otherwise impeded. The Lord of Mercury's domicile should also be free from affliction. Moon should not be descending and decreasing in light, as this slows the learning process. Lords of their domiciles should aspect them.
conditions: Mercury oriental and ascending, free from affliction
judgment: Properly elected chart for education produces swift and effective learning; Moon descending and decreasing slows the training.

rule: For an election to expel malevolent spirits, infestation, or phantasms from a place or person: avoid Moon or Ascendant in Leo, Cancer, Scorpio, or Aquarius. Place Moon in any other sign, separating from malefics and joining benefics.
conditions: Moon and Ascendant not in Leo, Cancer, Scorpio, or Aquarius
Moon separating from malefics and joining benefics
judgment: Avoiding the four prohibited signs and maintaining benefic configuration facilitates successful expulsion.

rule: For taking medicine for spasms, belly pain, or making a plaster: Moon or Ascendant should be in Libra or Scorpio with Moon in that sign, joined to benefics; no malefic should be in the Moon's angular houses. If a malefic must be present, it should be only by trine or sextile aspect, not opposition, not square, and not under the Sun's rays; otherwise pain and impediment result.
conditions: Moon or Ascendant in Libra or Scorpio
judgment: Properly configured election allows medicine to work; malefic in angular house or in square/opposition brings pain and complication.

rule: For treatments of the head and throat (including gargling and emetics): Ascendant and Moon should be in Aries or Taurus, Moon decreasing in light and joined to benefics. Beware the Sun in square or opposition aspect, especially in Aries, due to solar heat. For nasal treatments (inhalations, sneezing powders): Cancer, Leo, or Virgo should ascend, with Moon joined to benefics; avoid Moon joined to malefics, retrograde planets, or impeded planets.
conditions: Moon in Aries or Taurus, decreasing, joined to benefics
no square or opposition from Sun
for nasal: Cancer/Leo/Virgo ascending, Moon joined to benefics
judgment: Correct sign placement and benefic reception facilitates head and throat treatments; solar squares or opposition and malefic contact impede treatment.

rule: For curing ailments of the extremities (hands and feet): Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces should ascend, and the Moon should be in one of those signs, joined to benefics.
conditions: Ascendant and Moon in Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces
judgment: This configuration supports treatment of extremity conditions.

rule: For treating a chronic illness: Moon should be in her triplicity, with Taurus preferred (as an earthy sign associated with earth-related diseases). Moon should be free from malefics and benefics should be in the Moon's angular houses from Taurus. Avoid Moon joined to Saturn in particular, as this signifies prolongation of the illness.
conditions: Moon in her triplicity, preferably Taurus
judgment: Moon in triplicity with benefics in her angles facilitates recovery; Moon joined to Saturn prolongs the illness.

rule: According to Masha'allah: to treat conditions of the head, throat, or chest (upper body), elect when Moon is in Aries, Taurus, or Gemini. For the belly, lower abdomen, and navel area (middle body), elect when Moon is in Cancer, Leo, or Virgo. For the lower body including the anus and lower regions, elect when Moon is in Libra, Scorpio, or Sagittarius. For conditions from knees to feet, elect when Moon is in Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces. In all cases Moon should be joined to benefics, increasing in light and number.
conditions: Moon increasing and joined to benefics
judgment: Moon's sign should correspond to the body zone being treated for maximum effectiveness.

rule: An alternative body-zone system based on chart hemispheres: for conditions from the head to the navel, elect when the Moon is in the ascending hemisphere (from IC up through the Ascendant to the MC). For conditions from the navel to the feet, elect when Moon is in the descending hemisphere (from MC down through the 7th to the IC). A benefic in the Ascendant in either case indicates healing and recovery.
judgment: Moon in appropriate hemisphere for body zone, with benefic in Ascendant, produces healing.

rule: For elections involving cutting, surgery, scarification, or opening a vein: Moon should be increasing in light and number (except for cupping, where Moon should be decreasing). Jupiter should be above the horizon in the Ascendant, 11th, 10th, or 9th house; if this is impossible, Jupiter should at least aspect the Ascendant. Avoid Moon and Ascendant in earthy signs. Avoid the Nodes in conjunction or any relation with Mars. Avoid operating when Moon is newly emerged from combustion (within 12°), at the Full Moon, or when Mars is in the Ascendant. Saturn in the Ascendant at the time of cutting is also forbidden, unless Moon is increasing in the early lunar month. If any of these conditions are violated, the cut will putrefy and the intervention will not benefit the patient. Avoid cutting a vein or extracting a tooth when Moon is in a movable or common sign closely configured with malefics, unless Moon is free from malefics or a strong benefic is with Moon or aspecting her by trine or sextile.
conditions: Jupiter above horizon or aspecting Ascendant
no Mars or Saturn in Ascendant
Moon not in movable or common sign with malefics for vein-cutting or tooth extraction
judgment: Proper configuration permits successful surgical intervention; violations lead to putrefaction and ineffective treatment.
notes: The Arabic differs slightly; the ninth house for Jupiter may be a Latin addition.

rule: For surgeries or procedures on the eye: Moon should be increasing in light and number, free from Mars. If Mars aspects, the procedure should be abandoned. If Saturn aspects, the impact is lessened when Moon is increasing at the start of the lunar month. After the Full Moon, Moon may be configured to Mars by trine with Moon joined to a benefic. Never strengthen Mars in any eye treatment. The Moon and Ascendant should not be in earthy signs for such procedures.
conditions: Moon increasing and free from Mars
Saturn's aspect less harmful when Moon increasing at lunar start
after Full Moon: Moon in trine to Mars with benefic
judgment: Mars-free Moon in eye surgery election produces good outcome; Mars aspecting Moon signals the procedure should be halted.
notes: All sages agree on Mars's impediment to head-related treatments.
