Storm winds are generated by interaction between hot cloud masses and cold air, and by the mechanical displacement of air by moving cloud banks. Whirlwinds result from rotational wind patterns analogous to cloud vortices.
judgment: Wind direction and quality are not fixed to cardinal directions by an absolute rule; rather, they reflect the nature of the terrain and air mass over which the wind has most recently traveled. The same cardinal direction may produce different wind qualities in different geographic regions. Lightning and thunder accompany the violent separation of hot and cold air within storm clouds; lightning is perceived before thunder because visual perception requires no travel time while sound propagates at a finite speed proportional to distance.
notes: Māshā'allāh explicitly disagrees with earlier authorities who assigned fixed elemental qualities to the four cardinal winds, arguing that regional variation makes their assignments unreliable outside their own locales.

rule: Rain forms when solar evaporation lifts water vapor from seas and wet surfaces into the atmosphere, where it meets cold air, condenses into clouds, and eventually falls. When opposing cold and hot air masses interact violently within a cloud, freezing occurs on the cold-dominated edges, producing snow and hail; the explosive release of thermal pressure from the collision of these contraries generates thunder and lightning. Hail acquires a rounded shape because it partially melts and re-freezes during its fall. Rain events are most frequent and intense in spring and autumn, because these seasons produce the sharpest contrast between residual heat and advancing cold. Summer rain, when it occurs, is typically more violent due to the greater thermal contrast available.
conditions: vapor meeting cold vs hot air
judgment: The intensity of precipitation, lightning, and thunder is proportional to the degree of thermal contrariety within the cloud system. Greatest storm activity occurs at seasonal transitions (spring, autumn). Snow and hail are products of the same process as rain but with freezing temperatures dominating within the cloud.
notes: Māshā'allāh notes the resemblance to Aristotelian meteorological doctrine without naming Aristotle directly.

rule: Plant germination and growth are driven by solar heat acting on a seed's internal moisture, causing it to expand and draw additional moisture and fine nutriments upward from the surrounding soil. The Sun's lifting action on moisture is the primary motor; the seed responds by extending roots downward to access further moisture and by producing upward growth. The form of the mature plant is entirely contained within the seed from the outset and is simply actualized by the interaction of solar heat and terrestrial moisture. Every plant form is thus predetermined by the structure of its seed.
judgment: Plant growth is not random but is the predetermined unfolding of a form already present in the seed, facilitated by solar heat and soil moisture. Plants found growing wild in uninhabited locations confirm that the process requires no human intervention, only the appropriate combination of seed, heat, and moisture.
notes: The philosophical concept invoked is the Aristotelian vegetative soul, credited to 'the philosophers' without further specification.

rule: When any celestial body passes between the observer and a more distant body, the nearer body occults the farther one. The Moon, being closest to Earth, can occult planets and fixed stars as she passes in front of them. Similarly, planets can occult fixed stars when they come between the star and the observer. The nearer the occulting body to Earth relative to its size, the greater the fraction of the occulted body it can hide.
conditions: relative distances of bodies from Earth
alignment of bodies along line of sight
judgment: Occultation of a distant body by a nearer one is complete when the nearer body's angular diameter exceeds the more distant body's, and the centers are aligned. Partial occultation results from imperfect alignment. The Moon is the most frequent occultor of other bodies due to her proximity and apparent size.

rule: The celestial sphere is structured by three fundamental great circles: (1) the circle of east and west (celestial equator), which passes through the east point, zenith, west point, and nadir, and along which the Sun moves when day and night are equal; (2) the circle of south and north (meridian), passing through the north pole, zenith, south pole, and nadir; (3) the circle of the horizon, passing through east, south, west, and north. These three circles intersect to define six cardinal points on the sphere's surface (east, zenith, west, nadir, north pole, south pole) plus a seventh point at the Earth's center, for a total of seven defining points. Three corresponding chords connect opposite pairs of these points through the Earth's center. Mastery of these three circles, three chords, and seven points constitutes a sufficient geometric foundation for understanding the celestial sphere.
judgment: All celestial risings, settings, and culminations are derivable from the relationships among these three circles. The intersection of the equator circle with the horizon defines the east and west points exactly. The meridian defines the culmination points (zenith and nadir). Deviation of a body from the equator circle indicates its latitude north or south.
notes: This section is primarily geometrical and foundational; it does not in itself generate predictive judgments but is presented as the prerequisite framework for all positional astronomy.

rule: Cast a chart for the exact moment the Sun enters 0° Aries. Identify the planet that governs or rules that chart. The nature of that ruling planet determines the general character of the year for the world.
conditions: planet ruling the Ascendant of the Aries ingress chart
whether that planet is benefic or malefic or afflicted
judgment: A benefic ruler indicates a favorable and productive year; a malefic or afflicted ruler indicates deterioration and harm in worldly conditions.
notes: The same procedure is applied recursively to each seasonal quarter and to each month of the year.

rule: The technique used for the annual Aries ingress—erecting a chart and examining its ruler—is replicated for each of the four seasonal quarter-ingresses and for each monthly ingress throughout the year.
judgment: Each sub-period's quality (favorable or harmful) is judged by the nature and condition of the ruler of that sub-period's ingress chart.

rule: When multiple planets gather in signs of the same elemental triplicity at the time of an ingress or revolution, the dominant element of those signs manifests as a corresponding meteorological condition.
conditions: concentration of planets in watery signs
judgment: Watery sign concentration signals excessive rainfall; fiery sign concentration signals intense heat and drought or crop failure; airy sign concentration signals strong winds; earthy sign concentration signals frost and snowfall.

rule: When Mars and Saturn jointly dominate an ingress chart and no benefic planet casts an aspect to either of them, the period signified by that chart is prone to widespread warfare and severe worldly devastation.
conditions: Mars and Saturn ruling or prominent in the ingress chart
absence of any benefic aspect to Mars or Saturn
judgment: Signifies large-scale armed conflict and serious harm to the world's population or infrastructure.

rule: If Mars governs the summer quarter ingress and is located in one of the two signs that Mercury rules, that quarter will be marked by excessive rainfall and epidemic disease.
conditions: Mars as lord of the summer quarter ingress chart
Mars positioned in Gemini or Virgo
judgment: Indicates unusual rains and widespread pestilence during the summer season.

rule: The solar phase-orientation of the heavy planets as a group shapes weather conditions: when all of them are oriental, dryness prevails; when all are occidental, winter brings abundant rain and summer air is well-tempered; when they are emerging from combustion, winter weather is moderate but summer becomes excessively dry.
conditions: superior planets at heliacal rising / emerging from beams
judgment: Oriental: drought. Occidental: wet winters, mild summers. Emerging from beams: mild winters, very dry summers.
notes: The source text is ambiguous about the precise definition of oriental and occidental phases here; the translator suggests oriental may span from heliacal rising to first station, and occidental from second station to heliacal setting.

rule: When the heavy planets occupy signs associated with northern celestial latitude (northern signs), dryness and agricultural sterility are signified for the region under consideration; when they occupy southern signs, abundant rainfall is signified.
judgment: Northern sign placement: dryness and infertility. Southern sign placement: excess rain.
notes: Text is ambiguous about how to operationalize 'nearness' versus 'distance' from a region; the northern/southern sign interpretation is the one given in the source.

rule: Determine whether the heavy planets occupy hot or cold signs. Their elemental sign quality modifies expected seasonal temperatures.
judgment: Hot signs: amplified summer heat and moderated winter cold. Cold signs: intensified winter cold and moderated summer heat.

rule: For any eclipse (solar or lunar), erect a chart for the midpoint of the eclipse and identify the planet ruling the Ascendant of that chart. Assess whether that ruler is a benefic or malefic and whether it is afflicted.
conditions: Ascendant of the eclipse's midpoint chart
ruling planet's essential nature and condition
judgment: A benefic ruler indicates favorable outcomes; a malefic ruler indicates harm and disruption for the territory affected.
notes: The source also references assessing which planets 'conquer' the eclipse figure more broadly, not only the Ascendant ruler.

rule: The elemental character of the sign in which a lunar eclipse falls modifies the weather outcome, further conditioned by the actual season at the time of the eclipse.
conditions: season of the eclipse (summer or winter)
judgment: Eclipse in cold signs during winter: intensified cold. Eclipse in watery signs during winter: heavy rains. Either placement during summer: air becomes temperate rather than extreme.

rule: When benefic planets aspect the Moon at the time of a lunar eclipse and receive her, the negative significations of the eclipse are moderated and redirected toward beneficial outcomes in domains those benefics rule.
conditions: benefic planets aspecting the Moon during a lunar eclipse
reception of the Moon by those benefics
judgment: Eclipse harms are reduced; outcomes shift toward the positive significations of the aspecting and receiving benefics.

rule: The elemental triplicity of the sign in which a solar eclipse occurs shapes the category of harm it delivers. The eclipse always indicates significant negative events scaled to the magnitude of the eclipse itself.
conditions: malefic planets dominating the eclipse figure
judgment: Fiery sign eclipse: downfall of rulers and wealthy persons, drought, famine. Watery sign eclipse: flooding rains and damage from water. Malefic dominance amplifies all harms. Benefic aspect reduces but does not eliminate harm.
notes: The text specifies that a solar eclipse only becomes astrologically significant when the obscuration reaches at least a square of the Sun's body (roughly 90° arc of obscuration implied, though context suggests magnitude of coverage).

rule: When an eclipse occurs involving a luminary that serves as the hyleg or alcocoden in a nativity, that individual faces serious physical danger or grave illness from the eclipse.
conditions: Sun or Moon as natal hyleg or alcocoden
real-time eclipse falls on or involves that luminary
absence of benefic aspect to the eclipse or luminary
judgment: Significant personal danger or severe illness for the native whose hyleg or alcocoden is eclipsed; benefic aspects mitigate the threat.
notes: The text does not specify whether the mitigating benefic aspects are natal or transiting, or whether they are to the natal luminary position or to the degree of the eclipse.

rule: For any planetary conjunction relevant to mundane forecasting, erect a chart for the moment of exact conjunction and identify the planet dominating or ruling that figure. The nature of that dominant planet and the elemental quality of the sign of the conjunction together determine the type and quality of events signified.
conditions: nature of the planet ruling or conquering the conjunction chart
elemental quality of the sign the conjunction occurs in
judgment: Benefic dominance: favorable outcomes in the domain of the sign. Malefic dominance: harmful outcomes in that domain. Sign element specifies the category of effect (weather, crops, etc.). Fixed signs: long-lasting effects. Movable signs: brief or quickly-passing effects. Common signs: moderate duration.

rule: When planets conjoin in feminine signs, harm falls particularly on female animals and women; when the conjunction is in masculine signs, male animals and men are correspondingly affected.
conditions: conjunction of planets in masculine or feminine signs
judgment: Sign gender specifies which sex of animate beings bears the brunt of the signified affliction.

rule: When all three superior planets conjoin within the same term or face and the Sun aspects that grouping, the event signifies upheaval or transformation of religious orders and governmental structures. If one of the inferior planets also participates, the effects are amplified further.
conditions: Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars in the same term or face
possible participation of an inferior planet
judgment: Destruction or transformation of established religions or dynasties, emergence of prophetic figures, large-scale geopolitical change, and exceptional celestial or earthly phenomena. The strongest planet in the grouping determines whether the outcome is broadly fortunate or calamitous.
notes: The text identifies this as the 'greatest conjunction.' The source notes this may relate to the climacteric conjunction in early Aries occurring on an approximately 960-year cycle.

rule: Whether the superior planets occupy their exaltations or their fall signs at the time of their conjunction modifies the quality of the outcomes.
conditions: superior planets conjoining in their exaltation signs
superior planets conjoining in their fall signs
judgment: Exaltation conjunction: favorable weather, good conditions generally, but also increased military activity and wondrous events. Fall conjunction: damage, drought, agricultural failure, and famine, unless the planets are otherwise received or supported.

rule: The Saturn-Jupiter conjunction is classified as the 'greater conjunction' among paired superior-planet conjunctions. Its effects on kingdoms and religions are assessed by the chart of the conjunction moment, the ruling planet of that chart, and the relative strength of Saturn versus Jupiter within it.
conditions: Jupiter stronger than Saturn in the conjunction chart
conjunction falling in one of the four angles of the ingress chart
sign of the conjunction and its lord's condition
judgment: Jupiter dominant: good fortune signified. Saturn dominant: tribulation and harm. Conjunction angular (especially on the MC): emergence of a king or prophet originating from the direction associated with that sign; fortunate sign and lord = the figure's triumph; afflicted sign and lord = the figure's downfall.
notes: The text states that the conjunction's full effects unfold over a span of years counted from the conjunction; external timing techniques (referenced as described elsewhere) determine when specific events manifest.

rule: The elemental triplicity of the sign holding the Saturn-Jupiter conjunction specifies the type of worldly harm or benefit produced.
conditions: Saturn-Jupiter conjunction in fire or air signs
judgment: Fire or air: dryness, agricultural sterility, and intensified cold. Earth: destruction of crops and famine. Water: excessive rain and pestilence (when planets are afflicted); when planets are in favorable condition, all significations improve; when afflicted, all worsen.

rule: The Saturn-Mars conjunction is designated the 'middle conjunction.' Its chart ruler determines general quality; sign placement and angularity in the ingress chart further specify effects.
conditions: ruling planet of the Saturn-Mars conjunction chart benefic or malefic
conjunction on an angle of the ingress chart
benefic or malefic aspects to the conjunction
judgment: Human signs: widespread disease among people. Angular placement: conflict between rulers or wealthy elites, warfare lasting until the next Saturn-Mars conjunction. Fire: drought and sterility. Air: winds. Water: heavy rain. Earth: frost, snow, cold. Benefic aspects reduce harm; malefic aspects intensify it.

rule: The Jupiter-Mars conjunction is the 'lesser conjunction.' Its primary domains are rainfall, atmospheric disruption, and political unrest. Angularity in the annual ingress chart intensifies its political effects.
conditions: ruling planet of the Jupiter-Mars conjunction chart
conjunction falling on an angle of the ingress chart
judgment: Governs rains, clouds, and corrupted air as well as warfare. Angular placement in the ingress: agitation and conflict among rulers, unless benefics aspect.

rule: When a benefic and a malefic planet are in conjunction, the outcome follows the nature of whichever planet is the stronger of the two. When two malefics conjoin, harmful outcomes dominate unless the planet ruling or conquering the conjunction figure is a benefic.
conditions: one benefic and one malefic in conjunction: compare their relative strength
two malefics in conjunction: identify the chart's ruling planet
judgment: Stronger party's nature prevails in the mixed conjunction. In a double-malefic conjunction, evil predominates; a benefic chart ruler can partially counteract this.

rule: The designation of a planet's effect as beneficial or harmful is not absolute but must be evaluated relative to the climatic baseline of the region under examination. A planetary indication that brings excess cold is damaging to a cold region but merely tempering to a hot region, and vice versa.
conditions: planetary signification of cold excess applied to a cold-climate region vs. a hot-climate region
planetary signification of heat excess applied to corresponding regions
judgment: The same planetary indication is beneficial where it counteracts climatic extremes and harmful where it compounds them. Regional context is mandatory for correct judgment.

rule: Each of the twelve signs belongs simultaneously to one elemental triplicity, one modality group, and one gender/sect category. These classifications operate as a grid of essential sign qualities used in all branches of judgment.
conditions: fire signs: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius — hot, masculine, diurnal
earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn — cold, feminine, nocturnal
air signs: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius — hot, masculine, diurnal
water signs: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces — cold, feminine, nocturnal
movable signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn
fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius
common/bicorporeal signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces
judgment: These inherent qualities of signs determine what type of weather, event, or outcome their occupying planets will manifest, and how long those effects will last (fixed = enduring, movable = brief, common = moderate).
notes: The source presents two variant readings on the elemental heat/cold assignment: one version makes fire and air hot and earth and water cold; another version specifies fire hot, water cold, earth cold, air hot — these are consistent and both appear in the text.

rule: At the Sun's ingress into Scorpio, examine Venus's phase relative to the Sun. Her eastern or western position relative to the Sun indicates whether the first or second half of the winter season will receive greater precipitation.
conditions: Venus oriental (morning rising) = first half of winter has less rain, second half more
Venus occidental (western, setting after Sun) = first half of winter has more rain
judgment: Determines the relative distribution of rainfall between early and late portions of the winter season.
notes: Translator footnote suggests the text may contain an error regarding 'in front of' versus 'following' the Sun for the occidental position. The simile in the source is rhetorical; only the positional rule is extracted.

rule: When Venus and the Sun occupy the same sign simultaneously, the month of their co-presence or conjunction tends to bring increased precipitation.
conditions: Venus conjunct or co-present with the Sun in same sign
judgment: Increased rainfall in the month of the conjunction.

rule: Cast a chart for the exact moment the Sun reaches the first degree of Aries. Identify the ascendant degree and determine which planet holds dignity (specifically bound/term rulership) over that degree. That planet functions as the annual lord (lord of the year) for rainfall judgments.
conditions: Chart cast for Sun's entry into 0° Aries
Bound ruler of ascendant degree = lord of the year
judgment: Identifies the primary significator governing precipitation for the annual period.
notes: The text uses 'owner of the part of the degree of the rising' which the translator's footnote equates to a dignity, here taken as the bound/term lord of the ascending degree. The four angular houses (stakes) are also to be noted.

rule: After identifying the annual lord, examine whether it forms an application or co-presence with Venus or Mercury. Additionally, assess whether the ascendant falls in a water sign, and whether Venus, the Moon, and Mercury are placed in water signs.
conditions: Lord of year applies to or is co-present with Venus or Mercury
Venus, Moon, Mercury in water signs
Moon applying to Venus or Mercury without affliction by malefics
judgment: Confluence of these indicators signifies abundant rainfall for the year.

rule: When Mercury is harmed by Mars or is combust (under the rays of the Sun), and the Moon applies to Mercury, the rainfall pattern for the year shows scarcity early, increase in the middle portion, and the precipitation that does occur is accompanied by thunder, lightning, obstructive conditions, and strong winds.
conditions: Mercury afflicted by Mars OR Mercury combust
judgment: Rain scarce in first part of year, increasing in the middle; stormy atmospheric conditions throughout.

rule: When Venus is afflicted by Mars or is combust, rainfall is reduced across the entire year.
conditions: Venus applying to Mars OR Venus combust
judgment: Diminished precipitation throughout the annual period.

rule: When Mercury is in connection with Saturn and the Moon applies to either Mercury or Saturn, rainfall increases in the early portion of the year with elevated atmospheric moisture and obstructive weather conditions.
conditions: Moon applying to Mercury or Saturn
judgment: More rain in the first part of the year; increased humidity and difficult atmospheric conditions.

rule: When Jupiter is placed in a water sign and Venus and the Moon both apply to Jupiter, this configuration paradoxically indicates reduced rainfall for the year.
judgment: Less rain than expected despite beneficial planet in a water sign.
notes: This is a counterintuitive result; Jupiter in water signs combined with benefic applications reduces rather than increases rain. No explicit explanation is provided in the text.

rule: When the annual lord is afflicted by Mars, or Mars occupies the same sign as the annual lord, precipitation is reduced in both the early and late portions of the year, and the period is marked by hardship.
conditions: Lord of year afflicted by Mars OR Mars co-present with lord of year in same sign
judgment: Rainfall scarcity in first and last portions of the year; general difficulty.

rule: When the annual lord is co-present with Venus, but the Moon applies to Mars, cloud cover and wind activity increase while actual rainfall decreases.
conditions: Lord of year co-present with Venus in a sign
judgment: Increased clouds and winds; reduced precipitation.

rule: When the annual lord and Venus share an air sign, and the Moon applies to Mars, the atmosphere becomes polluted or degraded by moisture that is not rainfall (e.g., humidity, damp air).
conditions: Lord of year and Venus co-present in an air sign
judgment: Atmospheric corruption through non-rain moisture rather than precipitation.

rule: When Venus applies to Saturn, or the Moon applies to Saturn, fog and ground-level moisture increase to an extent resembling rain but without actual precipitation, creating a burden of dampness on the earth.
conditions: Venus applying to Saturn OR Moon applying to Saturn
judgment: Heavy fog and non-rain surface moisture; earth burdened by dampness without rainfall.

rule: When Mercury serves as the annual lord and is afflicted, precipitation becomes erratic—alternately scarce and present—with atmospheric corruption from wind and cloud activity.
judgment: Variable, unreliable rainfall; corrupt atmospheric conditions with winds and clouds.

rule: When Jupiter is the annual lord and is afflicted by a malefic, rainfall diminishes, but the atmosphere does not suffer the same degree of corruption (wind, storms) as it does when Mercury is the afflicted annual lord.
judgment: Reduced rainfall without severe atmospheric disturbance.
notes: Explicitly contrasted with the Mercury-as-lord-of-year afflicted scenario, which produces worse atmospheric corruption.

rule: When Venus is both the annual lord and is afflicted by Mars while also combust, fog increases and surface moisture comes from sources other than rainfall.
judgment: Increased fog; moisture on the ground is not from rain.

rule: When Mars is the annual lord, overall moisture, rainfall, and cloud cover are all diminished.
judgment: General reduction in moisture, rain, and clouds for the year.

rule: When Saturn is the annual lord, rainfall is reduced while fog increases.
judgment: Less rain, more fog.

rule: The Moon, Venus, and Mercury are the primary planetary indicators of rainfall abundance and scarcity through their connections with benefics and malefics. The Sun, Mars, and Saturn function as inhibitors of precipitation, with the exception that Saturn placed in a rain-producing sign may shift to a rain-indicating role.
conditions: Saturn in a rainy sign = exception, may indicate rain
judgment: Framework for identifying which planets support and which suppress rainfall in any annual or periodic chart.
notes: Saturn's dual role (normally inhibitor, but rain-positive in certain signs) is explicitly noted as an exception.

rule: Cast charts for the Sun's entry into Libra and Capricorn in addition to the Aries ingress. For each quarterly chart, record the ascendant, the four angular houses, and assess the positions and applications of Venus, Mercury, the Moon, and Mars. Apply the same interpretive procedures used for the annual chart to forecast precipitation for that quarter's period.
conditions: Sun ingress Libra = chart covers autumn to Capricorn ingress
Sun ingress Capricorn = chart covers winter quarter
Examine Venus, Mercury, Moon positions and their applications
Examine Mars placement and its connections in each quarter
judgment: Quarterly rainfall forecast including rain, clouds, fog, and wind conditions for each seasonal segment.
notes: The text indicates the Aries ingress procedures are explicitly referenced as the model for quarterly analysis.

rule: Erect a chart for the exact moment of each lunation—both the Sun-Moon conjunction (New Moon) and the moment the Moon reaches the seventh sign from the Sun (Full Moon/prevention). Evaluate this chart using the same framework as the annual and quarterly ingress charts to forecast conditions for that lunar half-month.
conditions: Chart cast for exact New Moon (Sun-Moon conjunction within one degree)
Chart cast for Full Moon (Moon in seventh sign from Sun, reaching Sun's degree)
Half-month chart governs its own period
judgment: Identifies rainfall prospects for each half of the lunar month.
notes: The translator's footnote clarifies 'reception' means the Full Moon or prevention here, not a dignity-based reception. The text appears to equate the monthly ingress procedure with the half-month lunation procedure.

rule: In a lunation chart, if the Moon applies to Venus or Mercury, precipitation is expected during that month. For pinpointing the specific day of rain, observe when the Moon reaches an angular position (stake) while applying to Venus or Mercury.
conditions: Moon applying to Venus OR Moon applying to Mercury in lunation chart
For day-specific timing: Moon at an angle while applying to Venus or Mercury
judgment: Rain occurs in that month; exact day identified when Moon is angular and applying to Venus or Mercury.

rule: When the Moon applies to Mars at the moment of the New Moon conjunction, the first half of the lunar month features increased thunder, lightning, and wind with reduced rainfall, continuing until the Full Moon (prevention). The New Moon chart does not serve as a valid foundation for that half-month's forecast.
conditions: Moon applying to Mars at New Moon conjunction
Condition applies through the first half of the lunar month until Full Moon
judgment: Stormy conditions with thunder, lightning, and wind; diminished rainfall in first half of lunar month; New Moon chart invalidated as a root chart for that period.
notes: The meaning of 'no root in that half' is flagged as ambiguous by the translator. Possibly means the New Moon chart loses its authority as a base chart for that half-month period.

rule: When the Moon applies to benefic planets immediately after separating from the Sun at the New Moon, the second half of the lunar month (after the Full Moon/prevention) tends to bring abundant rainfall.
conditions: Moon applies to benefics upon separation from Sun at New Moon
judgment: Increased precipitation in the second half of the lunar month.

rule: When the Moon separates from the conjunction or Full Moon and applies to Saturn, and Venus simultaneously applies to Saturn while Saturn is in a rain-producing sign, rainfall increases during that lunation period. This does not apply if Saturn is in a fire sign.
conditions: Moon separating from New or Full Moon, applying to Saturn
Saturn in a rainy sign (not a fire sign)
judgment: Increased rainfall during the lunation period.
notes: Saturn's placement in a fire sign nullifies this rain-positive interpretation, consistent with the annual chart rule about Saturn as an exception.

rule: When Mars is in application to Saturn in a lunation chart, cloud cover and wind increase while rainfall is scarce. The atmosphere acquires moisture only from what is already present rather than from new precipitation.
conditions: Mars applying to Saturn in a lunation chart
judgment: Increased clouds and winds; rain scarcity; atmospheric moisture stagnant rather than renewed by precipitation.

rule: To forecast rain on a specific day within a half-month period, observe when the Moon enters an angular house (stake) and simultaneously applies to Mercury or Venus, or to planets that were connected with the Moon at the New Moon, while the Moon is in a water sign. This indicates rainfall on that day.
conditions: Moon applying to Mercury or Venus OR applying to planets that connected with Moon at New Moon
judgment: Rain falls on that specific day.

rule: The signs designated as rain-producing for meteorological forecasting purposes are Cancer, Scorpio, Aquarius, and Pisces. Venus and the Moon are identified as the most powerful planetary indicators of rainfall.
conditions: Planet classification: Venus and Moon = strongest rain indicators
judgment: Reference framework for identifying favorable rain conditions based on sign placement.
notes: Aquarius is included despite being an air sign, consistent with its water-bearer symbolism in traditional meteorological astrology.

rule: When Venus occupies a rainy sign and is in the first or middle portion of that sign, and the Moon transits through rainy signs while applying to Venus, rain is indicated for that day in significant quantity. If Venus or the relevant planet is in the final portion of the sign at the time of the Moon's conjunction, rain still occurs but in lesser quantity.
conditions: Venus in a rainy sign in first or middle decanate/portion
Moon transiting rainy signs, applying to Venus
If planet in final portion of sign: rain indicated but reduced in quantity
judgment: Heavy rain when Venus in early or middle portion of sign; lighter rain when in final portion.
notes: The translator notes ambiguity about which planet must be in the last portion of the sign; since the Moon must be in the same degree to conjoin, all relevant planets would effectively be in the same sign portion.

rule: When both Venus and Mercury are in rainy signs and the Moon transits rainy signs while applying to either of them, heavy and sustained rainfall is indicated for that day.
conditions: Moon in a rainy sign applying to Venus or Mercury
judgment: Prolonged and abundant rainfall on that day.

rule: When the Moon and Venus are both in rainy signs but Mercury is not in a rainy sign, rain is still indicated, though the full triple combination is stronger.
judgment: Rain indicated, though not as strong as when all three are in rainy signs.

rule: When the Moon and Mercury are both approaching or in rainy signs but Venus is not in a rainy sign, rain is still indicated.
conditions: Moon in or entering rainy sign
Mercury in or entering rainy sign
Venus not in a rainy sign
judgment: Rain indicated even without Venus in a rainy sign.

rule: When the Moon is in a rainy sign and applies to both Venus and Mercury, or one of them is in the same sign as the Moon, continuous rainfall is indicated lasting as long as the Moon remains in that sign.
conditions: Moon applying to both Venus and Mercury OR one of them co-present in Moon's sign
judgment: Sustained, continuous rainfall for the duration of the Moon's sign transit.

rule: When Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are free from malefic application and no malefic occupies the same sign as any of them, rainfall is indicated for that day. If any of them applies to a malefic or a malefic is co-present, rain is withheld.
conditions: Venus, Mercury, Moon: no application to malefics
Venus, Mercury, Moon: no malefic co-present in their signs
judgment: Rain falls when all three are free from malefic contact; rain is suppressed when any malefic connection exists.

rule: The entry of Venus, Mercury, or the Moon into a rainy sign on a given day serves as an independent indicator of rainfall for that day.
conditions: Venus OR Mercury OR Moon ingresses into a rainy sign
judgment: Rain on the day of the ingress into the rainy sign.

rule: When either Venus or Mercury is in Capricorn and the Moon is simultaneously in Taurus, Cancer, or Pisces, rainfall is indicated for that day.
conditions: Moon in Taurus, Cancer, or Pisces
judgment: Rain on that day.
notes: Capricorn is an earth sign, not a designated rainy sign, yet this specific combination is given as a rain indicator. This may reflect Capricorn's connection to Saturn and cold/moist conditions.

rule: When the Moon is in Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn and applies to Venus or Mercury by reception, rain is indicated for that day.
conditions: Moon in Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn
Moon applying to Venus or Mercury by reception
judgment: Rain on that day.
notes: 'Reception' here likely refers to the Moon applying to a planet that has dignity in the Moon's current sign, though context in other parts of the chapter uses 'reception' for the Full Moon. The term may carry both meanings in this text.

rule: A particularly strong rain indication arises when the Moon is co-present with the South Node (Tail of the Dragon) in a sign, specifically when the Moon is in Taurus while separating from Saturn, and Venus and Mars are both in Aquarius, while Mercury is in Pisces or Capricorn.
judgment: Strongest possible indication of rainfall on that day.
notes: This is the most specific multi-factor configuration in the chapter. The combination of the South Node with the Moon as a rain intensifier is noteworthy and may reflect a broader principle about nodal involvement amplifying lunar moisture indications.

rule: When Saturn and the Moon are in mutual connection, the direction of each body's motion determines both the occurrence and duration of precipitation. If the Moon is slowing or stationary while Saturn is also stationary, short-duration rain results. If Saturn is slowing while the Moon is gaining speed in zodiacal motion, rain occurs in that period, with particular strength when Saturn occupies Cancer and the Moon occupies Capricorn.
judgment: Short-duration rain when Moon is slowing and Saturn stationary; rain of immediate onset when Saturn slows and Moon accelerates; greatest rainfall when one ascends and the other descends with Moon increasing in speed.
notes: The text uses 'descending' and 'ascending' vocabulary that the translator notes may refer to slowing and speeding in zodiacal motion rather than latitude; some ambiguity remains.

rule: Placement of the South Node in Aquarius correlates with atmospheric obscurity, cold condensation, snowfall, and reduced rainfall, with the snow period potentially extending up to approximately six days or longer.
judgment: Reduced rain, increased snow and cold, prolonged atmospheric obscurity lasting roughly six days or more.

rule: Saturn's occupation of signs where he has essential dignity or a sympathetic water-related connection to the Moon activates precipitation significations. Specifically, Saturn in Cancer combined with Moon in Capricorn, Pisces, or Scorpio signifies rainfall. Saturn in Libra (his exaltation) or Aquarius (his domicile) indicates sustained rain and heavy snow. Saturn in Aquarius with Moon in Leo, with one ascending and the other descending, indicates abundant water.
judgment: Rain and water abundance when Saturn is in dignity signs and Moon occupies the corresponding opposite or water signs; absence of rain when Saturn is in Aries, Taurus, or Gemini where his nature is not reinforced.
notes: Text specifies that Saturn in Aries, Taurus, or Gemini produces no rain because his nature is not strengthened there.

rule: When Saturn is in Aquarius and the Moon is in Leo and both bodies are simultaneously ascending, the result is strong hot winds accompanied by obscurity; rainfall occurs only while both remain in this configuration and ceases once they begin to descend, after which wind dominates.
judgment: Strong hot winds with atmospheric obscurity; rain present only during the ascending phase, replaced by wind after.

rule: When Venus is occidental of the Sun and descending simultaneously with the Moon being in a configuration described for rain, Venus adds signification of multiple winds, dew, and their persistence.
judgment: Increased winds, dew, and prolonged moisture.
notes: The translator flags grammatical ambiguity in the source Latin; meaning is somewhat uncertain.

rule: Saturn in retrograde motion combined with the Moon moving at reduced speed diminishes the quantity of rainfall from what would otherwise be expected.
judgment: Reduced rainfall volume.

rule: Rainfall patterns differ by geographic zone in relation to the Sun's degree position. In elevated northern regions (third climatic zone), rain accumulates from the Sun's entry into the nineteenth degree of Taurus. From that degree through the nineteenth degree of Scorpio, rainfall is multiplied in southern regions and those near the equator. Separate judgments apply to the first climatic zone.
judgment: Zone-specific rainfall abundance tied to the Sun's zodiacal position across the Taurus-Scorpio axis.
notes: CCAG reads 'seventh' for the clime but the translator notes the text itself specifies third; geographic names in the original are partially unidentified.

rule: The Aries and Libra ingresses serve as root charts for annual rain assessment. In the period of roughly ten days following the equinox, the positions of rain-significant planets are examined. Venus conjunct the Sun, and Venus subsequently conjoining the Moon, or certain planets in lunar hour positions, constitutes a rain indicator. The Moon holds the strongest rain signification due to her moist nature.
judgment: Rain signified; Moon's indication outweighs other planets.
notes: The translator notes this sentence suffered in manuscript transmission; some bracketed text is conjectural.

rule: Any planet positioned at the nineteenth degree of Taurus constitutes a rain indicator, though the strength of that indication is less than that of the Moon, which has a special relationship to Saturn's domain.
judgment: Rain signified, with lesser strength than a Lunar indication at that degree.

rule: At the Sun's entry into Aries (or the nineteenth degree of Scorpio), examine the domicile lords of the planets and whether they aspect that degree; if the Moon also supports them, abundant rain is signified for the year. If the Moon is decreasing in speed and does not aspect the lord of the Midheaven of the relevant configuration or any planet, rain is still indicated.
judgment: Moon supporting lords of the ingress = abundant rain; Moon decreasing and not aspecting Midheaven lord = rain still signified.
notes: Translator notes sentence is difficult; which specific domicile lords are intended remains ambiguous.

rule: The Moon under the rays of the Sun or in opposition to the Sun operates analogously to Saturn in producing rain signification, because in both of those configurations the Moon is in a receptive and releasing mode with respect to moisture.
judgment: Rain signified by the Moon alone in either of these configurations.

rule: When the Sun transits Aquarius (Saturn's domicile) within the year, the Moon's conjunction with the Sun in that sign indicates reduced rainfall. If Venus and Mercury also conjoin the Sun there, rain persists until Venus and Mercury separate from the Sun. Sun in Aquarius with Moon in Leo (Sun's domicile) simultaneously indicates heavy rain. Sun in Pisces or Aries with Moon in Cancer, Libra, or Virgo also indicates rain.

moon: conjunct Sun in Aquarius = rain scarcity
Leo while Sun in Aquarius = heavy rain
Cancer/Libra/Virgo while Sun in Pisces or Aries = rain
venus_mercury: conjunct Sun in Aquarius = sustained rain until separation

judgment: Varied: Moon conjunct Sun in Aquarius = scarcity; Moon in Leo opposite Sun in Aquarius = heavy rain; Venus/Mercury with Sun in Aquarius = rain until their separation from Sun.

rule: Mars aspecting the Sun, Moon, Venus, or Mercury, especially by conjunction or opposition, intensifies rainfall and adds dangerous atmospheric phenomena such as lightning. Mars retrograde during such configurations multiplies the dangerous phenomena. Mars in Pisces with Moon in Sagittarius and Sun in Pisces adds lightning to rain.

mars: aspecting Sun, Moon, Venus, or Mercury
sign_combinations: Moon in Taurus, Mars in Scorpio, Sun in Aquarius/Pisces/Aries
Moon in Scorpio, Mars in Taurus, Sun in Aquarius/Pisces/Aries
Mars in Pisces, Moon in Sagittarius, Sun in Pisces

judgment: Heavy rain with lightning; retrograde Mars increases dangerous phenomena.
notes: Text distinguishes between heat-lightning without thunder and lightning accompanied by thunder using two different Latin terms.

rule: When the Sun is in Scorpio or Sagittarius, Moon in Scorpio, Sagittarius, or Pisces, and Mars in Gemini, Virgo, or Taurus, lightning is produced but rainfall is reduced. Aries is additionally associated with lightning because it is the domicile of Mars.
judgment: Lightning activity with little rain; Aries associated with lightning via Mars's domicile rulership.

rule: Cold winds result when a planet (context implies Venus) aspects the Moon or is positioned in Pisces (Venus's exaltation), combined with the Sun in Scorpio or Libra, especially when Capricorn or Aquarius (Saturn's domiciles) are also active.
judgment: Cold winds.
notes: The subject of the aspect in this passage is ambiguous in the source; translator acknowledges uncertainty.

rule: The domicile groups of Jupiter and Mercury are paired (their domicile signs being in opposition to each other), as are those of Venus and Mars. In the annual revolution chart, Mercury aspecting Jupiter with one of them in a falling position and the other in an ascending position, where the falling one aspects the ascending one, produces abundant winds, because Jupiter's domain multiplies wind and Mercury is a wind significator.

conditions.condition: one falling, one ascending; falling one aspects ascending one

judgment: Abundant winds in that year.
notes: The translator notes 'falling' may refer to zodiacal latitude rather than cadent house position.

rule: Multiple sign-based configurations of Mercury, Moon, and Jupiter produce wind significations. These include: Mercury in Aquarius aspecting Moon in Taurus with Jupiter receiving Mercury by rulership; Mercury in Aquarius with Moon in Leo; Mercury in Pisces with Moon in Sagittarius or Virgo; Jupiter in exaltation with Mercury in Aries or Pisces aspecting Jupiter; Mercury in Scorpio with Jupiter in Taurus or Leo and Moon connecting from Aquarius, Pisces, Taurus, or Leo; Mercury in Scorpio with Jupiter in Taurus or Sagittarius and Moon connecting from Gemini or Virgo.

sign_pairs: Mercury Aries or Pisces aspecting Jupiter

judgment: Winds signified in each of these configurations.
notes: BN and CCAG differ slightly on whether Moon is with Jupiter, or Mercury alone, in one of the sub-cases.

rule: When the Sun is in Scorpio, Aquarius, Sagittarius, Libra, Pisces, or Aries and Mercury is under the Sun's rays, many winds result. If Venus additionally aspects Mercury in this state, rain is added. If Mars aspects Mercury in this state, lightning and thunder result. If the Moon transits through Mercury's position, rain results.
judgment: Winds as base condition; rain, lightning, or thunder added by Venus, Mars, or Moon aspects respectively.

rule: In the annual revolution chart, examine the Moon and Venus in opposition or at the moment of aspect formation; this indicates rain that will occur but may not complete its full expected duration. If the aspect originates from Scorpio, the rain will not persist.
judgment: Rain signified but potentially incomplete; rain from Scorpio configuration does not last.

rule: When Venus is in Taurus or Aquarius and the Moon aspects her from Scorpio with Mars also conjunct the Moon, rain with lightning and thunder and hail results. If Saturn additionally aspects the Moon in this configuration, severe hailstorms capable of damaging crops and killing birds or flying creatures are indicated.
judgment: Rain, lightning, thunder, hail; with Saturn aspect, destructive hailstorms harming agriculture and wildlife.
notes: CCAG substitutes Mercury for Mars in one reading; translator follows a different manuscript.

rule: In the annual revolution, when the Moon is in Scorpio, Sagittarius, Aquarius, or Pisces and Mars aspects the Moon from opposition but is not himself in Scorpio, the previously described rain and storm phenomena are reduced. If Mars is in Scorpio for this opposition, the harmful effect is nullified because of the vaporous quality associated with that sign.

conditions.mars: opposition to Moon, not in Scorpio

judgment: Reduction of rain/storm phenomena; nullification of harm if Mars is in Scorpio.

rule: Venus in Scorpio, Sagittarius, or Taurus signifies rain. Venus retrograde in Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius signifies heavy rainfall.
judgment: Rain when Venus is in listed signs; heavy rain when Venus is retrograde in Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius.

rule: In the context of a question's root chart, when the Moon separates from a superior planet and applies to an inferior planet or a planet of equal rank, rain is signified.

conditions.moon: separating from superior planet, applying to inferior or equal planet

judgment: Rain signified.
notes: The text uses language suggesting a horary or interrogational context ('foundation of the question').

rule: When Mars is in a falling condition and Venus is ascending and southern in latitude, rain results if the Moon aspects Mars from Virgo or Leo.

conditions.moon: aspects Mars from Virgo or Leo

judgment: Rain.

rule: When Venus is under the Sun's rays and the Moon aspects her from Pisces (with Venus in Taurus), or the Moon aspects Venus from Libra into Aries, heavy rain results. If Mars cuts off (intercepts) this aspect, the rainfall is reduced.

sign_pairs: Moon in Pisces aspecting Venus in Taurus
Moon in Libra aspecting Venus in Aries

judgment: Heavy rain; reduced by Mars intervention.

rule: Moon, Venus, and Mercury together in Pisces signify rain. Moon and Venus together in Aquarius signify rain. Moon and Venus together in Aries or Taurus signify decreased rainfall.
judgment: Rain for Pisces and Aquarius groupings; rain decrease for Aries and Taurus groupings.

rule: The Moon in opposition to the Sun, Saturn, or Venus in an annual revolution chart signals atmospheric corruption and rain from dew. If the Moon and the lord of her domicile are both increasing in numerical value (adding), the corruption from heavy dew is intensified.

conditions.moon: opposition to Sun, Saturn, or Venus
conditions.addition: Moon and domicile lord both increasing

judgment: Atmospheric corruption and dewy rain; intensified when Moon and domicile lord are both adding.

rule: At the Sun's entry into the twentieth degree of Scorpio, erect a chart and examine the Ascendant sign's elemental quality, the Moon's sign, and Venus's sign and solar relationship. If the Ascendant is a water sign and both Moon and Venus are in water signs, the beginning of winter is rainy and the end moist. If Venus is occidental and weak with Moon and Ascendant in water signs, both beginning and end are moist. Venus under the Sun's rays (occidental) acts as a moisture-producing significator. Venus oriental (arising before the Sun) indicates dryness at the start.
judgment: Rainy beginning and moist end with water Ascendant and water Moon and Venus; dryness at start with oriental Venus.
notes: CCAG reads 'first minute of Scorpio' but the translator reconciles with internal textual evidence to 20 Scorpio.

rule: The elemental combination of the Ascendant sign and the sign of its lord determines the moisture character of the year or season. Combinations include: fiery Ascendant with watery lord = temperate with slight moisture and lightning; fiery Ascendant with fiery lord = reduced rain; fiery Ascendant with airy lord = few rains, many winds; earthy Ascendant with watery lord = abundant rain and dew; earthy Ascendant with lord in angular fiery position = great dryness; watery Ascendant with airy lord = dews, winds, mists; fiery Ascendant with watery lord (variant) = very moist with little rain, or fair weather predominating; airy Ascendant with earthy lord = many winds, few dews.
judgment: Each elemental pairing yields a distinct moisture-wind-dryness outcome for the year.
notes: One entry has an unclear reference to 'Lord of the Lord of the hour' vs 'Lord of the Ascendant'; translator acknowledges ambiguity.

rule: The elemental quality of the lord of the hour at the ingress chart moment modifies the annual weather outcome: a moist/dewy lord of the hour produces a favorable year, while a dry lord of the hour corrupts the year's weather.
judgment: Moist lord of hour = good year; dry lord of hour = corrupted year.

rule: When the Sun conjoins one of the three superior planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars) and one of them occupies a specific angular house, the timing of rain within the year is indicated by that house: 4th house signals rain in the first quarter; 7th house signals rain in the middle quarter; 10th house signals dew across three quarters; 4th house also associated with end of year. The same rule applies to opposition and square aspects. Winter and spring accelerate the manifestation of these significations.
judgment: House position of superior planet at solar conjunction/opposition/square determines the quarter of the year when rain or dew manifests.
notes: The text appears to use the 4th house twice (first and last quarter), which the translator flags as potentially a manuscript error in assigning the quarters.

rule: The elemental quality of the sign(s) holding a conjunction or opposition between the Sun and a superior planet determines the nature of the resulting event. In summer: watery or earthy signs = heavy rain and flooding; fiery signs = wars, conflagrations, and destruction of vegetation. A conjunction in an airy sign combined with a square to an earthy sign produces damaging winds, storms, and crop destruction.

conditions.season: summer emphasis; applicable to any season

judgment: Sign element at conjunction/opposition determines whether rain, hail, war, wind, or agricultural damage results.

rule: The precise moment when the Sun applies to the degree of a planet that was in square aspect in the root configuration marks the time of the weather event. The effect is prolonged when the Moon is in the Ascendant or its opposite. The geographic direction of the event is determined by the house position of the relevant planetary conjunction: Ascendant = east, Midheaven = south, 7th = west, 4th = north.

conditions.timing_trigger: Sun applies to square planet's degree
conditions.duration_extension: Moon in Ascendant or opposite Ascendant

judgment: Time and geographic direction of weather event determined by solar application to square and house of planetary conjunction.
notes: BN and CCAG differ on whether 'place of rain' or 'place of a planet in square' is meant; the North Node may be involved in one reading.

rule: To determine when rain will fall during a period of extended drought, identify whether the North Node or the star Ras Alhague (alpha Ophiuchus) is in a water sign. When the Moon subsequently descends into a water sign, rain will occur promptly.

conditions.condition: one of them in a water sign

judgment: Imminent rain when Moon moves into a water sign while the Node or the star is already in a water sign.
notes: The identity of the second star ('Azaphora') is uncertain; the translator could not identify it definitively. The North Node connection is suggested by a parallel passage noted by the translator.

rule: A mundane annual chart is cast for the exact moment the Sun reaches 0° Aries. The Ascendant, four angles, and all house cusps are calculated to the degree and minute. Every planet's position, motion state, latitude, and ray projection is recorded before any judgment begins.
conditions: motion states: direct, retrograde, slow, fast
judgment: This chart is the foundation for all annual mundane judgments.
notes: Text also mentions the revision of this procedure for quarterly sub-revolutions depending on the rising sign's modality.

rule: A planet in retrograde motion lacks the capacity to produce beneficial outcomes; its constructive significations are suspended until it resumes direct motion.
judgment: No good is effected by that planet while retrograde; benefic signification resumes upon direct station.

rule: When the Lord of the Ascendant in a mundane ingress chart falls in a house that is unfavorable to the Ascendant (specifically the 6th, 8th, or 12th), the region signified suffers accordingly: the 6th indicates sickness, the 8th death, the 12th enmity or internal discord. The severity scales with the degree of the planet's adversarial position. The same principle extends to the Lord of the Ascendant's exaltation, bound lord, and triplicity lord, though each carries less weight than the Ascendant lord itself.
conditions: Lord of Ascendant in 6th, 8th, or 12th house of ingress chart
same rule applied to bound lord, exaltation lord, triplicity lord with reduced weight
judgment: 6th: disease in the region; 8th: death; 12th: enmity or conflict — scaled to the nature of the sign occupied.
notes: The text implies that the sign's nature modifies the specific form of the detriment.

rule: In a diurnal ingress, the Sun aspecting the Ascendant or its lord while free from malefic interference indicates strength and success for the population. The signification is enhanced if the Sun transfers his disposition to the Ascendant lord and is received in that place. In a nocturnal ingress, the Moon takes the role of the Sun and the same conditions apply.
conditions: diurnal chart: Sun aspecting Ascendant or its lord, free from malefics
nocturnal chart: Moon aspecting Ascendant or its lord, free from malefics
enhanced by mutual reception and disposition transfer
judgment: Strength and achievement for the citizenry; powerful individuals are subordinated to the ruler; prosperity, peace, and health follow. Reverse conditions yield the opposite.
notes: Text instructs that lords of the luminaries aspecting the luminaries from a strong place with reception also prevent disruption and promote justice.

rule: Each triplicity is assigned a cardinal direction and a corresponding angle of the chart. Fire signs (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius) correspond to the east and the Ascendant; Earth signs (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn) to the south and the Midheaven; Air signs (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius) to the west and the Descendant; Water signs (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) to the north and the IC. When a sign of a given triplicity occupies its corresponding angle, the mundane significations of that triplicity are amplified. The same enhancement applies to planets placed in those angular positions.
conditions: sign of a triplicity on its corresponding angle
or planet of that triplicity placed in the corresponding angle
judgment: The mundane significations associated with that triplicity's direction and peoples are strengthened.

rule: The seven terrestrial climate zones are each governed by one of the seven planets in the Chaldean order, analogous to the order of the planetary hours. Saturn rules the first clime, Jupiter the second, Mars the third, the Sun the fourth, Venus the fifth, Mercury the sixth, and the Moon the seventh. Each sign also rules specific lands and cities, and within each sign, the planetary bounds further subdivide rulership over particular cities. Benefic planets transiting a bound signify prosperity for the corresponding locale; malefic planets transiting it signify harm.
conditions: nature of planet: benefic or malefic
judgment: Benefic transit of a bound: good conditions for the city ruled by that bound. Malefic transit: adversity for that city or region.
notes: Iraq given as an example: ruled by Cancer, specifically the Jupiterian bound (19°–26° Cancer approximately).

rule: The modality of the Ascendant sign in the annual ingress determines whether and how many sub-revolutions (quarterly charts) must be consulted during the year. A cardinal Ascendant requires charts for each of the four seasonal ingresses. A mutable Ascendant requires two revisions, at the Aries and Libra ingresses. A fixed Ascendant means the Aries ingress chart governs the entire year without subdivision. These requirements are reinforced when the Lord of the Year occupies a sign of the same modality as the Ascendant. If the Lord of the Year is in a cardinal sign regardless of Ascendant modality, its specific significations apply only to the first quarter unless the subsequent quarterly charts confirm them.
conditions: Lord of the Year sign modality
judgment: Cardinal: four quarterly sub-revolutions required. Mutable: two sub-revolutions (Aries and Libra ingresses). Fixed: annual chart sufficient for all four quarters.

rule: The Lord of the Year is identified as the planet with the greatest overall strength and accumulation of dignitary testimonies at the moment of the ingress. Strength is assessed by house placement, with the Ascendant and Midheaven conferring maximum strength. The Descendant and IC confer one-quarter less. The 11th, 9th, 5th, and 3rd houses each represent successively diminishing levels of strength below that. A planet within 3° of the Ascendant cusp (in the same sign as the cusp) and holding the Ascendant rulership is preeminent and requires no further comparison.
conditions: planet in Ascendant or Midheaven: maximum strength
Descendant or IC: reduced by one quarter
Lord of Ascendant within 3° of Ascendant cusp: automatically strongest
judgment: The planet with highest aggregate strength and testimony is declared Lord of the Year and governs conditions for the region during that year.
notes: Dignity-based strength fractions also given: Lord of Ascendant = full; Lord of exaltation in its exaltation degrees = full; Lord of triplicity in Ascendant = 1/3; Lord of bound = 1/5; Lord of hour = 1/7. These fractions apply specifically when those planets are in the Ascendant or Midheaven, and are further reduced in angular cadency.

rule: If either luminary occupies an angle in the ingress chart, it becomes the Lord of the Year, unless it is impeded in that position. An impeded luminary in an angle indicates weakness and damage to the clime under its sign's dominion. Sect further qualifies: the Sun in an angle during a diurnal ingress and the Moon in an angle during a nocturnal ingress are each more powerful in their respective sect conditions, as are all planets when they are in their sect's appropriate time.
judgment: Unimpeded luminary in angle: that luminary is Lord of the Year. Impeded luminary in angle: signifies weakness of the region under that sign.

rule: If the Lord of the Year is placed in another planet's domicile, and that domicile lord occupies a favorable house and is conjoined to the Lord of the Year, the domicile lord absorbs the annual governance through reception. The transfer is further strengthened if the luminaries or their domicile lords aspect the receiving planet. If no such transfer occurs, the Lord of the Year retains governance through its own positional strength.
conditions: Lord of the Year in another planet's domicile
conjunction of domicile lord and Lord of the Year
optional: luminary aspect to domicile lord
judgment: When conditions are met, the domicile lord becomes effective Lord of the Year. Otherwise, the original Lord of the Year retains its role.

rule: When multiple planets transfer their disposition to the Lord of the Year, each one contributes its nature and strength to the annual outcome. The more planets committing to the Lord of the Year, the more comprehensive the good fortune distributed across the region from multiple directions.
conditions: one or more planets applying to and transferring disposition to Lord of the Year
judgment: Joy and benefit reach the clime from as many directions as there are planets committing their disposition to the Lord of the Year, proportional to each planet's strength.

rule: If one or both luminaries transfer their disposition to the Lord of the Ascendant, that planet is unambiguously the Lord of the Year, superseding all other candidates.
conditions: one or both luminaries committing disposition to Lord of Ascendant
judgment: Lord of Ascendant is conclusively identified as Lord of the Year.

rule: The significator of the king in a mundane ingress is determined by comparing the Lord of the Midheaven with the Sun. Whichever of the two holds greater positional strength according to house placement and dignity is taken as the king's significator. They are assessed using the same strength hierarchy applied to the Lord of the Year.
judgment: The stronger of Sun and Lord of Midheaven becomes the king's significator for that year.
notes: The Lord of the Year independently represents the condition of the common people (rustics).

rule: When the Lord of the Year occupies a house that does not aspect the Ascendant (2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th), it is considered weak and in need of support. A planet in the Midheaven that aspects the cadent Lord of the Year and is also the lord of the sign the Lord of the Year occupies can receive the annual governance, assume the role of Lord of the Year, and provide strength. The 3rd house is particularly weak because a planet there neither aspects the Ascendant nor the Midheaven.
conditions: Lord of the Year in 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th — houses not aspecting Ascendant
supporting planet is domicile lord of the sign occupied by Lord of the Year
Lord of the Year applies to supporting planet
judgment: The Midheaven planet receives the disposition and effectively becomes Lord of the Year, compensating for the original planet's cadency.
notes: The 3rd house is singled out as especially debilitated since it aspects neither Ascendant nor Midheaven.

rule: The type of aspect a malefic forms to the Lord of the Year or king's significator indicates the social origin of the resulting threat. Opposition indicates open enemies. Square indicates those who outwardly pose as peacemakers but harbor concealed hostility. Trine or sextile from a malefic indicates that the threat originates from apparent friends or allies.
conditions: malefic aspecting Lord of the Year or king's significator
aspect type: opposition, square, trine, sextile
judgment: Opposition: threat from overt enemies. Square: threat from hypocritical peacemakers. Trine/sextile: threat from those considered friendly.

rule: The house a malefic occupies when aspecting the Lord of the Year or king's significator specifies the domain of life through which adversity enters. Each of the twelve houses corresponds to a domain: 1st — general communal harm; 2nd — wealth and property; 3rd — siblings; 4th — fathers and land; 5th — children; 6th — sickness; 7th — war and conflict; 8th — death; 9th — foreign travel; 10th — royal authority; 11th — allies and friends; 12th — enemies.
conditions: malefic in a specific house aspecting Lord of the Year or king's significator
judgment: Domain of harm is identified by the malefic's house position. The same mapping is applied in reverse to benefic aspects for corresponding domains of benefit.
notes: Text explicitly states that the same principle applies when assessing a nativity's annual revolution.

rule: The direction from which a military threat or destructive event emanates is determined by the house angle in which the malefic falls: angular positions indicate the corresponding cardinal direction of threat. The relative age of a military leader or adversary is inferred from the malefic's solar phase: an oriental malefic (rising before the Sun) indicates a young person; an occidental one (setting after the Sun) indicates an older person; intermediate positions indicate intermediate ages.
conditions: malefic oriental or occidental relative to Sun
judgment: Angle position determines geographic direction of threat. Solar phase of malefic determines age profile of the adversary.
notes: Text notes that a retrograde malefic in an angle is especially damaging to cities and regions belonging to its sign.

rule: To identify the origin of an enemy to the king, examine the sign in which the malefic that threatens the king's significator is placed, and determine what testimony (if any) the king's significator or Lord of the Year holds in that sign. If testimony exists, the threat arises from the corresponding region in proportion to the amount of that testimony. If the Lord of the Year has this testimony but not the king's significator, the enemy is internal to the realm but the king will be weakened and replaced. If the king's significator holds the testimony but not the Lord of the Year, the enemy is external and the king will prevail.
conditions: king's significator has testimony in that sign
Lord of the Year has or lacks testimony in that sign
judgment: Testimony of king's significator: enemy from that region, king subdues them. Testimony of Lord of Year only: internal enemy, king weakened and displaced.
notes: Translator notes uncertainty about the exact scenario Māshā'allāh envisions.

rule: After identifying the Lord of the Year, assess the dignities of the sign it occupies: the domicile lord, bound lord, exaltation lord, and triplicity lord of that sign. If any of these lords aspect the Lord of the Year and receive it, the Lord of the Year is strengthened. The sign and its corresponding region or city then experiences superior conditions relative to other regions, and its ruler benefits most among all rulers in that year.
conditions: Lord of the Year in a sign
lords of that sign's dignities aspecting and receiving the Lord of the Year
judgment: The ruler of the region corresponding to the Lord of the Year's sign is the most powerful and prosperous ruler of the year; those born under that sign also benefit.

rule: A planet within the Sun's beams suffers a suppression of its active power, analogous to a state of subjugation. When it enters the solar rays, its capacity recedes. When it fully emerges from combustion, it begins to grow in strength and forward movement.
judgment: Under rays: weakened, subjects of the clime feel subdued. Emerging from combustion: increasing effectiveness and progress.
notes: Effect intensified if the planet is also in an angle or aspected by a malefic.

rule: Among all planets, the Moon and Mercury are the most subject to rapid reversals of fortune and condition, owing to their frequent changes in combustion status and the diversity of their configurations. A planet in deep combustion is at its worst; if the Lord of the Year or king's significator is combust and aspected by a malefic, the annual condition is at its most adverse. Conversely, when a planet matching the chart's sect (diurnal planet in a day revolution, nocturnal planet in a night revolution) falls under the Sun's rays, the Sun absorbs its strength, enhancing the Sun's signification of the king.
conditions: Moon or Mercury as Lord of the Year or king's significator
sect of planet matching sect of revolution
judgment: Combustion plus malefic aspect: worst possible annual condition. Sect-appropriate planet under rays: Sun becomes stronger as king's significator.

rule: A planet's capacity to produce effects through aspect is maximized when it aspects from its own domicile, exaltation, triplicity, or bound, or from a position of angular strength, or when it is also Lord of the Lot of Fortune, and when it is additionally oriental and direct.
conditions: aspecting planet in own domicile, exaltation, triplicity, or bound
or Lord of Lot of Fortune
judgment: Maximum strength in aspect signification; the greater the accumulation of these conditions, the more powerful the effect.

rule: The Lot of Fortune and its lord function as strengthening factors for the Lord of the Year and the king's significator. If these two significators are well-placed relative to the Lot of Fortune, good is indicated. If they are impeded while also under combustion, material and civic loss follows in proportion to the nature of the sign. The Lot of Fortune is understood as an extension of the luminaries' combined strength.
conditions: Lot of Fortune and its lord's house placement
Lord of the Year or king's significator aspecting or conjoining the Lot
judgment: Well-placed significators with Lot of Fortune: good and fitness. Impeded significators under combustion near Lot: detriment and loss according to sign nature.

rule: The planet to which the king's significator applies indicates the source of trust or danger. If the king's significator applies to the Lord of the Year, the king commits his concern to the people (rustics). If the king's significator separates from the Lord of the Year and then applies to a malefic that is adversarial to the Ascendant, the king becomes an instrument of harm to the people. Application of the king's significator to a planet in the 8th or 7th by opposition or square raises fear of the king's death that year; application to the 8th or 7th lords under similar conditions strengthens this concern. Application to a planet in the 3rd or 6th (or to their lords) indicates feared illness for the king.
conditions: king's significator applying to Lord of the Year or to a malefic
aspect type: opposition, square, or conjunction to planet in 8th or 7th
application to planet in 3rd or 6th or their lords
judgment: Application to Lord of Year: king oriented toward his people. Application to adversarial malefic: king harmful to people. Application to 8th/7th malefic: king's death feared. Application to 3rd/6th planet: king's illness feared.

rule: Retrograde motion in the Lord of the Year or the king's significator denotes deterioration and weakness in the kingdom and its citizens. When retrograde, the planet's bound and domicile lord modulate the severity: retrogradation in a benefic's domicile or bound is less harmful than in a malefic's territory. The retrogradation of the king's significator specifically indicates royal weakness; retrogradation of the Lord of the Year indicates weakness of civic governance.
conditions: bound and domicile of retrograding planet: benefic or malefic
judgment: Both retrograde: loss and weakness for king and citizens. King's significator retrograde: weakness of the king specifically. Lord of Year retrograde: weakness of communal governance. Retrograde in benefic territory: less severe.

rule: Mars direct at the ingress indicates adversaries who are aggressive and do not retreat. Mars retrograde indicates guerrilla-type enemies who avoid fixed engagement and do not advance openly. Saturn in any sign indicates civic difficulty for cities in that sign's region, moving through each house in sequence from Ascendant to 12th as the year progresses. A retrograde Saturn compounds the harm; Saturn applying to the Lord of the Year amplifies the adversity for the region's ruler.
conditions: Mars direct or retrograde in ingress chart
Saturn applying to Lord of Year
judgment: Mars direct: bold, non-fleeing enemies. Mars retrograde: evasive, irregular combatants. Saturn in a region's sign: civic hardship. Saturn retrograde and conjunct Lord of Year: intensified adversity for king and region.

rule: The conjunction cycle of Jupiter and Saturn governs changes of dominant political and religious structures. The greater conjunction (shift from one triplicity to another) indicates changes of entire dynasties or religious systems. The middle conjunction (the specific conjunction of Saturn and Mars) indicates wars. Speed of political change in a given year is assessed from the nature of Jupiter's and Saturn's conjunction and their advancement from the natal root of the conjunction.
conditions: Jupiter-Saturn conjunction in ingress or root chart
triplicity of conjunction: same or new triplicity
judgment: Triplicity shift of Jupiter-Saturn: change of kingdoms and religious systems. Saturn-Mars conjunction: wars and conflicts in that year.
notes: Reference made to a companion work ('On Roots') for elaboration of conjunctional cycles.

rule: When both Saturn and Mars occupy human signs (signs depicted with human figures) and are configured together by conjunction, square, or opposition — whether one is direct and the other retrograde — pestilence among people is indicated. A retrograde planet in this configuration makes the outbreak more insidious and rapid. The configuration's severity is compounded when it occurs in an angular house. The specific angle indicates the geographic direction from which the pestilence or destruction will spread.
conditions: Saturn and Mars in human signs
mutual configuration: conjunction, square, or opposition
judgment: Pestilence among the human population; retrograde intensifies speed and severity; angle placement increases strength and identifies direction of origin.

rule: When the slower of two malefics (Saturn) is in the 4th or 10th and a retrograde malefic applies to it from the 7th, the adversity originates from the western direction and the king gains power and expansion. When the slower malefic is in the 7th and a retrograde planet applies from the 4th, the adversity begins in the region associated with that angle and spreads westward.
conditions: or Saturn in 7th with retrograde malefic from 4th
judgment: Slower malefic in 4th/10th, retrograde applicant from 7th: evil from the west, king grows stronger. Slower malefic in 7th: evil starts in that region and moves westward.

rule: The onset of harm begins when the faster planet reaches the position of the slower one. The sign modality of the configuration determines the nature of harm: common signs produce death from war or killing; fixed signs produce whatever harm corresponds to the stronger malefic's nature. If Mars is stronger, death is from war or hot illness; if Saturn is stronger, death is from Saturnine illness, compounded by Mars's energy. Configurations outside angular houses reduce the magnitude of harm.
conditions: faster malefic applying to slower malefic
relative strength of Mars vs. Saturn in the configuration
judgment: Common sign: deaths from war or violence. Fixed sign: deaths according to the stronger malefic's nature. Outside angles: diminished harm, eventually dissipating.

rule: In assessing whether a particular annual ingress is dangerous, the presence of a Saturn conjunction in that year intensifies the danger. If no Saturn conjunction is present, the year is assessed as less severe. Additionally, if the Lord of the Year or king's significator transits over a slow malefic stationed in an angular house, this is considered a trigger for the signification of destruction or death.
conditions: Saturn conjunction present in the year
Lord of the Year or king's significator transiting over slow malefic in angle
judgment: Saturn conjunction present: year is more threatening. Transit over malefic in angle: feared outcome triggered.
notes: Text's reference ('conjunction of Saturn with whom?') left ambiguous; translator notes uncertainty.

rule: The harm produced by a malefic in an ingress chart is reduced when the malefic operates in conditions consistent with its sect: Saturn in a diurnal, masculine sign causes less damage; Mars in a feminine sign in a nocturnal context causes less damage. Additionally, if a malefic is received in its place (by the lord of the sign or bound it occupies), its destructive capacity is moderated: deaths from disease will be fewer, and killings will be less severe.
conditions: Mars in feminine sign, nocturnal context
malefic received by sign or bound lord
judgment: Sect-appropriate malefic: reduced impediment. Received malefic: fewer deaths, wounds mitigated, people show compassion.

rule: The North Node aligns with benefic planets in quality; the South Node amplifies malefic effects. The conjunction of the North Node with Saturn produces outcomes according to the nature of the sign in which they meet: fire signs — harm to animals and wild creatures; earth signs — damage to vegetation, trees, and grain with scarce rainfall; air signs — harm to people and birds with disruptive winds; water signs — floods, excessive cold, multiplication of fish, insects, and vermin. The square aspect or conjunction of a malefic with the South Node indicates war, famine, fear, intense cold, and broad adversity. Saturn conjunct the South Node specifically signifies famine, scarcity, destruction of trees, and cold in the corresponding direction.
