If neither luminary qualifies, test in order: the ruler of the pre-natal syzygy sign; the ruler of the Lot of Fortune's sign; the ascending degree itself (provided its own sign ruler aspects it). If none of these qualify, no hilaj exists for the chart.
conditions: Sect of chart; angular or succeedent placement of candidate; sign gender and chart-quarter position; aspect from at least one of the five dignity rulers of the candidate
judgment: The first candidate meeting all criteria becomes the hilaj. If no candidate qualifies, there is no hilaj.
notes: A footnote queries whether the Lot of Fortune's degree itself or its dispositor is the candidate at that step; tradition generally uses the degree of the Lot. The masculine quarter is described as from the 7th house backward; the text appears to omit the ascendant-to-midheaven quarter, which is also normally considered masculine.

rule: Once the hilaj is established, identify the kadukhudah (life-length ruler) by examining all five dignity rulers of the hilaj's position (domicile, bound, triplicity, exaltation, face rulers). The one among these that actually aspects the hilaj is the kadukhudah. When multiple dignity rulers aspect the hilaj, the one with the greatest inherent strength and closest angular distance to the hilaj takes priority.
conditions: Hilaj established; five dignity rulers of hilaj's degree identified; which of them aspect the hilaj; comparative strength and degree-proximity of multiple candidates
judgment: The strongest, closest-aspecting dignity ruler of the hilaj is the kadukhudah.
notes: Sun in Aries or Leo, and Moon in Taurus or Cancer, may serve simultaneously as both hilaj and kadukhudah regardless of whether their own dignity rulers aspect them.

rule: The years allocated by the kadukhudah depend on its positional and essential strength. If it is in an angle by degree (or in its own domicile, exaltation, or triplicity) and free from retrogradation and combustion, assign the planet's greater-year value. If it is in a succeedent house and free from malefic interference, assign the middle-year value. If it is in a cadent house without essential dignity in that location, assign the lesser-year value.
conditions: Kadukhudah's house type (angular, succeedent, cadent); essential dignity status; freedom from retrogradation and combustion
judgment: Greater, middle, or lesser planetary years are assigned accordingly.
notes: The text adds refinements: an oriental kadukhudah in good condition yields the greater years; one that is not oriental and has a harmful aspect yields the lesser years; one that is occidental with a harmful aspect and retrograde yields weeks equaling its lesser-year number; one in the worst possible condition, retrograde, and classified as a lighter planet, yields days equaling its lesser-year number.

rule: The North Node (Head of the Dragon) within approximately 12 degrees of the kadukhudah adds one quarter of that planet's years to the lifespan total; a closer orb increases this benefit. The South Node (Tail of the Dragon) in the same proximity subtracts one quarter of the kadukhudah's years. When either node is exactly conjunct the Sun or Moon by degree, it loses its subtracting effect. However, if the Sun is the kadukhudah and is separated from the South Node, the Node still subtracts from the years.
conditions: Nodal position relative to the kadukhudah; orb (approximately 12 degrees); exact conjunction with luminaries
judgment: North Node near kadukhudah: add one-quarter of kadukhudah's years. South Node near kadukhudah: subtract one-quarter. Exact nodal conjunction with a luminary neutralizes the subtraction. South Node separated from the Sun as kadukhudah still subtracts.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (regarding the general principle of Head adding fortune and Tail subtracting years)
notes: The text notes that nodal influence on the luminaries manifests more strongly for the Moon than for the Sun.

rule: Jupiter and Venus each placed in the ascending house add their own lesser-year values to the native's lifespan, provided that malefic planets are not obstructing them and the Moon is not in poor condition. However, if either benefic is simultaneously the ruler of the eighth house and is placed in the ascending house, the native will die very young rather than benefiting from the addition.
conditions: Jupiter or Venus in the ascendant; freedom from malefic impediment; Moon's condition; whether the benefic is the eighth-house ruler
judgment: Unafflicted benefics in ascendant: lifespan extended by each planet's lesser years. Benefic as eighth-house ruler in ascendant: very early death.

rule: Additional years, months, weeks, or days are added to or subtracted from the kadukhudah's base year count based on the condition of planets aspecting it. A benefic conjunct or aspecting the kadukhudah by a harmonious aspect while itself in a strong house adds that benefic's lesser-year value to the total. A weakened but otherwise well-intentioned benefic aspecting the kadukhudah converts its lesser years to months as the addition. A retrograde benefic aspecting the kadukhudah while impeded by a malefic converts its lesser years to weeks. If the kadukhudah is co-present with the eighth-house ruler and a malefic is also interfering, convert the lesser years to days. If a malefic is conjunct the kadukhudah, receives the degree of the kadukhudah, aspects it by square or opposition, and all three are in conjunction with the eighth-house ruler, the lesser years become hours.
conditions: Nature (benefic or malefic) of the aspecting planet; aspect type; the aspecting planet's strength (strong, weak, retrograde); presence of malefic impediment; relationship to the eighth-house ruler
judgment: The aspecting planet's lesser years are converted to years, months, weeks, days, or hours and added to or subtracted from the base lifespan total depending on the conditions described.
notes: Mercury in a good place aspecting the kadukhudah by a favorable aspect increases the lesser-year count; the reverse subtracts. The text states that the aspect of Mars with the kadukhudah is the most powerful malefic aspect.

rule: To determine the precise timing of death, identify the malefic planet obstructing the kadukhudah, then direct the kadukhudah to the degree of that malefic by primary direction. The point at which the kadukhudah reaches those degrees by direction marks the time of death.
conditions: Malefic identified as impeditor of kadukhudah; primary direction of kadukhudah to the impeditor's degree
judgment: Death occurs when the primary direction of the kadukhudah completes its arc to the impediting malefic's degree.

rule: Assess the native's character, speech, and intellect from the combined testimony of the ascendant lord and Mercury. In a cardinal sign: good speech, an honorable disposition, and piety are indicated. In a mutable sign: limited wisdom, proneness to anger, and disregard for others' counsel. In a fixed sign: a disposition toward honor, truthfulness, sound judgment, and the ability to resolve complicated matters.
conditions: Sign quality (cardinal, fixed, mutable) of the ascendant lord and Mercury
judgment: Cardinal: good eloquence and honorable piety. Mutable: limited wisdom and irritability. Fixed: honor, truthfulness, and practical wisdom.
notes: The text implies both planets are evaluated together, though it initially refers to them in the singular.

rule: The phase and house condition of the ascendant lord and Mercury jointly modify character judgment. Oriental and angular or succeedent: good natural disposition and sharp capability, with ease of accomplishment. Occidental and cadent: a malevolent inner character, association with base companions, and excessive anger.
conditions: Phase of planet (oriental or occidental); house position (angular, succeedent, or cadent)
judgment: Oriental and angular/succeedent: favorable character and effective action. Occidental and cadent: unfavorable character and social degradation.

rule: The planet ruling the ascending sign, when in good condition and free of malefic contact, produces positive character and social outcomes specific to that planet's nature. When in poor condition or a weak house, it produces negative expressions of the same planetary nature. Sun as ascendant lord, well-placed: eminence and authority; poorly placed: weak spirit and little material acquisition. Moon as ascendant lord, well-placed: honesty and modesty; poorly placed: shamelessness and speech that brings physical harm. Saturn as ascendant lord, well-placed: honor, popularity, and prudent counsel; poorly placed: melancholy, lamentation, and deception. Jupiter as ascendant lord, well-placed: elevation and generous spirit; poorly placed: shamelessness and miserliness. Mars as ascendant lord, free of affliction: liberality and courage; poorly placed: violent temperament and association with bloodshed. Venus as ascendant lord, well-placed: physical attractiveness and humility; poorly placed: excessive sensual desire (and, for women, promiscuity). Mercury as ascendant lord, free of affliction: intelligence and medical or scholarly skill; joined to Saturn: speech impediment, medical ability, involvement in complex affairs, and deviant sexuality; joined to Jupiter: goodness, wisdom, and attainment of prestigious authority; joined to Mars or in Mars's aspect: association with rulership or service as a royal secretary; joined to Venus: esteem for learning and judgment, but also treachery in law and persistence in either arrogance or ignorance.
conditions: Identity of the ascending sign's ruler; its house position (strong or weak); its essential dignity status; its conjunctions or aspects with other planets
judgment: Each planet as ascendant lord yields characteristic positive or negative delineations of the native's personality, body, and social role according to its condition.
notes: There is a textual lacuna in the Moon-as-ascendant-lord section. The Mercury-joined-to-Venus delineation is internally ambiguous, indicating contradictory outcomes simultaneously.

rule: For nativities of persons from royal lineage, elevated status is further confirmed when a hot (Mars or Sun-type) planet is conjunct the ascending degree or the midheaven, and the ascending degree is a bright (lucida) degree, or the sect light occupies the ascending degree. If additionally in a day chart the Sun is in Aries, or in a night chart the Moon is in her exaltation, and either luminary is in the midheaven or ascending degree, and the ascending sign is one of the signs associated with kings (the fiery signs), and the ascendant lord is strong, a kingdom is signified. If both luminaries are joined to the ascendant lord while it occupies its own exaltation, a powerful kingdom is indicated. If the ascendant lord is joined with the tenth-house ruler and both are oriental and in their own exaltations, the native will be a very powerful king. If many planets are joined with Jupiter in the midheaven or in his exaltation, imperial status is indicated. If the triplicity ruler of the ascendant is joined with the ascendant lord in the midheaven and is oriental, kingship is indicated. If the Sun is in his own domicile or in an angle or in his joy and the planets aspect each other, kingship is indicated.
conditions: Royal lineage of native; hot planet on ascendant degree or midheaven; lucida ascending degree; sect light on ascendant; Sun in Aries (day) or Moon in exaltation (night); ascending sign from fiery group; ascendant lord's condition; luminaries joined to ascendant lord in its exaltation; ascendant lord and tenth-house lord both oriental and exalted; Jupiter with multiple planets in midheaven or exaltation; triplicity lord of ascendant conjunct ascendant lord in midheaven; Sun in domicile or joy in angle
judgment: Combinations of these indicators confirm, amplify, or specify the degree of royal power or imperial status for the native.
notes: These conditions are explicitly framed as applying to persons of known royal descent; they are not presented as generic indicators of fame or authority for all natives.

rule: Evaluate the native's overall fortune and its timing by examining the triplicity rulers of the sect light's sign. In a day chart use the Sun's sign; in a night chart use the Moon's sign. If all three triplicity rulers are angular and unafflicted, good fortune is indicated throughout life. The first triplicity ruler governs the first life period, the second governs the middle period, and the third governs the final period. A triplicity ruler in a good house during its period indicates prosperity; one in a bad house or cadent indicates poverty or misfortune during that period. If the triplicity rulers are cadent but benefics occupy angles and aspect the ascendant without impediment, fortune is still indicated. If the luminaries themselves are also unafflicted, this strengthens the positive judgment.
conditions: Sect of chart; triplicity rulers of sect light's sign; house position of each triplicity ruler (angular, succeedent, cadent); malefic aspect or conjunction; benefic angular placement; luminary condition
judgment: Good fortune throughout life, or confined to specific life periods, or poverty, according to each triplicity ruler's condition matched to its corresponding life period.
notes: The source notes this section derives largely from Carmen I.22-26. A 15-degree rule within angular houses is referenced for closer placement yielding stronger benefit, apparently from Carmen.

rule: When both the ascendant lord and the Moon are angular and free from malefic interference, wealth is indicated, especially when mutual reception is present. If the ascendant lord applies to a luminary while that luminary is in its own domicile or exaltation, or a luminary applies to the ascendant lord, outstanding wealth is signified.
conditions: Ascendant lord and Moon both angular; freedom from malefics; presence of mutual reception; application between ascendant lord and a luminary in the luminary's own dignity
judgment: Angular and unafflicted ascendant lord and Moon indicate wealth; reception enhances it; mutual application within dignities indicates exceptional wealth.

rule: The Lot of Fortune and its ruler both angular (especially in the eastern angle) and aspecting the ascendant indicate great wealth. If both are in cadent or unfortunate places, harm and loss result, unless the triplicity rulers of the ascendant aspect the ascendant. If the Lot and its ruler are cadent but also conjunct or applying to benefics that are angular, good fortune precedes the harm. If the ascendant ruler is cadent and in its own detriment but applies to a planet that is in its own exaltation or domicile, good fortune follows after an initial period of hardship.
conditions: Lot of Fortune's house position; its ruler's house position; aspect of either to the ascendant; triplicity lords of ascendant aspecting the ascendant; condition of planets the ascendant ruler applies to
judgment: Angular Lot and ruler aspecting ascendant: great wealth. Cadent Lot and ruler: poverty and harm. Cadent but applying to angular benefics: good before harm. Ascendant ruler cadent and debilitated but applying to dignified planet: good after hardship.

rule: To identify the primary significator of a horary inquiry, assemble a candidate pool consisting of: the Ascendant ruler, the Moon, the domicile lord of the Moon's sign, the sect luminary (Sun in diurnal charts), the domicile lord of that luminary's sign, the Lord of the Hour, the Lord of the Lot of Fortune, and any planet occupying an angle (with the Ascendant and Midheaven given priority). Evaluate each candidate by the number of essential dignities it holds and the quality of its house placement. The candidate with the highest combined score of dignity and positional strength becomes the significator.
conditions: sect luminary and its domicile lord
judgment: The planet scoring highest on the combined measure of essential dignities and angular/good-place positioning is designated the horary significator through which judgment proceeds.
notes: Two slightly variant candidate lists appear in the same passage: one includes the Lot of Fortune itself (as a candidate point), the other specifies its lord; one list does not name a planet in the angles as a candidate while the other does. Peregrination for the Moon's purposes appears to exclude bound and face, treating only domicile, exaltation, and triplicity as relevant dignities.

rule: When the Ascendant ruler is physically located in the Ascendant sign, it outranks all other candidates as significator. If the Ascendant ruler is absent from the Ascendant but the exaltation lord of the Ascendant occupies it, that exaltation lord alone serves as significator. If both rulers are present in the Ascendant simultaneously, they share the role as co-significators. When one of the two also holds an additional dignity there and is better placed, it alone takes precedence. A third planet possessing any dignity in the Ascendant degree that applies to one of these two rulers—or the Moon occupying the domicile of one of them while applying to it—strengthens that ruler's claim through accumulation of dignities.
conditions: exaltation ruler of Ascendant in Ascendant
Moon's domicile position relative to candidate rulers
applying aspect or conjunction of Moon to candidate
judgment: Determines which planet or planets carry the role of significator, based on presence in the Ascendant, dignity accumulation, and relational ties through the Moon.
notes: If neither the domicile nor exaltation lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, the text instructs looking for any dignified planet in any angle that is strongest overall in the chart.

rule: A single planet (such as the Ascendant lord or the Moon) cannot serve as a blanket significator for all questions posed during the same rising sign or the same day, because outcomes vary from question to question within that period. The significator must be specifically identified for each individual question.
conditions: Moon's daily motion and successive applications
variation in outcomes among simultaneous questions
judgment: Affirms that horary judgment requires individualized significator determination for each query rather than a standing planetary assignment.

rule: Every horary question contains three layers of inquiry: (1) the subject matter and reason behind the question, discerned from the nature and condition of the significator itself; (2) the originating cause of the question, shown by the planet from which the significator is separating; (3) the likely outcome, shown by the planet to which the significator is applying.
conditions: significator's essential and accidental condition for layer 1
separating aspect or departure for layer 2
applying aspect or approach for layer 3
judgment: The significator's nature reveals what is being asked; its most recent separation reveals what triggered the question; its next application reveals how the matter will resolve.
notes: A footnote clarifies that these three layers correspond to condition/nature, past separation, and future application respectively.

rule: After identifying the primary significator, examine the sign it occupies and locate that sign's domicile lord (the significator's dispositor). Then determine which house that dispositor occupies relative to the Ascendant. The house position of the dispositor, combined with the planet's natural significations, indicates the subject matter of the question.
conditions: house occupied by dispositor counting from Ascendant
judgment: The intersection of the dispositor's natural rulership (e.g., Moon for mothers, Sun for fathers) and its house position (e.g., 6th for illness, 7th for marriage) identifies what topic the querent is actually asking about.
notes: The worked example shows that the 4th sign from the significator indicates family members, and the Moon specifically narrows the subject to the mother; the 6th house position of the dispositor then identifies illness as the topic. The text notes this dispositor-lookup step was not included in either of the formal candidate lists.

rule: To determine what prompted or caused the querent's question, identify the planet from which the horary significator is most recently separating. The nature and significations of that planet describe the circumstances or events that originated the question.
conditions: significator's most recent departure from another planet
nature of the planet being separated from
judgment: The separated-from planet's significations describe the triggering cause of the inquiry.
notes: In the worked example the Moon (acting as secondary significator) separates from Saturn, indicating a cold-dry illness as the cause; this appears to use the Moon's separations rather than the primary significator's, suggesting flexibility in which planet's motions are tracked.

rule: To determine the outcome of the queried matter, identify the planet to which the horary significator is applying. The nature of that planet—benefic or malefic—and whether it receives the applying planet indicates whether the matter resolves favorably or not. If the target planet is a malefic and receives the application, a negative outcome (including death in medical questions) is indicated; if it is a received benefic, a favorable resolution is indicated.
conditions: benefic or malefic status of receiving planet
judgment: Application to a received benefic signals a favorable outcome; application to a malefic signals an unfavorable or fatal outcome depending on the question's nature.

rule: Once the degree-distance between the applying and receiving planets is measured, convert that arc into a time unit determined by the sign quality of the planet making the application: movable signs indicate days, common (mutable) signs indicate months, and fixed signs indicate years.
conditions: degree arc between applying significator and receiving planet
sign quality: movable, common, or fixed
judgment: The number of degrees to exact aspect or conjunction, read through the sign-quality filter, gives the time elapsed before the indicated outcome occurs.

rule: Identify the subject of a horary by combining a key planet's natural signification with the house it occupies. Each planet carries a baseline referent (Venus: women; Sun: father; Mars: fugitives or robbers; Mercury: letters or knowledge; Jupiter: dreams or religion) and each house modifies that referent (e.g., 7th: marriage or adversary; 10th: king or authority; 5th: children; 9th: faith or long journeys; 2nd: wealth or theft; 3rd: siblings or short journeys; 11th: friends; Ascendant: self or fear; 8th: death).
conditions: planet acting as secondary indicator or dispositor
house that planet occupies from the Ascendant
judgment: The overlap of planetary nature and house topic defines the specific question the querent is implicitly asking about.
notes: The text presents these as illustrative combinations rather than an exhaustive table; the practitioner is expected to extend the logic to other planet-house pairings.

rule: A question carries stronger validity and yields more reliable judgment when the querent has genuinely held and reflected on the matter for a full day-and-night period (24 hours) or longer before posing it. Questions asked without this prior deliberation are harder to read accurately.
conditions: duration of querent's preoccupation with the matter
querent's ability to articulate the question clearly
judgment: Longer prior deliberation correlates with a clearer horary chart and more reliable significator identification; a poorly formed or impulsive question may prevent accurate significator selection.

rule: Horary judgment can fail for four identifiable reasons: (1) the timekeeping or angle-measuring instrument is defective or used on an uneven surface; (2) the querent formulates the question poorly or incoherently; (3) the astrologer is uncertain whether the Sun has already crossed the Midheaven, causing an error in determining the hour; (4) the benefic and malefic testimonies in the chart are so evenly balanced that neither side clearly dominates, making the overall judgment ambiguous.
conditions: balance of benefic versus malefic strength
judgment: Any of these four conditions can invalidate or significantly impair horary judgment; questions free from all four can be judged reliably if the significator is correctly identified.

rule: If none of the primary candidate planets (Ascendant lord, Moon, luminary, luminary's sign lord, Lord of Hour, Lot of Fortune lord, angular planets) qualifies because none is well-placed, fall back to the complete dignity hierarchy of the Ascendant degree: examine its domicile lord, exaltation lord, bound lord, triplicity lord, and face lord. Assess which of these holds the most dignities in the Ascendant and is best placed overall; that planet becomes the significator, provided it occupies a good house.
conditions: house placement quality of fallback candidates
judgment: The dignity lord of the Ascendant with the highest combined dignity count and best positional strength serves as a last-resort significator.
notes: 'Good place' is defined in the text as: the planet is in one of its own dignities, or in a favorable solar relationship, or in an angle, and free from malefic influence.

rule: Establish the Ascendant lord as the primary significator and then identify the planet that receives the Ascendant lord's disposition (its dispositor). The topic of the question is indicated by the actual house position of the Ascendant lord in the chart, or alternatively by the house position of the planet that receives the Ascendant lord's disposition.
conditions: planet receiving the Ascendant lord's disposition
judgment: Either the Ascendant lord's own house placement or its dispositor's house placement reveals the subject matter of the querent's concern.
notes: This method appears in the 'On Hidden Things' section and represents a slightly different approach to significator identification than the primary list in 'On Cognition'.

rule: Look at the exact degree of the Ascendant and determine to which planet that degree is applying. The house that planet occupies indicates the subject of the querent's intention. Additionally, if a planet is conjunct the Ascendant degree within a close orb, its own nature and the houses it rules contribute to identifying the question's subject; however, only those houses the planet rules that share a whole-sign aspect with the Ascendant sign are considered relevant.
conditions: planet receiving application from Ascendant degree
whole-sign aspect between planet's ruled house and Ascendant
judgment: The house position of the planet receiving the Ascendant degree's application, or the nature of a planet in the Ascendant, reveals the matter under inquiry.
notes: The restriction to whole-sign-aspecting houses is ambiguous in the source; it may be an editorial clarification rather than a firm rule.

rule: As an alternative significator method, identify the house the Lot of Fortune occupies counting from the Ascendant. That house's topical domain describes the subject of the querent's question—e.g., Lot in the 1st indicates a question about the querent personally, in the 2nd about finances, in the 3rd about siblings, and so on through all twelve houses.
conditions: Lot of Fortune's house position from Ascendant
judgment: The house of the Lot of Fortune identifies the question's subject matter as a second route to significator determination.
attribution_in_text: Dorotheus, Antiochus, Ptolemy, Vettius Valens (as cited within the passage)
notes: The attribution cluster here may be questionable; a footnote indicates uncertainty about where these citations originate.

rule: When a querent is concealing the true subject of the question, identify the lord of the Ascendant degree's minor dignity (bound or face—whichever is stronger) and observe to which planet it applies. The nature of the receiving planet reveals the concealed matter.
conditions: relative strength of these two dignity lords
planet receiving the application of the stronger dignity lord
judgment: The application of the stronger minor-dignity lord of the Ascendant reveals what the querent is hiding.
attribution_in_text: the Indians (as cited within the passage)

rule: Calculate the twelfth-part (dodecatemorion) of the Ascendant degree by multiplying the degree's position within its sign by 2.5, then counting that many degrees from the beginning of the Ascendant sign through the zodiac. The sign where the count terminates indicates the relevant house topic. If a planet occupies that terminating sign, the intention concerns that house's domain. If no planet is there, find the lord of that sign and observe which house it occupies; that house's domain reveals the intention.
conditions: planet presence or absence in terminating sign
lord of terminating sign and its house position
judgment: The twelfth-part of the Ascendant degree, whether occupied or ruled, identifies the subject matter of the querent's question and is described as the strongest of the significator-finding methods presented.
notes: This method is presented as the most reliable of the four methods enumerated. The calculation is: take the degree number of the Ascendant within its sign, project 2.5 degrees per sign forward from the Ascendant sign; the sign where the accumulated arc ends is the twelfth-part sign.

rule: To locate a concealed object within a space, determine the direction-quality of the sign occupied by the Ascendant lord (east, west, north, or south). Divide the search area into four directional quadrants and focus on the quadrant corresponding to the Ascendant lord's sign direction. Then find the domicile lord of that sign and apply the same directional logic to subdivide the identified quadrant further. Repeat this telescoping subdivision iteratively—each iteration using the next planet in the dispositor chain—until the location is narrowed to a specific area.
conditions: Ascendant lord's sign and its directional quality
dispositor chain of successive sign lords
directional assignment of signs: fire=east, air=west, earth=south, water=north
judgment: The object's location is progressively narrowed by iterating through the dispositor chain, each step halving or quartering the remaining search area by directional quality.
notes: Sign-direction assignments given: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius = east; Gemini, Libra, Aquarius = west; Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn = south; Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces = north.

rule: Select as significator the planet among the Ascendant lord, its exaltation lord, and the Lord of the Hour that most strongly aspects the Ascendant. Map the significator's house position to a compass direction using the angular framework: 1st house = east, 10th house = south (right when facing east), 4th house = north (left when facing east), 7th house = west. For houses between angles, interpolate proportionally between the two surrounding cardinal directions, with proximity to the nearer angle indicating greater proximity to that direction.
conditions: significator selection from Ascendant lord, its exaltation lord, Lord of Hour
judgment: The significator's house position maps to a compass bearing indicating where the hidden object lies within the space.
notes: This method uses a different significator-selection rule (best aspect to Ascendant from three candidates) than the primary horary significator procedure.

rule: To determine the vertical level within a structure where an object is hidden, use the elemental quality of the Ascendant sign: fire signs indicate the roof or upper wall area; air signs indicate the walls; water signs indicate the foundation or ground level; earth signs indicate the floor surface.
conditions: elemental quality of Ascendant sign or relevant sign
judgment: The element of the relevant sign maps to the structural level within a building where the hidden item should be sought.

rule: When a specific planet occupies the Ascendant at the time of the question about a concealed object, that planet indicates the precise type of location within the structure: Mercury in Ascendant = buried in the ground; Venus = under a bed or couch; Jupiter = under a wall; Saturn = a dark, foul-smelling, deserted, or latrine area; Sun = a better or more prominent area of the structure. For planets in the 7th house: Moon = an area associated with women or wine storage; Mars = a passageway, oven, kitchen, or fire area; North Node (Head) = a higher elevated area such as a dining room; South Node (Tail) = a dark, damp, foul-smelling low area.
conditions: planet or node occupying the 7th house
judgment: The planet or node in the Ascendant or 7th specifies the type of physical location within the structure where the hidden object will be found.
notes: The shift from Ascendant planets to 7th-house planets mid-list is noted as unexplained in the source.

rule: If the Sun and Moon both aspect the Ascendant, the hidden object is near the entrance or door of the structure. If the Lord of the Hour is in the Midheaven, the object is in the central area of the structure. If the Lord of the Hour is in the 7th house, the object is in the western section. If the Lord of the Hour is in the 4th house, the object is toward the north.
conditions: Lord of Hour house position: 10th, 7th, or 4th
judgment: Specific structural sub-locations (door, center, west, north) are assigned based on the luminary-Ascendant aspect condition and the Lord of Hour's angular house.

rule: The Lord of the Hour's orientation (eastern or western) indicates the relative age of the concealment: an eastern Lord of the Hour signifies the object was hidden recently; a western Lord of the Hour signifies the hiding occurred long ago.
conditions: Lord of Hour's eastern or western condition
judgment: Recent versus ancient concealment is distinguished by the Lord of Hour's eastern/western status.
notes: The precise technical meaning of 'eastern' and 'western' for this purpose is ambiguous in the source.

rule: A planet occupying the 8th house at the time of a question about a hidden or buried thing acts as significator of the object itself, indicating by its own nature what kind of thing is concealed.
judgment: The planet in the 8th identifies the nature or type of the hidden object.

rule: As an alternative directional method, derive the bearing of the hidden object from the Lot of Fortune and its lord: if these are in eastern signs the object is eastward, and so forth by sign direction. The nature of the hidden thing is indicated by the 4th house and its lord. A strong and well-placed Ascendant lord and Moon together confirm that something is in fact buried or hidden at the location.
conditions: Lot of Fortune sign directional quality
lord of Lot of Fortune sign directional quality
4th house and its lord for object identification
Ascendant lord and Moon condition for presence confirmation
judgment: The directional quality of the Lot and its lord yields the bearing; the 4th house lord describes the object; strong Ascendant lord and Moon confirm something is genuinely there.

rule: To judge whether a querent will recover a lost or hidden item, examine the Ascendant lord and Lord of the Hour. If both are in angular houses, recovery is indicated. If both are in houses that do not aspect the Ascendant (cadent/averse houses), recovery is not indicated. If either or both are in the Ascendant, the object has not actually been lost and remains with the querent. If either or both are in the 7th house, recovery occurs but only after a delay of several days. If either aspects the Sun, recovery is indicated; Moon aspecting the significators makes recovery more certain. The Lord of the Hour's house position indicates where the lost item physically is.
judgment: Angular placement of both key planets indicates recovery; averse placement denies it; Ascendant placement means the item was never truly lost; 7th-house placement means delayed recovery; solar aspect indicates recovery; lunar aspect adds confirmation. Lord of Hour's location indicates the object's whereabouts.

rule: To determine whether something of value is present at a given location, check for a benefic planet in any angular house. If one is found free from malefic aspects, something of value is present there, with quantity proportional to the benefic's strength. If a malefic aspects that benefic by a harmful aspect, nothing of value is at the location.
conditions: malefic aspect or absence thereof to the angular benefic
strength of the benefic in its position
judgment: An unafflicted angular benefic confirms presence of buried or hidden valuables; malefic aspect to the angular benefic denies it. Strength determines quantity.

rule: Once an angular benefic confirms the presence of a valuable item, determine whether the querent will actually retrieve it by checking whether the Ascendant lord or the Moon applies to that benefic, aspects it by a harmonious aspect, or receives it. Any of these conditions indicates successful recovery; their absence indicates failure to recover.
conditions: Ascendant lord or Moon applying to angular benefic
harmonious aspect from Ascendant lord or Moon to angular benefic
reception of Ascendant lord or Moon by angular benefic
judgment: Application to, harmonious aspect toward, or reception by the angular benefic confirms the querent will obtain the item; none of these denies recovery.

rule: To judge how deeply something is buried, examine the relevant planet's distance from its apogee (awj): if the planet is at or near its apogee, the item is not deeply buried; if the planet is near its perigee (opposite apogee) or at a middle position, the item is buried deeply.
conditions: planet's position relative to its apogee and perigee
judgment: Proximity to apogee indicates shallow burial; proximity to perigee or mid-cycle position indicates deep burial.

rule: Once a general directional zone within a space is established, refine the precise spot using the relevant planet's celestial latitude. If the planet has northern latitude, shift the estimated location toward the north within the identified zone; if southern, shift south. The magnitude of the latitude corresponds to the distance of displacement. If the planet has no latitude, the object's location corresponds to where the Lord of the Lot of Fortune is positioned within the zone.
conditions: Lord of Lot of Fortune as fallback when planet has zero latitude
judgment: Planetary latitude fine-tunes the precise location within the quadrant; zero latitude defers to the Lot of Fortune's lord for placement.

rule: When electing an auspicious moment to physically extract a buried or hidden item, choose a time when the Moon is applying to a benefic by body or by harmonious aspect. Avoid times when malefics occupy the angular houses or when the Moon is in signs associated with harmful spirits.
conditions: Moon applying to benefic by conjunction or harmonious aspect
absence of malefics in angular houses
Moon not in designated harmful signs
judgment: A chart meeting these conditions is suitable for the physical act of retrieval; charts failing these conditions should be avoided.
notes: The text does not specify which signs are 'signs of evil spirits.'

rule: If the significator is positioned at the very boundary between two signs—near the end of one and the beginning of the next—this indicates the object was neither deliberately stolen nor intentionally concealed, but rather was accidentally dropped or misplaced.
conditions: significator at or near cusp boundary between two consecutive signs
judgment: Sign-boundary placement of the significator rules out theft or intentional hiding; the item was lost accidentally.

rule: If a benefic planet occupies the 7th house, there is hidden material at or associated with that place. Similarly, if a benefic occupies the 4th house (the angle of the earth), something is buried at or beneath that location.
judgment: Benefic presence in the 7th indicates a hidden item in the associated location; benefic presence in the 4th indicates a buried item.
notes: The logic for the 7th house is not explained in the source; the 4th house connection to buried things is consistent with its traditional earth-and-foundation signification.

rule: To determine the body part affected by illness, identify the sign occupied by the planet that represents the cause of the illness (the planet from which the significator separates) and map that sign to its corresponding body part. The face (decan) occupied by that planet within its sign may further specify the body part.
judgment: The sign (and optionally the face) of the illness-indicating planet identifies the anatomical location of the condition.
notes: The worked example uses Saturn in Leo, first face, to indicate the stomach. Leo's standard body-part correspondence is the heart or sides; the text states 'stomach,' which may reflect a different scheme or the influence of the decan.

rule: A highly authoritative significator (termed the 'significator of the philosophers') is a planet that: holds dignities in the Ascendant degree of the question and in the degree positions of both luminaries; has not committed its disposition to another planet (or if it has, the receiving planet has in turn not committed to any further planet and is strong in its own position); is direct, free of all impediments, angular, and holds at least one dignity in its current position. This planet's authority is further enhanced if it also holds dignity in the Ascendant of the most recent syzygy (new or full moon) preceding the question, in the Ascendant of the current annual solar revolution, in the Ascendant of the lesser Saturn-Jupiter conjunction currently in effect, in the degree of the current Saturn-Jupiter conjunction itself, and in the sign receiving the annual profection. When a full set of these testimonies cannot be assembled, the planet should at minimum hold dignities in the question's Ascendant, in the luminaries' degree positions, in the Ascendant or degree of the most recent syzygy, and in the current Saturn-Jupiter conjunction chart, while being angular, direct, and free of affliction.
conditions: no chain of disposition to a third planet
dignity in syzygy Ascendant preceding question
dignity in current lesser Saturn-Jupiter conjunction Ascendant
dignity in sign receiving annual profection
judgment: A planet meeting all or the majority of these criteria holds maximal authority as significator, and judgment based solely on it is considered highly reliable and authoritative.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (as cited within the passage, described as pseudo-Ptolemy in a footnote)
notes: The source acknowledges that finding a planet satisfying all conditions simultaneously is exceedingly rare. The 'lord of the conjunction or prevention' is defined as the planet holding dignity in both the degree of that syzygy and in the Ascendant of the chart cast for that syzygy's moment; such a planet co-participates in all questions arising under that syzygy's period.

rule: When determining the nature of a hidden thing: if the significator aspects the Ascendant, the object is of the nature of the Ascendant sign; if the significator does not aspect the Ascendant, the object's nature matches the sign the significator occupies. The color of the object is shown by the Lord of the Hour's nature.
conditions: significator aspect or non-aspect to Ascendant
sign of the Ascendant or of the significator
Lord of Hour's planetary nature for color
judgment: Ascendant sign quality (when aspected by significator) or significator's sign quality (when no aspect) describes the object's nature; Lord of Hour indicates its color.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (as cited within the passage, described as pseudo-Ptolemy in a footnote)

rule: The Moon's position relative to the horizon indicates how long the object has been concealed: if the Moon is above the horizon (in houses 7 through 12 or equivalently in the upper hemisphere), the item was recently hidden; if the Moon is below the horizon (in houses 1 through 6), the item has been buried or hidden for a long time.
conditions: Moon's position above or below the horizon
judgment: Moon above horizon = recently concealed; Moon below horizon = concealed long ago.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (as cited within the passage, described as pseudo-Ptolemy in a footnote)

rule: The physical size or dimensions (length and shortness) of a hidden object, or the extent of the material from which it derives, is indicated by the lord of the Lot of Fortune.
conditions: lord of Lot of Fortune and its condition
judgment: The Lord of Fortune's significations describe the scale or physical extent of the hidden item.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (as cited within the passage, described as pseudo-Ptolemy in a footnote)
notes: The text's phrasing about 'length or shortness of the matter whence it was taken up' is ambiguous; it may refer to the material substance of the object rather than its literal dimensions.

rule: The nature of a hidden or buried object is determined from: the lord of the bound of the IC degree, the lord of the Midheaven (specifically whichever of these two is in an angle), and the lord of the bound of the Moon's degree. These three factors together describe the object's fundamental nature.
conditions: which of the two is angular
bound lord of Moon's current degree
Ptolemaic bound system to be used
judgment: Combining the significations of the angular one of IC-bound lord or Midheaven lord with the Moon's bound lord reveals the nature of the concealed item.
attribution_in_text: Ptolemy (as cited within the passage, described as pseudo-Ptolemy in a footnote)
notes: The source explicitly specifies that Ptolemy's own bound system should be used for this method, not another authority's bounds.

rule: To determine the direction of a hidden object by calculation: note how many degrees the Lord of the Hour has traveled through its current sign; multiply that figure by 12; divide the result into 30-degree units counting consecutively through the signs beginning from the Ascendant; the sign where the count terminates determines the directional quadrant (using the same fire/air/earth/water directional assignments). Then subdivide that quadrant by repeating the process using the lord of the terminating sign and allocating 7.5 degrees per sign, starting fresh from the sign that planet occupies. Repeat with the next dispositor, again assigning 7.5 degrees per sign, to progressively narrow the location.
conditions: Lord of Hour's degree-travel within its sign
division into 30-degree sign units from Ascendant
subsequent iterations using dispositor chain with 7.5 degrees per sign
judgment: The iterative calculation progressively narrows the hidden object's location to increasingly small directional zones within the search area, ideally to within arm's reach.
notes: First iteration uses 30 degrees per sign; subsequent iterations use 7.5 degrees per sign. The process is repeated as many times as needed to achieve the desired precision.

rule: Before proceeding with directional analysis in a hidden-object question, check whether the Moon aspects the Ascendant or the significator, and whether the benefics do so as well. If the Moon aspects either, recovery will be swift. If the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant, recovery will be slow or difficult.
judgment: Lunar aspect to the Ascendant or significator indicates quick discovery; absence of such aspect indicates slowness.

rule: Reception between two planets is established when one planet occupies the domicile or exaltation of another, and an applying aspect or bodily conjunction exists between them. Reception may be one-directional or mutual. For mutual reception, each planet must simultaneously occupy a dignity of the other.
conditions: One planet must be in the domicile or exaltation of a second planet; an applying aspect or conjunction must connect them; the aspect must perfect before either planet changes sign.
judgment: When reception accompanies a conjunction or aspect, the planets are disposed to cooperate and the matter signified tends toward completion. Without reception, the planets act at cross-purposes and obstruct the matter.
notes: The text omits detriments from the dignity scheme. There is ambiguity about whether reception exists before the aspect perfects, or only at exact perfection. The text also distinguishes reception by domicile from reception by exaltation, noting exaltation carries greater weight in matters concerning royalty or kings.

rule: When a question concerns a king or matters of rulership and authority, the lord of the exaltation carries more weight as a receiving planet than the lord of the domicile.
conditions: The question pertains to royal or governmental authority; one planet occupies the exaltation of another.
judgment: Reception by exaltation is the stronger testimony in royal or regal questions; reception by domicile is secondary in such contexts.

rule: When two planets receive each other, the quality of the connecting aspect modifies the outcome: trine, sextile, and bodily conjunction indicate ease, harmony, and elevation; square and opposition indicate strain, conflict, and difficulty, even though the matter may still be perfected.
conditions: Mutual reception between two planets; the type of aspect connecting them.
judgment: Trine or sextile reception yields smooth perfection; square or opposition reception yields the matter with labor, error, anxiety, or contention.

rule: When two benefics receive each other, the positive result is amplified. When two malefics receive each other, their harmful qualities are tempered and mutual harm recedes. When a benefic and malefic receive each other, the evil is diminished and the matter tends toward completion, unless the connecting aspect is a square or opposition.
conditions: Nature of the two planets involved (benefic or malefic); whether reception is present; type of aspect.
judgment: Benefic-benefic reception increases benefit; malefic-malefic reception reduces harm; benefic-malefic reception mitigates evil and allows completion, with difficulty if the aspect is square or opposition.
notes: The text attributes the doctrine of malefic-malefic tempering to certain unnamed ancients, referenced via a note connecting to Abū Maʿshar.

rule: When two planets are in opposition (or square) and neither occupies any dignity of the other, the result is enmity, refusal, ignorance, and obstruction of the matter. Each planet in its own exaltation or domicile without receiving the other compounds the conflict rather than ameliorating it.
conditions: Two planets in opposition or square; no reception in either direction.
judgment: The matter fails; the parties represented by the planets are at odds and uncooperative.

rule: A faster-moving planet always applies to a slower one; the slower does not apply to the faster. The aspect or conjunction perfects when the faster planet reaches the exact degree of the slower. At that moment the faster commits its disposition to the slower. After perfection the faster planet separates and its aspect to that planet gradually concludes.
conditions: Two planets at unequal speeds; the faster is not yet at the exact degree of the slower.
judgment: The applying planet signifies what is yet to come; the separating planet signifies what is already past and concluded.
notes: Disposition is committed only when the aspect perfects at exact degree. If the faster planet changes sign before perfection, the conjunction does not complete and disposition is not committed.

rule: If a planet moves into the next sign before the planet applying to it reaches it, the conjunction or aspect does not perfect and the disposition is not committed.
conditions: Two planets in the same sign; the slower planet exits the sign before the faster reaches it in exact degree.
judgment: The aspect fails to complete; any indication of an event from that applying pair is negated.
notes: It remains ambiguous whether partial reception exists in anticipation of an aspect that will not perfect.

rule: When a planet perfects an aspect and commits its disposition to the receiving planet, that receiving planet becomes responsible for the matter. If it in turn aspects and commits to another, the chain continues. The planet at which the chain of disposition ends—the final dispositor—is the lord and author of the matter and governs its outcome.
conditions: A series of applying aspects, each committing disposition to the next planet; no further applying aspect from the last planet.
judgment: The final planet in the disposition chain determines whether the matter succeeds or fails, and its nature and condition dictate the quality of the outcome.
notes: The text uses 'mubtazz' generically here to mean the planet holding final disposition, not necessarily the planet with the highest dignity score.

rule: In any horary question the primary significators of the querent are the lord of the ascendant and the Moon. Determine which is stronger by checking which aspects the ascending sign. The stronger of the two is the primary significator; the other participates as a secondary co-significator.
conditions: Lord of ascendant aspecting the ascending sign; Moon aspecting the ascending sign; relative strength of each.
judgment: The planet that aspects the ascendant is used as the primary operative significator; the other participates.

rule: If the lord of the ascendant does not itself aspect the ascending sign, examine whether it is applying to a planet that does aspect the ascendant, thereby transferring light to the ascendant indirectly. A chain of light transfer through intermediate planets is acceptable. The lord of the ascendant regains functional connection to the ascendant through such a chain.
conditions: Lord of ascendant not aspecting ascendant; an intermediate planet aspects the ascendant and receives the lord of the ascendant's applying aspect.
judgment: The lord of the ascendant is operative through the chain; his strength or weakness is proportional to the quality of the chain.

rule: When the lord of the ascendant does not aspect the ascendant and is void of course, and the Moon likewise does not aspect the ascendant and is void of course, determine which of the two has fewer degrees remaining in its current sign and will therefore exit first. Notionally transfer that planet into the following sign and identify the first planet it would apply to there; use that applying planet as the basis of judgment.
conditions: Both lord of ascendant and Moon void of course; neither aspecting the ascendant; the one with fewer degrees remaining exits its sign first.
judgment: The first applying aspect after the sign change indicates the outcome; void of course in current sign signals slowness, difficulty, and delay in the matter.
notes: Saturn void of course is the worst condition. The lighter planet (Moon in most cases) is more suitable than a heavy one for this notional transfer.

rule: Any planet occupying the ascending sign participates as a co-significator alongside the primary significators, contributing testimony about the matter.
conditions: A planet physically located in the ascending sign at the time of the question.
judgment: The planet in the ascendant adds weight but does not override the lord of the ascendant or Moon as the principal agent of perfection.

rule: A planet occupying the house of the quesited matter provides testimony about that matter's quality. If the planet is concordant with the sign it occupies and is received there, it indicates a favorable and worthy outcome. If it is discordant with the sign and not received, it indicates impediment and a poor result.
conditions: A planet in the house governing the quesited matter; whether it has dignity or concordance in that sign; whether it is received.
judgment: Concordance and reception in the quesited house signal a good matter; discord and absence of reception signal an impeded matter.

rule: The Moon is always a partner to the lord of the ascendant in every question regardless of her placement. When the lord of the ascendant is impeded, the Moon takes over as the primary operative significator and the lord of the ascendant participates with her in a weakened capacity.
conditions: Lord of ascendant impeded (not aspecting ascendant, not connected to it through light transfer); Moon's condition relative to the ascendant.
judgment: Degree of impediment to the lord of the ascendant proportionally affects the matter; the Moon compensates when she is better placed.

rule: In a question about whether a sick person will survive or die, examine whether the lord of the ascendant is applying to a malefic or to the lord of the eighth house. If the lord of the ascendant applies to the lord of the eighth without reception, and the Moon is also afflicted, the person will die.
conditions: Lord of ascendant applying to malefic or to lord of eighth; absence of reception between them; Moon also badly placed.
judgment: Death is signified when the lord of the ascendant applies to the lord of death without reception, and the Moon corroborates.
notes: Either the lord of the ascendant applying to the lord of death, or the lord of death applying to the lord of the ascendant, equally signifies death. The Moon is not the decisive factor in life-and-death questions; the lord of the ascendant governs this matter more than the Moon does.

rule: In a question about survival from illness, if the lord of the ascendant applies to the lord of the eighth and the lord of the eighth receives the lord of the ascendant, the person escapes death. Reception by the lord of death neutralizes the death signification.
conditions: Lord of ascendant applying to lord of eighth; lord of eighth receiving the lord of the ascendant in its domicile or exaltation.
judgment: Reception by the lord of the eighth overrides the death signification; recovery is indicated.
notes: The text specifies reception by domicile and exaltation as 'strong' reception capable of overriding death testimony. Reception of the lord of death by the lord of life constitutes 'weak' reception that partially mitigates but does not fully remove danger.

rule: To time a death indicated by the lord of the ascendant applying to the lord of the eighth without reception, count the degrees of arc separating them and convert each degree to one day. If death does not occur at that interval, it will occur when the bodies are in exact conjunction.
conditions: Death signified by the applying planets; degree separation between lord of ascendant and lord of eighth.
judgment: The degree count gives the approximate timing; exact bodily conjunction confirms the event.

rule: When recovery is indicated, time it by counting the degrees between the lord of the ascendant (or Moon) and the planet signifying recovery, converting each degree to one day. If recovery does not occur at that arc, it will occur when the planets reach bodily conjunction.
conditions: Recovery signified by an applying aspect to a benefic or a receiving planet; degree arc between significators.
judgment: Degree count from aspect to exact bodily conjunction gives the time frame for recovery.

rule: After the primary significators complete their application and commit disposition through a chain, the planet holding final disposition governs the ultimate outcome. If that final planet then applies to another benefic without reception, the matter follows well after the initial resolution. If it applies to a malefic without reception, the matter is taken away or reversed after initially coming to pass.
conditions: Chain of disposition reaching a final planet; that planet's subsequent application to another benefic or malefic.
judgment: Final dispositor applying to a benefic: matter concludes favorably. Final dispositor applying to a malefic without reception: matter is undone or reversed.

rule: The Sun destroys any planet he afflicts by combustion or by projecting his rays upon it through an aspect, unless he receives that planet by domicile or exaltation. Without such strong reception, the Sun destroys the matter governed by the combust planet. The Sun's destructive effect applies whether the planet is benefic or malefic, provided the Sun is not the lord of the house of life and does not receive the planet with a strong reception.
conditions: A planet in combustion or within the Sun's rays; no reception of that planet by the Sun via domicile or exaltation; the Sun not being lord of the ascendant.
judgment: The matter under the combust planet's governance is destroyed or severely harmed.

rule: If a malefic planet occupies the eighth house and has the lord of the ascendant attached to it with no reception between them, death is signified. Similarly, a benefic in the eighth that has dignity there and is attached to the lord of the ascendant without reception also signifies death.
conditions: A planet (malefic or benefic with dignity) in the eighth house; lord of the ascendant applying to it; no reception present.
judgment: Death is signified regardless of the planet's benefic or malefic nature when it holds the eighth house and is unconnected by reception to the lord of life.

rule: A succession of applications and dispositions from the lord of the ascendant or Moon through multiple planets reflects fluctuating health: periods of improvement alternate with new crises according to the benefic or malefic nature and reception status of each planet in the chain.
conditions: Multiple successive applying aspects from the lord of the ascendant or Moon; alternating benefic, malefic, receiving, and non-receiving planets in the chain.
judgment: Each link in the chain corresponds to a phase of the illness; the final link determines whether the patient ultimately recovers or dies.

rule: Whatever planet rules the house of life cannot impede itself even if it is a malefic by nature. Other malefics can still harm it, but its own rulership of the life house immunizes it against self-destruction of the life signification.
conditions: A planet ruling both the ascendant and any other house simultaneously; other malefics aspecting it.
judgment: The lord of life does not destroy the life signification through its own nature; external malefics may still afflict it.
notes: The converse also holds: whatever planet rules the house of death is an enemy of the lord of life regardless of its benefic nature, unless reception is present between them.

rule: The lord of the eighth house is inherently antagonistic to the lord of the ascendant and to life, regardless of whether it is a benefic or malefic by nature. It threatens life unless reception intervenes between them. Reception by the lord of death of the lord of life, or of the planet carrying the lord of life's light, constitutes strong reception and repels the death indication. Reception by the lord of life of the lord of death is weaker and does not fully neutralize the danger.
conditions: Lord of eighth applying to or receiving application from lord of ascendant; presence or absence of reception; direction of reception.
judgment: Strong reception (lord of death receiving lord of life) averts death; weak reception (lord of life receiving lord of death) mitigates but does not eliminate danger.

rule: For a question about acquiring wealth or goods, the primary significators are the lord of the ascendant and the Moon. If the stronger of these applies to the lord of the second house, the querent will obtain the substance regardless of whether reception is present and regardless of the lord of the second's benefic or malefic nature, provided the lord of the second does not immediately commit its own disposition onward.
conditions: Lord of ascendant or Moon applying to lord of second house; lord of second house not further committing its disposition.
judgment: The application alone is sufficient for attainment when it terminates at the lord of the second.
notes: If the lord of the second commits its disposition further, the next planet in the chain governs perfection: a malefic receiving the lord of the second completes the matter; a malefic not receiving it does not; a benefic in a strong place completes it whether or not reception is present.

rule: When the lord of the second house (or a planet in the second house) applies to the lord of the ascendant rather than the reverse, the querent obtains the substance without any effort or seeking on his part; the matter comes to him spontaneously and in greater measure than anticipated.
conditions: Lord of second or planet in second applying to lord of ascendant; not the reverse.
judgment: Passive, effortless acquisition; the matter exceeds expectation.
notes: Contrast with the reverse direction: lord of ascendant applying to lord of second requires active pursuit by the querent.

rule: A malefic that is the final dispositor and has not received the planet committing disposition to it destroys the matter. A benefic as final dispositor completes the matter whether or not reception is present, unless the benefic subsequently commits its own disposition to a malefic that does not receive it.
conditions: Final dispositor is malefic and lacks reception; or final dispositor is benefic.
judgment: Malefic without reception as final dispositor destroys the matter; benefic as final dispositor completes it.

rule: Once reception is established between two planets in the chain of disposition, the matter will eventually be perfected regardless of the time elapsed. Reception guarantees ultimate completion even if significant delay intervenes.
conditions: Reception present between the relevant planets in the chain of disposition.
judgment: The matter will come to pass; timing may be slow but the outcome is certain when reception is in place.

rule: Planets in angular houses hasten and reinforce the matter, making it firm and stable. Planets in succeedent houses support and assist the matter but more slowly. Planets in houses that do not aspect the ascendant (the second, sixth, eighth, and twelfth) delay and postpone the matter most severely. Angular placement makes both good and bad outcomes more lasting.
conditions: Placement of significators and final dispositor in angular, succeedent, or non-aspecting houses.
judgment: Angular: fast and firm. Succeedent: moderate speed and support. Non-aspecting cadent: slow and obstructed.
notes: The text conflates two definitions of cadent: cadent from the angles (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) and cadent from the ascendant (not aspecting it: 2nd, 6th, 8th, 12th). The intended meaning appears to be the latter group for maximum delay.

rule: In a question about recovering lent money or goods from a specific person, the lord of the ascendant and Moon represent the querent, the lord of the seventh represents the debtor, and the eighth house (second from the seventh) represents the debtor's substance. Apply the same perfection rules as for general substance questions but direct them toward the lord of the eighth.
conditions: Lord of ascendant or Moon applying to lord of eighth; presence or absence of reception; planets in the eighth house.
judgment: Application to the lord of the eighth with reception or with a benefic in the eighth indicates recovery of the debt; absence of these testimonies denies recovery.

rule: When a querent asks about obtaining substance from a king's treasury or resources, the relevant house of the king's substance is the eleventh (the second from the tenth).
conditions: Question about acquiring wealth or resources from a royal or governmental source; use the eleventh house as the house of the king's substance.
judgment: Apply the same rules of application, reception, and perfection directed toward the lord of the eleventh.

rule: To time when a matter will come to pass, count the degrees of arc between the significator and the planet to which it applies, and assign one day per degree for faster planets (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun) and one month per degree for slower planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars). If perfection does not occur by aspect first, it will occur when the applying planet reaches the exact degree of the other by bodily conjunction.
conditions: Applying aspect or conjunction between significators; degree separation between them; whether planets are fast or slow.
judgment: The degree count yields the timing in days (fast planets) or months (slow planets).

rule: If the planet that is the final dispositor or author of the matter is under the Sun's rays, the matter will perfect when that planet emerges from combustion and becomes heliacally rising. The planet's emergence renews its capacity to act and renews the matter it governs.
conditions: Final dispositor under the Sun's rays; upcoming heliacal rising of that planet.
judgment: The matter is activated when the author of the matter exits the Sun's beams.

rule: If two planets are moving toward a perfecting aspect, but a third planet reaches exact conjunction or exact aspect with one of them before the original two perfect, the third planet cuts off the original conjunction and the matter indicated by it fails. The intervening planet destroys the intended union.
conditions: Two planets approaching perfection; a third planet applying to one of them at a closer degree, reaching exact aspect first.
judgment: The matter is prevented; hope for its completion is lost at the moment the intervening planet perfects its own aspect.
notes: The text uses a chart example where Mars reaches Saturn before the Sun does, cutting off the Sun's sextile to Saturn and destroying the intended outcome.

rule: When the Moon occupies the sign of the Midheaven and is applying to the lord of the ascendant, the matter aimed for (especially a kingdom or high office) is perfected, regardless of whether reception is present, because the Moon is both in the place of the purpose and a general significator of matters.
conditions: Moon in the tenth house sign; Moon applying to the lord of the ascendant; question about attaining a kingdom or position.
judgment: The matter will be perfected even without reception and even if the lord of the ascendant is a malefic.

rule: In a question about obtaining a kingdom or high office, if the lord of the ascendant or Moon applies to the lord of the Midheaven, the querent will attain the goal. Reception by the lord of the Midheaven adds stability and esteem; without reception, attainment is still possible. If the lord of the Midheaven is instead applying to the lord of the ascendant, the querent obtains the position without effort, as it comes to him spontaneously.
conditions: Application direction between lord of ascendant and lord of Midheaven; presence or absence of reception; aspect type (trine/sextile vs. square/opposition).
judgment: Any application toward the lord of the Midheaven yields attainment; Midheaven lord applying to querent yields effortless attainment; trine/sextile gives ease; square/opposition gives difficulty.

rule: If the lord of the ascendant and Moon have both completed their operative dispositions yet the matter has not come to pass, the astrologer should shift operation to the lord of the sign in which the lord of the ascendant is placed, and continue timing from there.
conditions: Lord of ascendant and Moon cadent or having exhausted their disposition; matter not yet manifest.
judgment: Operation through the lord of the lord of the ascendant's sign extends the timing and provides a further opportunity for the matter to perfect.

rule: If a malefic planet is positioned in the sign of the Midheaven and is in its own exaltation there, it can perfect the matter for the querent whether or not it receives the lord of the ascendant or the Moon.
conditions: Malefic in the Midheaven sign; malefic in its own exaltation in that sign; lord of ascendant or Moon applying to it.
judgment: The matter is perfected without requirement of reception when the malefic is in its own exaltation in the tenth.
notes: Contrast: a malefic in the Midheaven without any dignity must receive the lord of the ascendant to perfect the matter.

rule: When timing a future event, the matter perfects when the significator or author of the matter is in a strong place that it favors, or when another planet arrives at the degree the author of the matter occupied at the time of the question while the author is in such a strong position. If the event does not occur when the aspect perfects, it will occur when bodily conjunction reaches that degree in a strong placement.
conditions: Author of the matter in an angular or dignified position; arrival of another planet to that degree; or arrival of the author to a place of strength.
judgment: Angular placement and dignity of the author of the matter hasten and confirm the timing of the event.

rule: Planets falling away from angular positions slow down any matter that is expected to come to be. Conversely, planets receding from angular strength are optimal significators for things expected to end or depart: travel, a pilgrim setting out, a king losing power, or an official being removed from rank. The degree of cadence corresponds to the degree of slowness or departure.
conditions: Planets in cadent positions relative to the angles; question about departure, travel, or ending of something.
judgment: Cadent planets delay forthcoming events but accelerate the timing of things ending or departing.

rule: The strength of the twelve houses follows a ranking: first in power is the ascending sign; second is the tenth; third is the seventh; fourth is the fourth. Among the intermediate houses, the eleventh is highest, then the ninth, fifth, and third. The lowest-ranked houses—those not aspecting the ascendant—are the eighth, sixth, twelfth, and second.
conditions: Planet or significator placement by house.
judgment: Houses are evaluated for their capacity to hasten, strengthen, and perfect matters in the order stated.
notes: The ninth and third are technically cadent from the angles but are included among the moderate houses because they aspect the ascendant. The text notes some inconsistency in how cadence is defined.

rule: For a daytime birth, the hilaj is selected by testing candidates in this order: Sun, Moon, Lot of Fortune, degree of the prenatal syzygy (new or full Moon), degree of the ascendant. Each candidate must occupy one of eight eligible houses (the four angles plus the four succeedents: eleventh, fifth, eighth, and second), must not be more than five degrees before the cusp of that house, and must be in applying aspect or conjunction with the lord of its domicile or exaltation.
conditions: Daytime nativity; candidate hilaj in one of the eight eligible houses; within five degrees of the house cusp (not earlier); lord of domicile or exaltation applying to or from the candidate.
judgment: The first candidate meeting all criteria becomes the hilaj. The planet receiving it (lord of domicile or exaltation) becomes the kadukhudhah, the giver of years.
notes: For a nighttime birth the same sequence is used. The ascendant is always eligible as a fallback hilaj even if its lord of domicile or exaltation is not applying to it; in that case there may be no kadukhudhah.

rule: When the nativity occurs near or within a new Moon, the degree of the prenatal solar-lunar conjunction is a candidate hilaj. It must fall in one of the eight eligible houses and not be more than five degrees before the cusp. The lord of the bound or lord of the domicile of that degree, whichever is applying, becomes the kadukhudhah.
conditions: Nativity at or near a new Moon; degree of conjunction in an eligible house; within five degrees of cusp; lord of bound or domicile applying to that degree.
judgment: Prenatal conjunction degree serves as hilaj; the applying bound or domicile lord gives years.

rule: When the nativity occurs near a full Moon (opposition of luminaries), the degree of the Moon at that opposition is the candidate hilaj (not the exact degree of the opposition point above the horizon). It must be in one of the eight eligible houses, within five degrees of the house cusp. If the lord of its bound or domicile applies to it, that planet is the kadukhudhah. If no lord applies to it, the degree still functions as the hilaj but the kadukhudhah identification is less certain.
conditions: Nativity near a full Moon; Moon's degree at the opposition in an eligible house; within five degrees of cusp.
judgment: Moon's degree at opposition serves as hilaj; applying bound or domicile lord gives years.
notes: The text specifies using the Moon's own degree rather than the antiscion or the rising degree of the opposition.

rule: The kadukhudhah's allotment of years depends on its house placement and condition. Angular placement with direct motion and free of solar rays yields greater years if it is also in its own sign, exaltation, bound, triplicity, or face; or if the fourth angle, it yields greater years if in such a dignity and oriental. Succeedent placement (eleventh or fifth) without oriental phase or dignity yields middle years. Second or eighth house placement with dignity yields middle years. Placement in the ninth or third yields lesser years, but ninth with oriental phase and dignity in a sect-appropriate nativity yields middle years. Sixth or twelfth house without descension yields lesser years. Sixth or twelfth in descension and retrograde yields months instead of years. Sixth or twelfth in descension, retrograde, and under the rays yields days instead of years. Angular placement while retrograde or under the rays yields middle years. Succeedent placement while retrograde or under the rays yields lesser years. Cadent placement while retrograde or under the rays yields months instead of the lesser years.
conditions: House of the kadukhudhah; its motion (direct, retrograde); solar phase (oriental, under rays); dignity condition (domicile, exaltation, triplicity, bound, face, descension).
judgment: The combination of house, motion, and dignity determines whether the kadukhudhah gives its greater, middle, or lesser years, or a reduced allotment in months or days.
notes: The text references Ptolemy's system of hourly times for degree-based additions and subtractions to the kadukhudhah's years.

rule: Benefic planets aspecting the kadukhudhah from any aspect (including square and opposition) add years proportional to the hourly times of the degree they occupy, at one year per degree of hourly time, provided the benefic is not retrograde, under the Sun's rays, or in the sixth or twelfth house. Malefic planets aspecting the kadukhudhah from any aspect subtract years at the same rate regardless of their house placement.
conditions: Benefic or malefic aspecting the kadukhudhah; the planet's house, motion, and solar phase; calculation of hourly times for the relevant degree in the birth latitude.
judgment: Net years of life = kadukhudhah's base allotment plus benefic additions minus malefic subtractions.
notes: The text references a source reporting that the Dragon's Head or Tail within eight degrees of the kadukhudhah subtracts one-quarter of its years; the author states he has not verified this.

rule: When the North Node or South Node is within eight degrees of the kadukhudhah, each subtracts one-quarter of the years that the kadukhudhah would otherwise grant.
conditions: North or South Node within eight degrees of the kadukhudhah.
