judgment: Each node within this orb reduces the life grant by one quarter.
notes: The author explicitly states this is from an unverified source and he has not tested it. Normally the North Node is considered to add years in other treatments.

rule: Direct the hilaj or the ascending degree through the bounds at one year per degree of ascensional time. When the directed point reaches the rays (aspect) of a malefic, investigate whether a benefic also projects its rays onto that same degree. If a benefic does, the native escapes death but may experience illness or hardship. If the malefic's degrees in that sign outnumber the benefic's, the native survives only until the direction passes through the benefic's degrees and then enters the malefic's, at which point death is indicated.
conditions: Direction of hilaj or ascendant through bounds; arrival at a malefic's aspect or body; presence or absence of a benefic aspect at the same degree.
judgment: Benefic aspect at the malefic degree rescues the native; the native dies when the direction exits the benefic's degrees and enters the malefic's degrees exclusively.
notes: The text distinguishes between aspects as indicators of illness and the exact opposition or square as indicators of death. Trines and sextiles of malefics also testify to illness.

rule: The hurling of rays operates by whole signs: a planet in the tenth sign from another casts an overcoming aspect to that planet, while the lower planet hurls its rays back toward the planet above it. The planet in the superior position (tenth sign from the other) receives aspects from below and projects its influence downward; the lower planet projects its rays upward. This dynamic applies in all four angular whole-sign relationships.
conditions: Two planets in a whole-sign angular relationship (square or opposition by whole signs); the planet in the superior position overcomes the lower.
judgment: The planet in the tenth whole-sign position from another has overcoming influence on it; the lower planet's hurled rays reach the upper but with less force.
notes: The text attributes this as received doctrine from unnamed wise authorities. The exact application of this doctrine to longevity calculations is not made explicit in the text.

rule: Many authorities extend the valid zone for the hilaj to include the five degrees immediately preceding an angular cusp (rising before the cusp). A planet in those five pre-cusp degrees may qualify as the hilaj. However, a kadukhudhah in those same five degrees before an angle cannot grant the greater years but only the middle years.
conditions: Candidate hilaj or kadukhudhah in the five degrees just before an angular cusp; whether the planet is the hilaj or the kadukhudhah.
judgment: Hilaj valid in five pre-cusp degrees; kadukhudhah in those degrees restricted to middle years.
notes: The author frames this as the opinion of the majority of the wise, suggesting he is reporting a consensus view.

rule: When the kadukhudhah is in a strong position, a malefic projecting its rays onto the ascendant, the Sun, the Moon, or the hilaj does not immediately kill the native. The native will survive until the kadukhudhah has exhausted the full number of years it signifies (greater, middle, or lesser), at which point the malefic influence takes effect. However, the benefic aspects of the Sun, Venus, Jupiter, or Moon can break the malefic's power when they aspect the same point.
conditions: Kadukhudhah in a strong position; malefic rays reaching the hilaj or degree of life; benefic aspects present at the same degree.
judgment: Strong kadukhudhah plus benefic aspects protect the native from malefic rays; the native experiences hardship rather than death.

rule: When the lord of the ascendant is positioned in an angular house, particularly the 10th, and is in direct motion, this indicates the querent's strength, elevated status, and capacity to attain the matter under question.
judgment: Querent gains authority, honor, and achieves the requested matter.
notes: The worked example shows the lord also aspecting both its own domiciles and all four angles, which appears to amplify the testimony; it is unclear whether this is considered separately necessary or merely reinforcing.

rule: A planet simultaneously aspecting both of its own domicile signs, particularly while angular, contributes additional strength to whatever it signifies.

conditions.requirement: aspects both of its own domicile signs simultaneously

judgment: Strengthens significations of that planet and its significator role.
notes: This appears as a reinforcing factor alongside angularity; whether it functions independently as a standalone strength indicator is not fully clarified.

rule: When the primary significator of the querent occupies an angular position that is also the exaltation sign of that same significator, the indication of the querent attaining high position or rulership is especially strengthened.

conditions.placement: angular position coinciding with the planet's exaltation sign

judgment: Confirms the querent's attainment of honor and command.
notes: In the worked case, the 10th house serves both as the angle of kingship and as the exaltation sign of the ascendant lord; the combination of angle and exaltation is treated as especially potent.

rule: When planets apply to a third planet from within that planet's own domicile sign, and the receiving planet takes them in from its own domicile, the reception is classified as strong, reinforcing favorable outcomes for all parties involved.

conditions.applying_planets: two or more planets in a sign
conditions.receiving_planet: in its own domicile or exaltation at the time of reception

judgment: Strong reception; significations of both the applying and receiving planets are reinforced toward positive outcomes.
notes: The source also mentions 'the Sun receiving Jupiter by his light,' which may refer to a sect-based or solar-light-based form of reception distinct from domicile reception; this variant is ambiguous.

rule: The planet from which the Moon is separating serves as an additional indicator of the querent's condition and recent circumstances. When that planet is the lord of the ascendant and is well-placed, it reinforces positive testimony for the querent.

conditions.that_planet: ideally lord of ascendant or in a strong position

judgment: Provides corroborating evidence of the querent's strength or weakness depending on the condition of the planet from which the Moon separates.

rule: The planet to which the Moon is applying serves as an indicator of the opposing party's condition. The state of that planet—its motion, dignity, and house placement—describes the opponent's strength or weakness and the likely outcome for them.

conditions.that_planet: any; its condition is assessed for the opponent

judgment: Condition of the planet receiving the Moon's application reflects the opponent's situation and fate.
notes: In the worked case, the Moon applied to Mars, which was retrograde and in its fall, indicating the opponent's undoing; the Moon's application must be distinguished from the Moon's separation used for the querent.

rule: The sign on the 7th house cusp (descending sign, opposite the ascendant) and its lord represent the opposing party in a conflict or rivalry question.
judgment: Condition of the 7th house lord and any planets in the 7th describes the opponent's strength, resources, and likely fate.
notes: The source uses 'nadir of the ascendant' as a synonym for the 7th house sign, not the 4th; translators note this terminology.

rule: When the lord of the 7th house is retrograde and placed in a cadent house, the opposing party loses authority, counsel, and the ability to sustain their position.
judgment: Opponent suffers loss of standing, reversal of plans, and dissolution of their command or enterprise.

rule: When the lord of the 7th is retrograde and cadent, and also applies to another retrograde and cadent planet by opposition, the opponent's ruin is compounded: their alliances break down, their reputation collapses, and gathered resources are lost.
judgment: Severe and compounded debilitation of the opponent; dispersal of networks, destruction of gathered assets, obliteration of reputation.
notes: Absence of reception between the two planets appears to be a necessary condition intensifying the negative outcome.

rule: Placement of the opponent's significator in the 12th house from the ascendant adds a distinct layer of weakness and adversity to the opponent's condition, beyond mere cadency.
judgment: The opponent faces hidden adversity, weakening of position, and inability to sustain their cause.
notes: The 6th house placement of a supporting planet is also treated as cadent from the 7th (i.e., cadent from the nadir), which similarly weakens the opponent's supporting factors.

rule: When a planet significator is simultaneously in its sign of fall, retrograde, and in a cadent house, it indicates fundamental weakness at the outset of whatever enterprise it signifies, including inability to maintain momentum or initial effort.
judgment: Weakness from the beginning of the signified enterprise; inability to sustain effort.
notes: This triple debility—fall, retrograde, cadent—is treated as the most undermining combination for a significator.

rule: When the Moon applies to a planet from that planet's exaltation sign, and mutual reception exists between the Moon and that planet, this combination indicates that the signified party gains victory over their immediate opponents and secures control of contested resources.

conditions.location_of_moon: sign of the receiving planet's exaltation

judgment: The party signified by the receiving planet prevails over opponents and acquires what they held.
notes: This principle can operate even when the receiving planet is otherwise debilitated (e.g., in fall or retrograde), suggesting mutual reception with the Moon partially overcomes those debilities for the specific purpose of victory in conflict.

rule: When the primary significator of the querent and the primary significator of the opponent are in sextile aspect with each other, the matter is resolved through peaceful means rather than open conflict.
judgment: Resolution by negotiation, agreement, or peaceful settlement rather than armed confrontation.
notes: The sextile is explicitly characterized as an aspect of peace and concord, contrasted with the opposition which is characterized as an aspect of contrariety and enmity.

rule: When a lighter (faster-moving) planet is retrograde and thereby moves back into sextile with a heavier (slower) planet, the party signified by the lighter planet is the one who seeks the agreement or submits to the other party.
judgment: The party represented by the lighter planet initiates the approach toward settlement; the heavier planet's party receives the approach from a position of strength.
notes: Retrograde motion of the lighter significator is treated here as directionally meaningful: moving backward into aspect with the heavier planet symbolizes the weaker party seeking terms.

rule: An opposition aspect between two significators indicates a relationship of enmity, contrariety, and active conflict between the parties they represent.
judgment: Contention, opposition of interests, and hostile relationship between the signified parties.
notes: This is used diagnostically to describe the nature of the relationship between Mercury (opponent's significator) and Saturn (querent's allies); no reception between them intensifies the adversarial quality.

rule: When a cadent and retrograde planet's domicile lord is angular but combust, and situated in a bicorporeal (common) sign, the party signified by that dispositor repeats their military or competitive effort more than once but is ultimately consumed and destroyed.

conditions.domicile_lord_of_that_planet: angular, combust, in a common/bicorporeal sign

judgment: Multiple engagements or attempts by the signified party, followed by their ultimate defeat, rout, and destruction.
notes: The common sign placement specifically indicates repetition of the action (two or more battles or attempts); combustion specifically indicates final consumption and flight.

rule: The 8th house from the ascendant represents the allies, soldiers, and material resources of the opposing party (being the 2nd from the 7th).
judgment: Planets in or ruling the 8th describe the state of the opponent's supporters and their financial or material base.
notes: This is a derived house technique—the 8th is interpreted as the opponent's 2nd house.

rule: The 2nd house from the ascendant represents the querent's own allies, soldiers, and material resources in a conflict question.
judgment: Planets occupying or ruling the 2nd reflect the condition of the querent's supporting forces and financial base.
notes: The Moon's position in the 2nd house is used to show the querent's allied forces; it also serves simultaneously as a general significatrix of the opponent through application, illustrating how the Moon can carry dual testimony.

rule: When the Moon, acting as a general significatrix of the opposing side, applies into the house representing the querent's resources and allies, this indicates that soldiers or supporters of the opponent will seek material compensation from the querent and, upon receiving at least partial payment, transfer their allegiance.

conditions.moon: acting as significatrix of the opponent
conditions.application: Moon moving into the querent's 2nd house sign
conditions.reception: Moon received by planet in that sign or ruler

judgment: Enemy forces or allies defect to the querent's side after receiving payment or gifts; defection is conditional on at least partial fulfillment of material demands.
notes: The full demand is not met—the opposition aspect between Moon and Mars indicates the defecting soldiers do not obtain everything they sought; partial satisfaction is sufficient for the transfer of loyalty.

rule: An opposition aspect between the Moon and a martial planet, when both are involved in a negotiation or resource-transfer scenario, indicates that the demanding party will be troublesome and persistent in their demands but will not receive full satisfaction.

conditions.moon: opposing Mars or equivalent martial planet

judgment: Partial rather than complete fulfillment of demands; ongoing pressure and difficulty in the negotiation process.
notes: This principle operates in conjunction with the Moon's house placement and the derived-house analysis of both parties' resources.

rule: When a planet rules both the 2nd and 3rd houses from the ascendant, it signifies the querent's close associates, brothers, and soldiers. If this planet receives an applying opposition from the opponent's significator without mutual reception, those close associates will actively oppose the opponent and withdraw their obedience from him.
judgment: The querent's close allies and soldiers turn against the opponent, rendering him opposition and refusing to follow his commands.
notes: The absence of reception is emphasized as the factor that converts the opposition aspect from mere conflict into a definitive severing of allegiance.

rule: When the primary significators of competing parties are both cadent from angles, the judgment of which party will prevail is made by examining the lords of the domicile signs occupied by those significators rather than the significators themselves.

conditions.technique: shift analysis to domicile lords of those significators

judgment: The party whose significator's domicile lord is in better condition (more angular, better dignified, direct) will gain the victory or the contested matter.
notes: This is a fallback technique invoked specifically when primary significators are too weak (cadent) to judge directly; it mirrors the general principle of using dispositors when a significator is compromised.

rule: When the Sun occupies the 1st house, it indicates high status, authority, and the elevation of the native's affairs.
judgment: Sovereignty, eminence, and the magnification of the native's undertakings.

rule: The Sun placed in the 2nd house points to an attractive material condition, a reputation for high regard, and fortunate eyesight.
judgment: Physical and financial well-being; eyes are favored; esteem is visible to others.

rule: The Sun in the 3rd house facilitates the completion of projects, connections to ruling authority, and movement between localities.
judgment: Matters are accomplished; links to power figures; relocation or journeys occur.

rule: The Sun in the 4th house brings hidden or stolen goods to light, and confers honor and distinction among peers.
judgment: Concealed valuables surface; the native gains praise and standing.

rule: The Sun in the 5th house indicates a declaration concerning offspring, widespread popular reverence, and fortunate outcomes connected to gifts or benefactions.
judgment: A pronouncement about a child; mass veneration; joy and generosity.
notes: Original text uses a Latin term suggesting the astrologer should make a statement about a child — probably indicating the native will have one.

rule: The Sun in the 6th house produces bodily affliction, troubles involving servants or subordinates, sorrow, and reproach from low-status persons.
judgment: Sickness and difficulties with servants; censure from inferiors.

rule: The Sun in the 7th house brings opposition or hostility from wealthy, high-ranking, or powerful persons.
judgment: Conflict or adversity originating from elite or powerful opponents.

rule: The Sun in the 8th house signifies loss of possessions, mortality concerns, and deprivation inflicted by those in authority.
judgment: Loss and death; powerful figures take away what belongs to the native.

rule: The Sun in the 9th house inclines toward religious devotion, fear of the divine, and spiritual cultivation.
judgment: Piety, faith, and engagement with sacred matters.

rule: The Sun in the 10th house brings great authority, renown, honor, and material advantage.
judgment: High office, glory, and favorable outcomes in professional matters.

rule: The Sun in the 11th house produces joyful relations with friends and wealthy associates, alliances with subordinate officials, and competence in trusted endeavors.
judgment: Joy with allies and supporters; skill and reliability in important affairs.

rule: The Sun in the 12th house indicates the destruction of powerful persons, removal of high status, and affliction through servants and enemies, including interference from base individuals.
judgment: Ruin of the mighty; stripping of rank; tribulation from inferiors and opponents.

rule: Venus in the 1st house indicates delight, the ability to act according to one's own wishes, enjoyment of food, clothing, jewelry, and fragrance, moral uprightness, and bodily pleasure.
judgment: Joy, self-gratification, adornment, good character, and physical enjoyment.

rule: Venus in the 2nd house brings material resources and benefit connected to women, nobility of gain, and reliable assistance in financial matters.
judgment: Wealth derived from or connected to women; honest and noble profit.

rule: Venus in the 3rd house may indicate lack of self-discipline, distress arising from wrongful acts or injustices, and accumulation of friends who act contrary to religious or moral standards.
judgment: Intemperance; sorrow from immoral acts; friends of dubious character.
notes: Translator reads the Latin as 'against God,' suggesting friends who oppose divine law.

rule: Venus in the 4th house produces early sorrow and distress in matters involving mothers, but the conclusion of such affairs becomes beneficial and honorable.
judgment: Initial grief regarding maternal figures, but praiseworthy outcomes in the end.

rule: Venus in the 5th house first brings hardship connected to children, followed subsequently by happiness and joy.
judgment: Initial trouble with children; subsequent joy.

rule: Venus in the 6th house signifies sickness and difficulties with male and female servants and with mothers; it also indicates widows or unmarried women. Despite these troubles, the querent ultimately attains the object of the question. In a question about illness, the sick person recovers, and the timing of recovery follows the method described for such calculations. A general principle is embedded here: a benefic planet in the 6th house lightens the illness of the afflicted, while a malefic in the same house worsens it.

conditions.general_principle: benefic in 6th = illness relieved; malefic in 6th = illness aggravated

judgment: Troubles with servants and maternal figures, eventual success; for the sick, recovery; benefic softens illness, malefic intensifies it.
notes: This entry contains an embedded general rule about benefics and malefics in the 6th house that applies beyond Venus specifically.

rule: In any chart where the question concerns illness: the presence of a benefic planet in the 6th house reduces the severity of the sick person's affliction; the presence of a malefic planet there increases it.
judgment: Benefic: illness lightened; malefic: illness worsened.
notes: Extracted from the Venus-in-6th entry as a general rule applicable to all planets.

rule: Venus in the 7th house brings marriage, happiness relating to women, and favorable outcomes in all partnership matters; whatever the querent seeks in this sphere is easily accomplished.
judgment: Successful marriage and partnerships; easy attainment of desired outcomes.

rule: Venus in the 8th house indicates the death of mothers and maternal relatives, particularly the elder members of that family line.
judgment: Death of maternal figures and older maternal relations.
notes: The exact term for maternal relatives is unclear in the source.

rule: Venus in the 9th house points to travel abroad, shifts in religious practice or institutions, engagement with devotional matters, and the occurrence of true or prophetic dreams.
judgment: Foreign travel, religious change, piety, and veridical dreams.

rule: Venus in the 10th house brings joy and favor in connection with the ruler or those in authority.
judgment: Favorable royal or official patronage.

rule: Venus in the 11th house produces friendship, happiness, the enjoyment of good things, and trusting relations with companions.
judgment: Strong friendships, happiness, and fortunate associations.

rule: Venus in the 12th house generates severe hostility from women, and especially from persons of low standing.
judgment: Serious enmity and tribulation from women and base individuals.

rule: Mercury in the 1st house indicates learning, wisdom, skill in written communication, eloquent speech and debate, and proficiency in geometry and arithmetic.
judgment: Intellectual gifts, verbal and written skill, mathematical ability.

rule: Mercury in the 2nd house brings material benefit, honor from ruling authority, and a favorable overall condition.
judgment: Financial gain, royal honor, good standing.

rule: Mercury in the 3rd house indicates many brothers and sisters, and a large circle of friends and prominent acquaintances.
judgment: Numerous siblings and a wide, distinguished social network.

rule: Mercury in the 4th house produces sorrow, prolonged deliberation, quarreling, and contentiousness.
judgment: Grief, mental conflict, and disputes.

rule: Mercury in the 5th house brings the arrival of correspondence or news, joy following prior grief, and good fortune connected to children.
judgment: Messages or news received; joy after sorrow; children fortunate.

rule: Mercury in the 6th house produces quarrels, mental confusion or disorder of the mind, and deception by servants and low-status persons.
judgment: Contention, mental disturbance, and treachery from subordinates.

rule: Mercury in the 7th house brings contention involving women and a surplus of luxury or indulgence.
judgment: Disputes with women; excessive luxury.

rule: Mercury in the 8th house produces intense hostility from neighbors, and the native is subject to contempt arising from false accusations related to the dead — disputes about inherited property or longstanding, unresolved matters.
judgment: Enmity from neighbors; slander involving the dead or their estates; conflict over old disputes.

rule: Mercury in the 9th house confers learning, wisdom, knowledge of the stars, and honorable recognition from knowledgeable peers.
judgment: Scholarly attainment, astrological knowledge, and peer respect.

rule: Mercury in the 10th house brings considerable influence through writing, arithmetic, and geometry, and through proximity to ruling powers.
judgment: Authority and power derived from intellectual skills and official connections.

rule: Mercury in the 11th house multiplies friendships, produces joy, and enables association with learned persons.
judgment: Many friends, happiness, and fellowship with scholars or sages.

rule: Mercury in the 12th house produces dullness of mind, distorted judgment, and restless, pointless activity — the native asks or moves without sound purpose. Any knowledge the native possesses will tend toward quadrupeds.
judgment: Mental weakness, aimless wandering, purposeless questioning; knowledge, if any, concerns animals.

rule: The Moon in the 1st house indicates authority, effective execution of matters, movement between places, and joy connected to mothers and influential women.
judgment: Sovereignty, accomplishment of affairs, travel, and good relations with mothers and noble women.

rule: The Moon in the 2nd house signifies the diminishment or loss of material resources, along with sorrow and grief.
judgment: Financial loss, sorrow.

rule: The Moon in the 3rd house brings fortune from wealthy persons and elevation through rulers, the accomplishment of aims, foreign travel, the acquisition of friends, trust, association with nobles, and an increase of affection.
judgment: Good fortune through powerful patrons; aims fulfilled; travel; expanded friendships.

rule: The Moon in the 4th house in a diurnal chart produces initial grief and sorrow but a praiseworthy ending. In a nocturnal chart, it signifies ruin at both the beginning and the end of the matter. An exception applies to questions about buried treasure or hidden objects: in that specific inquiry, the Moon in the 4th house is optimally favorable regardless of sect, indicating that the thing will be found.

conditions.sect: diurnal = initial grief, praiseworthy end; nocturnal = ruin throughout; exception: treasure questions = best outcome

judgment: By day: difficulty then success; by night: ruin; for buried/hidden objects: discovery guaranteed.
notes: The sect distinction (day/night) is explicitly operative here.

rule: The Moon in the 5th house indicates many children. If the chart is nocturnal, the children will tend to be male; if diurnal, the offspring will tend to be female. It also promises the warding off of frightening events and the arrival of strong news from a distant location. To determine the nature of incoming news: examine the planet from which the Moon is separating — the news will correspond to that planet's nature. To determine whether news arrives in writing or is delivered verbally by a messenger: if the Moon is separating from the lord of the 7th and joining the Ascendant degree, the messenger will convey the news orally. The conjunction or separation of the Moon with Mercury indicates the written or spoken character of the communication.

conditions.sect: night = male children; day = female children
conditions.moon_separation: planet separated from = nature of news
conditions.moon_mercury: Moon joined to or separated from Mercury = written/oral news
conditions.moon_7th_lord_to_asc: Moon separating from 7th lord and joining Ascendant degree = oral delivery by messenger

judgment: Many children; sex indicated by sect; good news from afar; nature of news from Moon's separation; mode of delivery from Moon-Mercury and Moon-Ascendant relationship.
notes: This entry contains multiple embedded horary techniques about the nature and mode of delivery of news.

rule: When a question concerns incoming news or rumors, the nature of the expected news corresponds to the essential character of the planet from which the Moon is currently separating.
judgment: The content or quality of arriving news mirrors the significations of the planet the Moon just left.

rule: To determine whether incoming news arrives as a written document or via a spoken messenger: examine whether the Moon is joining Mercury or separating from him. Additionally, if the Moon separates from the lord of the 7th house and then joins the degree of the Ascendant, the news will be conveyed verbally by a messenger in person.
judgment: Moon joining Mercury suggests written communication; Moon separating from 7th-lord and joining Ascendant = oral delivery by messenger.
notes: The precise distinction between Moon applying to Mercury versus separating from Mercury for written vs. oral is not fully explicit; both cases are referenced but the polarity is ambiguous in the source.

rule: The Moon in the 6th house creates conflict or quarrels involving fathers, brings wealth from animals or livestock, and is associated with bodily health.
judgment: Disputes involving paternal figures; gain from animals; physical health.

rule: The Moon in the 7th house indicates a favorable condition regarding women and marriage, with material benefit arising from them.
judgment: Good circumstances with women and marriage; benefit therefrom.

rule: The Moon in the 8th house signifies destruction and the overthrow or death of a ruler, disruption in activities, false testimony, conflicts, flight, mental anguish of a manic or unstable kind, fear, occult interference, and instability of thought.
judgment: Ruin; royal deposition or death; chaotic affairs; false witness; mental instability and fear.

rule: The Moon in the 9th house in general indicates changes in kingdoms between regions and women holding command, along with understanding of how kingdoms are ordered. The specific type of knowledge signified depends on which planet rules the sign occupied: Mercury's domicile = astrological knowledge; Venus's domicile = knowledge of refined arts and traditional songs; Mars's domicile = mastery of weapons and instruments of war; Jupiter's domicile = religious knowledge, legal expertise, and the role of judges; Saturn's domicile = knowledge of alchemy and related arts; the Sun's domicile = understanding and foresight regarding quadrupeds; Cancer (Moon's own sign) = knowledge of aquatic creatures and substances from water. This specificity by domicile lord is described as a particular property of the Moon among all planets.

conditions.sign_ruler: varies: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Sun, or Cancer

judgment: Type of knowledge varies by domicile ruler of the 9th sign occupied by the Moon.
notes: The text explicitly states this multi-layered sign-ruler refinement is unique to the Moon among planets.

rule: The Moon in the 10th house by day brings effectiveness in matters involving a ruler's command. By night, it indicates success in matters connected to both the ruler and women, and this outcome is swift. In either sect condition, results are not enduring. If a woman were to assume ruling authority with this placement, the king will quickly be deposed — because the 10th house is primarily associated with the Sun's significations, and the Moon's capacity there is only moderate.

conditions.sect: day = command from king; night = king and women, quickly; either sect = not lasting

judgment: Effective but temporary; day = royal matters; night = royal and female matters, swift; Moon's power in 10th is moderate compared to the Sun's.

rule: The Moon in the 11th house brings joy through friends and the fulfillment of hoped-for aims in which the native had placed confidence.
judgment: Joy with friends; hoped-for matters attained.

rule: The Moon in the 12th house signifies hindrance, pressure, instability of authority, quarrels, and danger of imprisonment from enemies. For timing purposes: when the Moon is the primary significatrix and is in the 12th house, the matter will be perfected at the moment the Moon exits that house. If this occurs near the end of the lunar month and the Moon is afflicted by Saturn, the outcome should be judged as severely bad.

conditions.timing: matter perfects at Moon's exit from 12th
conditions.saturn_affliction: especially bad if near end of lunar month and Moon impeded by Saturn

judgment: Impediment and pressure now; resolution when Moon leaves the 12th; if Saturn also afflicts near month's end, outcome is very bad.
notes: The timing rule — that the matter perfects upon the Moon's exit from the 12th — is an embedded horary timing technique.

rule: When the Moon serves as the chart's primary significatrix and is located in the 12th house, the matter under judgment will be resolved at the moment the Moon departs from that house. If additionally this situation occurs at or near the close of the lunar month and the Moon is under Saturn's affliction, the prognosis is extremely negative.
judgment: Resolution upon Moon's exit from 12th; Saturn affliction near month's end = very bad outcome.

rule: Saturn in the 1st house indicates sorrow connected to financial obligation and real property or land.
judgment: Grief arising from debt and land-related matters.

rule: Saturn in the 2nd house brings the diminishment of material resources and the disruption or disarray of friendships.
judgment: Loss of substance; friendships disordered.

rule: Saturn in the 3rd house causes destruction among brothers by provoking quarrels between them.
judgment: Siblings harmed by disputes and conflict.

rule: Saturn in the 4th house brings ruin to buildings, land, crops, and buried wealth; the native faces danger or loss because of these things.
judgment: Destruction of real property, harvests, and treasures; consequent danger.

rule: Saturn in the 5th house destroys or harms children and produces conflict with messengers or envoys.
judgment: Children harmed; disputes with legates.

rule: Saturn in the 6th house brings illness among servants and their insubordination.
judgment: Sickly, disobedient servants or subordinates.

rule: Saturn in the 7th house brings harm to the spouse and to real property, with a malign conclusion to the overall matter.
judgment: Spouse and land damaged; evil end to affairs.

rule: Saturn in the 8th house drives the native to pursue property left by the dead and to contend with old, ancient affairs; grief, sorrow, and prolonged mourning result.
judgment: Pursuit of inherited or old matters; grief and lengthy lamentation.

rule: Saturn in the 9th house corrupts or destroys faith and leads to undertaking wicked schemes, comparable to the acts of the mentally disturbed or those who desecrate graves for plunder. Foreign travel is accompanied by anguish and grief of long duration.
judgment: Loss of faith; malign undertakings; protracted grief on journeys.

rule: Saturn in the 10th house produces grief, adversity, danger from the ruler, and prolonged imprisonment. The eventual fate of the imprisoned or endangered person varies according to which planet rules the 10th house sign: Sun as 10th ruler = the king kills the native in prison; Moon as 10th ruler = same result as the Sun, unless the Moon is in conjunction with Saturn; Jupiter as 10th ruler = the king kills without formal justification and does injury; Mars as 10th ruler = the native perishes by their own fault; Venus as 10th ruler = after tribulation, the native attains elevation, benefit, and joy; Mercury as 10th ruler = killed with dishonor, due to lies told about him; if Mercury also aspects Mars, the native is beaten with whips; if Mercury is with the Sun, the king strips the native of wealth, inflicts injury through financial assessment, and subjects them to examination. This rule is described as uniquely applicable to Saturn in the 10th among all planets.

10th_house_ruler.Moon: same as Sun unless Moon conjunct Saturn
10th_house_ruler.Mercury: killed dishonorably via slander; if Mercury aspects Mars = beaten; if Mercury with Sun = financial persecution

judgment: Danger and imprisonment; specific fate determined by the 10th house's sign ruler.
notes: The text explicitly flags this multi-ruler refinement as particular to Saturn in the 10th.

rule: Saturn in the 11th house brings abundant grief in connection with friends, little benefit from hoped-for matters, complication and difficulty in affairs, and excessive reliance on false promises that yield nothing.
judgment: Grief from friends; hoped-for benefits fail; affairs complicated; trust misplaced.

rule: Saturn in the 12th house produces hindrances arising from royal authority, bold defiance in the face of those obstacles, capture by enemies, and pervasive fear throughout all the native's affairs.
judgment: Royal impediment; capture by enemies; constant fear.

rule: Jupiter in the 1st house confers dignity, physical attractiveness, integrity in faith and religion, learning, rational capacity, and the eventual resolution of all involvement toward a favorable and salvific outcome; authority is entrusted to the native.
judgment: Honor, beauty, faith, learning, and a saving end to all undertakings; authority granted.

rule: Jupiter in the 2nd house brings the accumulation of abundant material resources through competence and sound management, along with the attainment of all things that wealth can provide.
judgment: Wealth gathered through skill; all material needs fulfilled.

rule: Jupiter in the 3rd house produces good fortune in matters involving brothers and close associates, and abundant joy with relatives.
judgment: Fortune with siblings and kin; widespread joy among relatives.

rule: Jupiter in the 4th house brings benefit from the estates of the dead, land inheritances, buried wealth, and ancient resources; it removes grief, troubled thoughts, quarrels, and sorrow, and provides safety from all threatening circumstances.
judgment: Inheritance and buried wealth; relief from grief; security from harm.

rule: Jupiter in the 5th house produces many children in good condition with benefit through them, honest praise, connection with wealthy and noble persons, and favorable results in all trusted endeavors.
judgment: Many well-conditioned children; honor; noble connections; success in trusted matters.

rule: Jupiter in the 6th house reduces illness, favors the health of the body, brings the native honor and advantage regarding servants, and confers benefit from animals.
judgment: Illness minimized; bodily health; good relations with servants; gain from animals.

rule: Jupiter in the 7th house brings joy in marriage and with women, and enables the native to gain the upper hand over all opponents.
judgment: Happy marriage; enemies overcome.

rule: Jupiter in the 8th house causes the native's property to pass into opponents' hands, bringing difficulty; however, the conclusion of this situation is ultimately praiseworthy.
judgment: Wealth temporarily seized by enemies; difficult passage, but honorable resolution.

rule: Jupiter in the 9th house brings joy from travel, integrity of faith, and the capacity to interpret dreams truthfully. For dream interpretation within the chart: the content or meaning of a dream is read from the planet that Jupiter is separating from or that is separating from Jupiter — the dream's meaning corresponds to the nature of that separating planet.

conditions.dream_technique: planet separating from Jupiter or from which Jupiter separates = nature of the dream

judgment: Joy on journeys, faithful conduct, true dreams; dream interpretation derived from the separating planet.
notes: This entry embeds a specific horary/consultational technique for dream interpretation using Jupiter's separations.

rule: When a consultation concerns the interpretation of a dream and Jupiter is in the 9th house, determine the content or significance of the dream by identifying which planet Jupiter has most recently separated from, or which planet has most recently separated from Jupiter. The nature and meaning of the dream corresponds to that planet's essential significations.
judgment: Dream meaning corresponds to the nature of the planet involved in the most recent separation with Jupiter.

rule: Jupiter in the 10th house brings enrichment, the gathering of resources, honest renown, high social standing, and honor in all spheres.
judgment: Wealth, honor, loftiness, and good reputation.

rule: Jupiter in the 11th house brings praise from friends and favorable outcomes in all hoped-for matters in which the native has placed trust.
judgment: Honored by friends; hoped-for matters succeed.

rule: Jupiter in the 12th house produces servitude, poverty, and destitution, along with sorrow connected to animals and grief from servants.
judgment: Poverty and servitude; grief from animals and slaves.

rule: Mars in the 1st house indicates sorrow, fear, conflict, threatening circumstances, cunning, opposition, taking of resources without just credit, and meddling in affairs that do not concern the native.
judgment: Sorrow, fear, conflict, intrusion into others' affairs, loss of substance.

rule: Mars in the 2nd house brings the destruction of material resources, poverty, and the disorganization of the native's subordinates or officials.
judgment: Financial loss, poverty, disrupted subordinates.

rule: Mars in the 3rd house by default signifies enmity among siblings and mutual hatred leading to harm. However, the outcome is modified by the planetary ruler of the occupied sign: Venus's sign = joy from brothers and sisters; Jupiter's sign = substantial gain from commerce; Saturn's sign = digging up graves and walls, searching for stolen goods; Mercury's sign = elevation through divination and writing, but also false testimony and consequent dangers; Moon's sign = breaking down walls, theft, and harmful robbery in commerce; Sun's sign = highway cutting and plundering of settlements. This variation by domicile lord is described as a peculiar property of Mars among all planets.

sign_ruler.Mercury: elevation via divination/writing; false testimony and danger

judgment: Baseline = sibling enmity and harm; modified significantly by domicile ruler of occupied sign.
notes: The text explicitly designates this sign-ruler sensitivity as unique to Mars.

rule: Mars in the 4th house produces destruction, violence or killing, bloodshed, and suspicion related to blood. The conclusion of the matter falls into sorrow and extended tribulation.
judgment: Violence, bloodshed, ruin; prolonged grief at the end.
notes: The phrase 'suspicion of blood' may relate to family suspicion or paternity questions.

rule: Mars in the 5th house brings many daughters born outside marriage, along with defects associated with such circumstances, and a scarcity of joy or benefit from them. Despite this, the native's own livelihood or sustenance is fully adequate.
judgment: Illegitimate daughters, defects, little joy from children; personal livelihood sound.

rule: Mars in the 6th house produces many illnesses characterized by hot and dry fevers and disturbance of the blood, along with grief and troubles involving servants.
judgment: Hot fevers, blood disorders, servant trouble, grief.

rule: Mars in the 7th house produces commercial dealings accompanied by conflict, sexual conduct marked by injustice, harm resulting from these acts, general disorder, and severe ongoing contention.
judgment: Commercial conflict, sexual injustice, harm, disorder, and contention.

rule: Mars in the 8th house brings killing, severe physical mutilation, and the utmost disgraceful censure. The native acquires from the estates of the dead but suffers greatly as a result; others take from the native's own hand, and the native falls into extreme poverty.
judgment: Killing, mutilation, disgrace; gains from inheritance lost to others; poverty follows.

rule: Mars in the 9th house orients the native toward horses, warfare, and armies; it also indicates the drinking of wine, lack of self-control, religious infidelity, many quarrels and divisions, and dreams that are false or deceptive.
judgment: War, arms, intemperance, irreligion, discord, and lying dreams.

rule: Mars in the 10th house brings tribulation involving rulers, physical punishment by whipping, distress, imprisonment, poverty in daily life, and incessant conflict in matters that do not concern the native.
judgment: Royal adversity, beating, imprisonment, poverty, and unwanted conflict.

rule: Mars in the 11th house reduces benefit, turns friends into enemies, causes loss of material resources, and removes confidence in the native's own hopes.
judgment: Little benefit; friends become enemies; loss of wealth and hope.

rule: Mars in the 12th house inclines the native toward thievish conduct in all respects, produces delays in all possible endeavors, causes loss of resources, multiplies enemies, involves the native in perpetrating something terrible, and brings grief connected to large animals.
judgment: Robber's character; delays; wealth lost; many enemies; terrible deed; animal-related grief.

rule: The North Node (Head) in the 1st house signifies increase, elevation, and strength, modified according to which planet or planets it is conjoined with.
judgment: Growth, loftiness, and strength; specific character depends on conjunct planet.

rule: The North Node in the 2nd house increases material resources and brings the greatest good fortune.
judgment: Increase in wealth; very favorable.

rule: The North Node in the 3rd house brings the acquisition of success, soundness of faith, and truthful dreams.
judgment: Success, sound faith, and true dreams.

rule: The North Node in the 4th house increases benefits when located in fire or air signs. When located in earth or water signs, the judgment is reversed — unfavorable outcomes replace favorable ones.

conditions.sign_element: fire or air = increase; earth or water = contrary, negative

judgment: Fire/air: benefit increases; earth/water: reverse — harm instead.
notes: This is a notable rule that elemental sign quality inverts the Node's usual positive indication.

rule: The North Node in the 5th house increases children and protects the native from those who would turn against them.
judgment: More children; freedom from adversaries.

rule: The North Node in the 6th house strengthens any illness present, increases the number of servants, and enlarges the livestock or animals.
judgment: Illness intensified; servants and animals increased.

rule: The North Node in the 7th house increases involvement and association with women.
judgment: Increased association with women.

rule: The North Node in the 8th house strengthens vitality and reduces mortality risk.
judgment: Life strengthened; death reduced.

rule: The North Node in the 9th house indicates faith and the increase of religious devotion, modulated by whichever planets are conjoined with it — beneficial planets strengthen favorable outcomes, malefic planets degrade them.
judgment: Faith and religion increased; specific quality shaped by conjunct planet's nature.

rule: The North Node in the 10th house pertains to inquiry into divine or exalted matters, and signifies elevation, strength, veneration, reverence, and fortunate outcomes in one's profession.
judgment: Exalted inquiry; honor, strength, veneration, and professional fortune.

rule: Neither the North Node nor the South Node has any operative signification when placed in the 11th house.
judgment: No effect in the 11th house for either node.
notes: The text describes this as apparently an unusual doctrine not widely encountered elsewhere.

rule: The North Node in the 12th house increases harmful and evil circumstances, and reduces fortune.
judgment: Evils increased; fortune diminished.

rule: The South Node (Tail) in the 1st house signifies separation, harm, uprooting, dangers, tribulations, and the diminishment of affairs.
judgment: Separation, danger, tribulation, and decrease.

rule: The South Node in the 2nd house brings poverty and preoccupation, along with a fall from positions not expected to be unstable.
judgment: Poverty; unexpected loss and fall from standing.

rule: The South Node in the 3rd house destroys sibling bonds and causes severe quarrels among friends; one sibling or brother/sister may perish.
judgment: Sibling destruction; severe friend quarrels; possible death of a sibling.

rule: The South Node in the 4th house brings want or need, prompts investigation or searching into matters, but also yields some benefit.
judgment: Need and searching; some benefit attained.

rule: The South Node in the 5th house expels good fortune, brings terrible things upon the children, and creates a state of need for them.
judgment: Fortune removed; children afflicted; need and poverty for offspring.

rule: The South Node in the 6th house produces illness and laziness in male and female servants, and weakness in animals.
judgment: Sickly, lazy servants; weak animals.

rule: The South Node in the 7th house strengthens enemies and brings about scorn; damage to the partnership domain is implied.
judgment: Enemies strengthened; scorn and contempt for the native.
notes: The source text at this point is partially unclear about what exactly is destroyed; a parallel text mentions difficulties between men and women generally.

rule: The South Node in the 8th house signifies death, inherited or posthumous property matters, the presence of ruin, and destruction.
judgment: Death, ruin, and matters relating to the dead.

rule: The South Node in the 9th house reinforces change, movement, and travel, while reducing faith and religious inclination.
judgment: Strengthened change and movement; faith diminished.

rule: The South Node in the 10th house brings deposing from authority, danger, foreign travel (possibly as exile), or a fall.
judgment: Removal from power, danger, exile or travel, and a fall.

rule: The South Node in the 12th house diminishes evil and harmful outcomes, contrary to its usual negative tendency.
judgment: Evils are reduced in this placement.
notes: This is a notable exception: the South Node in the 12th is relatively favorable, inverting its general malefic tendency — parallel to the North Node in the 12th increasing evil.

rule: The significations assigned to each planet in each house are stated for a neutral or moderate condition. When the planet is in a stronger or better condition (greater dignity or favorable state), the judgment should be improved and stated more positively. When the planet is in a weaker or worse condition, the statement should be reversed — what was positive becomes negative, and the astrologer should declare the contrary with confidence.
judgment: Better condition = improve the stated signification; worse condition = reverse it to its opposite.
notes: This is stated as a general operating meta-rule for the entire chapter's planet-in-house system.

rule: Any given arc measurement (e.g., 60°, 90°, 120°) carries the same archetypal meaning whether it appears as an aspect between two planets, as a sign counted from the zodiac's starting point, or as a house counted from the ascending point; the sign's ruling planet also shares this same underlying principle.
conditions: arc distance between two chart points
judgment: The aspect, the corresponding sign, the corresponding house, and the sign's ruler all express one common developmental theme.

rule: Aspects are not inherently fortunate or unfortunate; tense aspects (square, opposition) mark critical turning points that force conscious growth and problem-solving, while easy aspects (sextile, trine) provide confidence and facility but can produce complacency unless deliberately engaged.
judgment: Hard aspects build character through challenge; soft aspects require conscious effort to avoid passivity or avoidance of growth.

rule: Aspects occurring between the conjunction and the opposition (the waxing hemicycle) govern subjective self-formation, instinctive self-assertion, and the building of personal identity, generally without regard for consequences to others.
conditions: aspect phase falls between conjunction and opposition points
judgment: Indicates formative, self-oriented, largely unconscious expression focused on establishing individual identity.
notes: Author associates this framework with 'leading humanistic astrologers.'

rule: Aspects occurring between the opposition and the next conjunction (the waning hemicycle) govern conscious evaluation of self versus others, social integration, and depersonalized objectivity, and tend to manifest more through external circumstance than internal impulse.
conditions: aspect phase falls between opposition and next conjunction point
judgment: Indicates reflective, socially-oriented, more fated-feeling development requiring integration with others.

rule: In any two-planet aspect, the naturally slower-moving planet (by orbital period, not apparent speed at birth, so retrograde status is irrelevant) sets the governing theme or 'home base' of the aspect, while the faster-moving planet must adapt or develop itself in relation to that theme.
conditions: relative natural orbital speed of the two planets in aspect
judgment: The slower planet conditions and directs the developmental task; the faster planet must assimilate experience according to the slower planet's principle.
notes: Author states this is a personal interpretive stance ('in my opinion').

rule: An aspect is 'lower' (waxing) when the faster planet, moving in zodiacal sequence, is still approaching the slower planet's opposition point (faster planet positioned dexter/clockwise-preceding the slower planet); it is 'upper' (waning) when the faster planet has passed that opposition point and is heading toward reconjunction (faster planet positioned sinister/following the slower planet).
conditions: relative zodiacal position of faster planet to slower planet's opposition point
judgment: Classifies any non-conjunction, non-opposition aspect as either a lower/waxing or upper/waning variant, each carrying a distinct interpretive nuance.

rule: The conjunction (0° separation) corresponds symbolically to the 0° point of Aries, the Ascendant/1st house, and the planet Mars.
judgment: Conjunctions carry Aries/1st-house/Mars-like qualities of self-assertion and self-containment.

rule: A separating conjunction (faster planet just past exact) behaves more like a waxing/outward-projecting aspect; an applying conjunction (faster planet approaching exact) behaves more like a waning/inward-consolidating aspect, since the faster planet is still technically within the waning hemicycle.
judgment: Separating conjunctions incline toward outward projection of energy; applying conjunctions incline toward inward consolidation before expression.

rule: The conjunction fuses the two planets' energies into a single, highly self-contained mode of expression that resists external influence, lacks reflective perspective, and often functions as a blind spot the native cannot easily see in themselves though others observe it readily.
conditions: conjunction aspect between any two planets
judgment: Produces intense, undifferentiated, subjectively-driven behavioral traits with strong personal impact but reduced self-awareness of how they appear to others.

rule: A chart with many conjunctions (especially in fire signs or fixed signs, or forming stelliums) indicates strong self-reliance, initiative, and a tendency toward self-absorption or reluctance to cooperate; a chart with few or no conjunctions indicates reduced self-driven initiative, greater reliance on others, but potentially more objectivity, and this deficiency may be offset by strong Aries placements, a prominent Mars, or 1st-house emphasis.
conditions: number of conjunctions in the natal chart
compensating factors: Aries emphasis, angular/strong Mars, 1st-house emphasis
judgment: Predicts degree of self-initiated action versus dependence on others' support and initiative.

rule: The 30° semi-sextile corresponds to Taurus/2nd house/Venus when in its lower (waxing) phase, and to Pisces/12th house/Neptune when in its upper (waning) phase.
conditions: semi-sextile aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Assigns differing significations depending on phase.

rule: Combining earth and water qualities, the semi-sextile is a receptive, internalizing aspect that attracts latent resources or values but rarely generates enough energy on its own to activate them without deliberate personal effort.
judgment: Indicates untapped potential requiring conscious cultivation rather than automatic expression.

rule: Minor aspects (semi-sextile, semi-square, sesqui-square, quincunx, etc.) express subtler nuances of personality, operating more through internal attitude than through overt, noticeable life events, compared to major aspects.
judgment: Minor aspects manifest as background dispositional tendencies rather than dramatic circumstances.

rule: The lower (waxing) semi-sextile stimulates instinctual awareness of material/physical values and attraction, providing small-scale resources and opportunities that remain largely passive and undeveloped until acted upon.
judgment: Indicates latent material or sensory resources requiring patient cultivation to become tangible assets.

rule: The upper (waning) semi-sextile activates subtle, unconscious spiritual or psychic resources carried over from prior experience, requiring release of self-will and altruistic orientation before they can be constructively expressed.
judgment: Indicates latent spiritual/psychic assets that become available through selfless, compassionate application.

rule: The 45° semi-square corresponds to the 15th degree of Taurus (lower phase) and the 15th degree of Aquarius (upper phase), both fixed signs, associating the aspect with stubborn, self-willed but persistent minor friction.
conditions: semi-square aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Produces minor, nagging irritation and stubborn resistance to needed small changes, but also stamina for small-scale efforts.

rule: The lower semi-square generates rudimentary, largely unconscious irritability and petty criticism over minor imperfections, requiring practical small adjustments and emotional moderation to resolve.
judgment: Indicates fussiness, impatience with minor flaws, and a need to accept small necessary changes gracefully.

rule: The upper semi-square generates mental-level friction from attempting to impose one's social ideals on others, producing exasperation when reform efforts meet resistance, and can manifest as eccentric or erratic behavior if misused.
judgment: Indicates frustration over unwelcome social idealism and risk of alienating others through erratic or overbearing behavior.

rule: The 60° sextile corresponds to the cusp of Gemini (lower phase, tied to 3rd house/Mercury) and the cusp of Aquarius (upper phase, tied to 11th house/Uranus), associating this aspect with the air element and mental/perceptual stimulation.
conditions: sextile aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Sextiles function as intellectually stimulating, opportunity-oriented aspects requiring personal engagement to actualize.

rule: Unlike the trine, the sextile is not weaker but rather more stimulative and situational, requiring active personal engagement with available opportunities to yield benefit, whereas the trine operates more as a passive internal state.
conditions: comparison of sextile and trine aspects
judgment: Sextile benefits depend on active participation; trine benefits are received passively.

rule: The lower sextile stimulates curiosity, factual learning, and versatile mental engagement with immediate surroundings; an abundance of lower sextiles indicates alertness and adaptability but risk of scattered, superficial interests, while a deficiency indicates reduced motivation toward communication and learning (which may be offset by Gemini emphasis, 3rd-house emphasis, or a prominent Mercury).
conditions: compensating factors: Gemini emphasis, 3rd house emphasis, prominent Mercury
judgment: Predicts degree of intellectual curiosity, communicativeness, and adaptability to everyday circumstances.

rule: The upper sextile extends mental opportunity toward social reform and innovative, detached expression; an abundance indicates unconventional mental brilliance and social idealism (with unpredictable nervous energy), while a deficiency indicates reduced drive to explore the unconventional or participate in broader social causes (which may be offset by Aquarius emphasis, 11th-house emphasis, or a prominent Uranus).
conditions: compensating factors: Aquarius emphasis, 11th house emphasis, prominent Uranus
judgment: Predicts capacity for innovative thought and engagement with social/collective ideals.

rule: The 90° square corresponds to the cusp of Cancer (lower phase, tied to 4th house/Moon) and the cusp of Capricorn (upper phase, tied to 10th house/Saturn); both belong to the cardinal quality and the earth-water elemental combination, making the square an internally-rooted but action-forcing aspect.
conditions: square aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Squares generate internal tension resolved through direct, forceful action; they mark major crisis/turning points.

rule: A natal square between two planets may manifest either as suppression/inhibition of the planetary energies or as excessive, forceful over-expression; which mode dominates cannot be determined from the chart alone and often shifts over the native's lifetime, typically beginning with inhibition and later shifting toward overdrive after crises, though the reverse pattern is also possible.
conditions: square aspect present in natal chart
judgment: Requires direct inquiry into lived behavior to determine whether the square manifests as inhibited or overdriven expression.

rule: The lower square reflects subconscious insecurity rooted in early family conditioning, producing defensive habits that must eventually be released for psychological growth; an abundance indicates entrenched defense mechanisms and difficulty processing past experience, while a deficiency indicates less impact from early conditioning but also less depth of empathy for others' subjective pain (with the Moon, Cancer, or 4th-house placements amplifying significance).
conditions: emphasis on Moon, Cancer, or 4th house
judgment: Predicts degree of subconscious insecurity, defensiveness, and capacity for emotional depth.

rule: The upper square reflects conscious tension between personal drives and social/authority expectations, producing self-discipline and ambition when well-used or ruthless self-preservation when misused; an abundance indicates over-cautious, controlling, or domineering tendencies, while a deficiency indicates less felt restriction by authority but also less drive toward disciplined achievement.
judgment: Predicts degree of ambition, self-discipline, and relationship to authority/social structure.

rule: The 120° trine corresponds to the cusp of Leo (lower phase, tied to 5th house/Sun) and the cusp of Sagittarius (upper phase, tied to 9th house/Jupiter), both fire signs, making the trine an easy, harmonious, but passively-received aspect.
conditions: trine aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Trines produce ease, confidence, and creative flow but lack the impetus for dynamic action or change.

rule: Trines are equal in inherent strength to squares, but because their energy is directed inward rather than outward, they appear less influential in external events and instead manifest as subjective states of well-being, insight, and magnetic receptivity.
conditions: trine aspect present natally or by transit
judgment: Trines are best understood as descriptors of inner attunement rather than as producers of external events.

rule: The lower trine grants natural, effortless creative self-expression, charisma, and magnetic appeal; an abundance can create a self-indulgent, entitled disposition avoiding hard work, while a deficiency reduces creative confidence and willingness to display talent (with Sun, Leo, or 5th-house placements amplifying significance).
conditions: emphasis on Sun, Leo, or 5th house
judgment: Predicts ease and confidence of creative self-expression versus risk of complacency or self-indulgence.

rule: The upper trine grants generosity, idealism, and philosophical or spiritual uplift oriented toward collective benefit; an abundance can produce unrealistic optimism, procrastination, or escapism, while a deficiency reduces faith, hope, and broad-minded perspective (with Jupiter or 9th-house placements amplifying significance).
judgment: Predicts capacity for idealism, generosity, and philosophical breadth versus risk of impracticality or diminished faith.

rule: When a third planet squares one member of a trine, that square supplies the dynamic tension needed to activate the trine's latent potential, and conversely the trine can serve as a resource for resolving the stress of the connected square; the shared planet becomes a key transformative point in the chart.
conditions: a third planet in square aspect to one of the trine planets
judgment: Identifies the connecting planet as a pivotal point where stress (square) and ease (trine) can be mutually integrated for growth.

rule: The 135° sesqui-square corresponds to the 15th degree of Leo (lower phase, tied to 5th house/Sun) and the 15th degree of Scorpio (upper phase, tied to 8th house/Pluto), combining fixed quality with fire and water elements, producing volatile, emotionally-charged friction.
conditions: sesqui-square aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Indicates sudden emotional upsets and a tendency toward extreme or disproportionate reactions requiring self-restraint.

rule: The lower sesqui-square produces an exaggerated, attention-seeking display of ego and authority that alienates others and habitually falls short of anticipated results, requiring recognition of the limits of self-will.
judgment: Indicates overbearing self-assertion in relationships leading to interpersonal friction.

rule: The upper sesqui-square produces covert attempts to psychologically remake or control others, provoking mutual resentment and periodic relationship breakdowns unless one learns to accept others as they are.
judgment: Indicates hidden power struggles and manipulation risk in close relationships.

rule: The 150° quincunx corresponds to the cusp of Virgo (lower phase, tied to 6th house/Mercury) and the cusp of Scorpio (upper phase, tied to 8th house/Pluto); it connects signs of incompatible element and quality, marking it as a correctional, adjustment-demanding aspect.
conditions: quincunx aspect; lower vs upper phase
judgment: Requires ongoing reorganization and discrimination to resolve inefficient or self-depleting patterns.

rule: Quincunx tension typically remains below conscious awareness for an extended period before circumstances suddenly force a cluster of related problems into focus requiring decisive resolution; this pattern is especially pronounced in a double-quincunx (Yod) configuration.
conditions: quincunx aspect(s) in the natal chart
special emphasis when forming a Yod
judgment: Predicts a delayed but eventually forceful confrontation with previously unaddressed adjustment issues.

rule: The lower quincunx (the 'health quincunx') indicates disorganization of physical/routine energy patterns, often manifesting as somatic malfunction, especially when the planets involved relate to the 1st or 6th houses or their rulers, and requires methodical adjustment of daily habits and technique.
judgment: Predicts recurring physical or routine dysfunction until corrective habits of discrimination and skill are adopted.

rule: The upper quincunx (the 'death quincunx') indicates deep psychological adjustment requiring self-mastery of intense desire and emotion, typically triggered by crisis, separation, or loss, and can lead to regenerative transformation once embedded, outworn attitudes are released.
judgment: Predicts periodic psychological crises that, if worked through, produce deep inner renewal and capacity for relational transformation.

rule: The 180° opposition corresponds to Libra, the 7th house, and the planet Venus; like the conjunction it does not belong strictly to either hemicycle but marks the transition point between them.
judgment: Opposition carries Libra/7th-house/Venus themes of relationship, balance, and mutual awareness.

rule: An applying opposition tends to behave like a waxing aspect, producing difficulty sharing energies in relationship due to self-interest, while a separating opposition tends to behave like a waning aspect, producing greater awareness and give-and-take in relating.
judgment: Predicts relative ease or difficulty of achieving reciprocal balance in relationships governed by the opposition.

rule: When one planet of an opposition is over-identified with and the other neglected, the neglected planet's function tends to be projected onto and acted out by another person, producing external relational conflict rather than internal struggle (which is more characteristic of the square); balanced integration requires alternately expressing and witnessing both planetary functions.
conditions: opposition aspect with unequal identification between the two planets
possible exception if the slower planet is conjunct the Ascendant, in the 1st house, or rules the 1st house
judgment: Predicts that unintegrated opposition energy will manifest through conflict with other people rather than purely internal tension.

rule: Many oppositions in a chart indicate a life of alternating extremes and difficulty with decisive independent action, with strong dependence on relationships for self-understanding; few or no oppositions indicate reduced natural inclination to evaluate situations objectively or compromise with others, and reduced tendency toward face-to-face conflict resolution (which may be offset by a Libra stellium, strong 7th house, or prominent Venus).
conditions: number of opposition aspects in the natal chart
compensating factors: Libra emphasis, 7th house emphasis, prominent Venus
judgment: Predicts degree of reliance on relationship dynamics for self-awareness and capacity for objective compromise.

rule: For any aspect that is scarce or absent in a chart, its qualities may still be expressed if there is compensating emphasis through the corresponding sign (stellium or strong placement), the corresponding house, or the corresponding ruling planet.
conditions: low or zero count of a specific aspect type
presence of corresponding sign, house, or planet emphasis elsewhere in the chart
judgment: The absence of an aspect does not by itself rule out expression of its associated qualities if compensating chart factors are present.

rule: A lack of a given aspect in the natal chart describes only the individual's early, unconsidered pattern of behavior; through conscious effort over the course of life, the individual can deliberately cultivate and even strongly express the qualities that aspect would normally signify, gaining greater self-directed control over that expression than one who possesses the aspect naturally.
conditions: absence or scarcity of a given aspect (or of an associated element/quality) in the natal chart
judgment: Predicts that the missing quality can be consciously built up over time rather than being permanently absent from the personality.

rule: Any integer division of the 360-degree circle can generate a valid aspect with distinct symbolic meaning, not just the traditionally recognized divisors.
conditions: Division of circle by any whole number
judgment: Each resulting angular division constitutes a legitimate aspect with its own signification
notes: Presented as an extension of Pythagorean number symbolism applied to astrology

rule: An aspect and all of its harmonic multiples (e.g., the quintile, semi-quintile, sesqui-quintile, bi-quintile) belong to one interpretive family and share a common underlying theme derived from the base divisor number.
conditions: A base aspect angle (360/n) and its multiples
judgment: All members of the family should be read as variations on the core meaning of the base division number

rule: The traditionally used aspects correspond to circle divisions by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12 (conjunction, opposition, trine, square, sextile, semi-square/sesquisquare, semi-sextile/quincunx respectively).
judgment: These map to the conjunction, opposition, trine, square, sextile, octile family, and semi-sextile family

rule: Less commonly used aspects arise from circle divisions by 5, 7, 9, 10, and 11, yielding the quintile (72°), septile (~51.5°), novile (40°), semi-quintile/decile (36°), and undecile (~33°).
judgment: These angles represent additional valid but rarely analyzed aspects

rule: The quintile aspect (along with the semi-square, sesquisquare, and septile) was introduced into astrological practice in the 17th century, later than the Ptolemaic aspect set.
judgment: Quintile treated as a later addition to standard aspect doctrine

rule: Prominence of the quintile family in a chart indicates use or misuse of power and authority, along with an intensely focused, specialized drive in some field of activity.
conditions: Quintile or its harmonic multiples emphasized in the 5th harmonic chart or natal aspects
judgment: Native shows one-pointed, driven engagement with power/authority themes, expressed constructively (creative genius, scientific or artistic achievement) or destructively (criminality, victimization, tyranny, revolutionary violence) depending on level of development
notes: Positive vs negative expression tied to level of self-realization per author's commentary

rule: The quintile is associated in esoteric tradition with alignment of the individual's creative will with a larger cosmic will/purpose, an association more fully activated in spiritually developed individuals.
judgment: In an unawakened individual the aspect may remain dormant or express compulsively; in a self-realized individual it fulfills a higher creative/transcendent function

rule: The number five (and by extension the quintile) is numerologically linked to a composite of Jupiter/Uranus themes (with Mars undertones): freedom, exploration, restlessness, experimentation, variety, sensory indulgence, and sexual magnetism.
conditions: Number five symbolism applied to quintile aspect
judgment: Quintile aspects express these behavioral/psychological themes

rule: The 5th harmonic (quintile family) has relevance to assessing sexual tendencies and deviations.
conditions: Prominent quintile series in 5th harmonic chart
judgment: Indicates sexual proclivities/aberrations

rule: The quintile signifies the capacity to shape mental or artistic material into a form that faithfully expresses its underlying archetypal idea, representing a rare, innate creative or intellectual gift rather than a skill built through external conditioning.
judgment: Indicates uncommon creative genius, insight, and mental artistry that may require refinement before productive expression, and may operate mainly on internal/altered states of consciousness rather than everyday affairs

rule: The quintile family relates to the faculties of knowing and to the means by which knowledge and information are received and communicated.
conditions: Quintile series emphasized in 5th harmonic chart
judgment: Indicates gnostic/mental faculties; if afflicted, may indicate impairment such as nervous disorders, sensory defects, or speech/communication problems

rule: A strong quintile-based connection between Saturn and Uranus in the 5th harmonic chart signifies innate astrological aptitude.
conditions: Exact or strong quintile aspect between Saturn and Uranus in 5th harmonic chart
judgment: Indicates a natively gifted astrologer

rule: The lower quintile phase corresponds to roughly the 12th degree of Gemini (counterclockwise) linking to the Libra dwad/Libra decanate of Gemini, the 3rd house, and Venus; the upper quintile phase corresponds to roughly the 18th degree of Capricorn (clockwise) linking to the Leo dwad/Taurus decanate of Capricorn, the 10th house, and Saturn.
judgment: Provides sign/house/planet correspondences for interpreting the quintile in a symbolic wheel-based system
notes: Degree correspondences described as irregular unlike symmetric correspondences of standard aspects

rule: The number seven (and thus the septile) numerologically corresponds to a composite of Saturn/Neptune themes (with Pluto undertones): self-knowledge, introspection, search for wisdom, solitude, contemplation, and withdrawal from worldly concerns.
conditions: Number seven symbolism applied to septile aspect
judgment: Septile aspects express these introspective, solitary, and occult-oriented themes

rule: The septile family signifies the capacity to perceive an underlying unifying idea or principle behind the parts of a subject, and to receive inspiration through participation in that idea's formative energy.
conditions: Septile series prominent in 7th harmonic chart
judgment: Indicates ability to grasp mysterious wholeness and to be creatively inspired; prominent among clergy/those exercising a priestly social function and among creative artists (visual artists, musicians, writers, poets)

rule: The septile family relates to the psychology of sex, particularly its more repressive, self-denying, or sublimating aspects (in contrast to the more expressive/experimental sexuality of the quintile family), often correlating with redirection of libidinal drive into artistic inspiration.
judgment: May manifest as celibate inclination, sexual repression, or sublimation feeding creative output

rule: The septile signifies actions or compulsions that fall outside the accepted social-cultural norms of the native's environment, often experienced as fated, compelled by a collective or karmic force, and associated with self-sacrifice or symbolic living.
judgment: Indicates a fatalistic, compulsive, or destiny-driven quality of experience, with occult, psychic, or mystical predisposition
attribution_in_text: Dane Rudhyar; Doris Thompson; Delphine Jay; Michael Meyer
notes: Author cautions against delivering deterministic 'inevitable fate' pronouncements to clients based on this aspect

rule: The lower septile phase corresponds to roughly 21.5 degrees of Taurus (counterclockwise), linking to the Capricorn dwad/Capricorn decanate of Taurus, the 2nd house, and Venus; the upper septile phase corresponds to roughly 8.5 degrees of Aquarius (clockwise), linking to the Taurus dwad/Aquarius decanate of Aquarius, the 11th house, and Uranus.
judgment: Provides sign/house/planet correspondences involving fixed signs and Venus-Saturn-Uranus undertones for interpreting the septile
notes: Degree correspondences described as highly irregular

rule: The number nine (and thus the novile) numerologically corresponds to Neptunian themes of selflessness, universal compassion, spiritual completion, and personal sacrifice for collective upliftment.
conditions: Number nine symbolism applied to novile aspect
judgment: Novile aspects express these emotionally oriented, self-transcending themes and mark the close of a life cycle preparing for a new one
